Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.

As a Technical Program Manager within our Platform Gen organization, you’ll drive complex, cross-functional engineering initiatives spanning runtime systems, device drivers, deployment, observability, and hardware enablement. This is a technical role for someone who can go beyond tracking timelines and coordinating meetings. You’ll work closely with software, hardware, systems, and architecture teams to understand technical challenges, identify dependencies, drive solutions, and turn ambiguous engineering problems into clear execution plans.

Our team’s work directly impacts the reliability and performance of Tenstorrent’s AI platforms, from individual accelerators to large-scale AI compute clusters. You’ll help improve system reliability, streamline deployment and debugging, accelerate software and hardware readiness, and ensure our platforms meet the needs of internal teams and external customers.

This role is   hybrid, based out of Santa Clara, CA; Austin, TX; or Toronto, Canada.

We welcome candidates at various experience levels for this role. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting.

Who You Are

- Technically grounded, with experience in software engineering, systems engineering, or technical program management in a complex engineering environment.

- Able to understand software architecture, system dependencies, and hardware/software interactions, and translate technical challenges into actionable plans.

- Comfortable driving ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives involving multiple engineering teams, competing priorities, and evolving requirements.

- Data-driven and proactive about identifying risks, investigating issues, and driving problems to resolution.

- Hands-on and resourceful, with strong communication skills and an interest in using code, automation, dashboards, and AI-powered tools to improve engineering workflows.

What We Need

- Drive end-to-end execution of complex platform engineering initiatives, from problem definition and technical planning through implementation, validation, and delivery.

- Coordinate across runtime, device drivers, deployment, observability, debug tools, hardware, and architecture teams to manage dependencies and unblock engineering progress.

- Lead reliability and scalability initiatives for AI systems, including fleet-scale deployment, cluster recovery, hardware/software integration, and resolution of recurring system issues.

- Establish execution plans, milestones, success metrics, and reporting mechanisms that help engineering teams identify risks and make informed decisions.

- Improve engineering execution through technical problem-solving, telemetry, dashboards, automation, and AI-assisted workflows while supporting platform readiness for new hardware and customer requirements.

What You Will Learn

- How runtime systems, device drivers, and platform software work together to enable reliable, high-performance AI accelerators and end-to-end AI systems at scale, from individual devices to distributed compute clusters.

- How software, firmware, hardware, and observability systems come together to deliver production-ready AI platforms.

- How to lead technically complex initiatives across multidisciplinary engineering teams.

- How to use data, automation, and AI-powered tools to improve engineering execution and operational efficiency.

**Position Summary**

  

The NPI Program Manager is responsible for the **end-to-end delivery of new product introduction programs** , from concept through development, industrialization, and production ramp. This role ensures that products are launched on time, within cost, and at target quality, by orchestrating cross-functional teams across engineering, operations, supply chain, and quality.

The NPI PM acts as the **single point of accountability** for program execution and serves as the **bridge between product development and manufacturing** .

  
  

**Key Responsibilities :**

  

**1. Program Leadership & Execution**

* Lead NPI programs from **concept to volume production**
* Define program scope, objectives, milestones, and deliverables
* Build and maintain **integrated program plans (WBS, schedules, roadmap)**
* Drive execution to meet **cost, schedule, quality, and performance targets**
* Ensure transition from development to manufacturing readiness

**2. Cross-Functional Coordination**

* Lead and align global cross-functional teams:
  + Silicon / HW / SW engineering
  + Product management
  + Manufacturing & test
  + Supply chain & procurement
  + Quality & reliability
* Act as the **central communication hub across stakeholders and executives**

**3. NPI Process & Industrialization**

* Drive NPI lifecycle phases:
  + Concept & feasibility
  + Design & development
  + Prototyping / validation (EVT/DVT/PVT)
  + Manufacturing ramp

* Drive Design for Excellence to ensure first-time-right product industrialization, optimizing manufacturability, testability, cost, and supply chain readiness

* Manage product build plans, pilot runs, and validation activities

**4. Manufacturing & Supply Chain Readiness**

* Ensure:
  + Component readiness and supplier alignment
  + Manufacturing capacity and tooling readiness
  + Test and production flows are qualified
* Coordinate ramp planning and **global factory readiness**
* Optimize **cost, yield, and cycle time** during ramp-up

**5. Risk & Issue Management**

* Identify, track, and mitigate program risks
* Lead resolution of cross-functional issues (technical, supply, schedule)
* Escalate critical issues and drive recovery plans

**6. Financial & Resource Management**

* Manage program budget, cost tracking, and forecasting
* Drive cost optimization and margin targets
* Allocate and manage resources across multiple workstreams

**7. Governance & Reporting**

* Lead program governance (phase reviews, gate reviews, exec updates)
* Provide **clear, data-driven status reporting to leadership**
* Ensure compliance with internal processes and product lifecycle standards
  

  
  

**Key Deliverables (Typical NPI Outputs)**

* Program charter, roadmap, and WBS
* Integrated schedule (milestones, critical path)
* Product build plans and validation reports
* Manufacturing readiness and ramp plans
* Risk registers and mitigation plans
* Cost model / BOM evolution
* Post-launch performance metrics (yield, quality, cost)

* Formal **Lessons Learned report at key milestones**

  

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Semiconductor, SW or related
* 5–10+ years in program/project management in high-tech or manufacturing environment
* Proven experience in **NPI / product development lifecycle management**
* Strong understanding of:
  + Manufacturing processes and supply chain
  + Product development lifecycle (HW/SW systems)
  + Semiconductor or electronics industry (preferred)

**Core Skills**

* **Program leadership & execution excellence**
* Strong **cross-functional influence (matrix organization)**
* Advanced **planning & scheduling (WBS, critical path)**
* Risk management & problem-solving
* Financial acumen (cost, budget, ROI)
* Excellent communication with technical and executive stakeholders
* Ability to thrive in ambiguity and fast-paced environments

**Success Metrics (KPIs)**

* On-time product launch (milestone adherence)
* Cost vs. target / margin achievement
* Product quality (yield, reliability)
* Production ramp efficiency
* Customer satisfaction / business impact

**Typical Reporting Line**

* Reports to: Director / Sr Director Program Management
* Interfaces extensively with:
  + Engineering leadership
  + Operations / manufacturing
  + Supply chain
  + Business units
  + Finance

raw.description:
The application window is expected to close on: 11/30/2026
Your Impact

As the Silicon NPI Business Process Manager for Silicon One, you will be the chief operational architect responsible for standardizing and scaling how Cisco brings pioneering networking silicon from tape-out through production ramp.
Silicon One represents Cisco's flagship routing and switching silicon architecture. In this role, you will design, deploy, and govern end-to-end operational processes across prototype lot planning, supplier forecasting, supply commits, and phase-gate readiness. A central pillar of your scope will be establishing multi-functional clarity by building, embedding, and actively maintaining RACI (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed) frameworks across Silicon Engineering, Product Management, Sourcing, and Manufacturing Operations. Rather than running a single product line, you will establish the institutional framework, playbooks, governance swimlanes, and automated dashboards that empower a team of Supply Chain Program Managers (SCPMs) to implement flawless, predictable new product introductions.

Key Responsibilities

1. Prototype & NPI Build Planning & Supplier Forecast Governance
·       Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs): Design, implement, and govern SOPs for prototype build planning (engineering samples, EVT, DVT, PVT, and qualification lots) across all Silicon One programs.
·       Supplier Forecasting: Establish a unified mechanism for translating engineering build demand into rolling supplier forecasts (foundry wafer starts, OSAT packaging substrates, probe, and final test).
·       Closed-Loop Commits: Build and manage closed-loop supply commit processes with external manufacturing partners and foundries to guarantee material availability against aggressive development schedules.
·       Clear-to-Build (CTB): Standardize Clear-to-Build methodologies, risk-buy policies, and prototype lot prioritization frameworks across multi-project environments.

2. Multi-functional RACI Architecture & Governance
·       RACI Matrices: Architect and maintain comprehensive RACI matrices across the entire pre-production lifecycle, clearly delineating decision rights, achievement sign-offs, and deliverable ownership between SCPMs, Silicon Design Engineering, Sourcing, Product Ops, and Manufacturing.
·       Decision Swimlanes: Establish and govern formal blocking issue paths and decision-making swimlanes for critical NPI inflection points (e.g., ECOs, late tape-out shifts, wafer scrap excursions, split-lot trade-offs, and allocation conflicts).
·       Governance Audits: Periodically audit, refresh, and align RACI boundaries as organizational structures evolve, ensuring zero ambiguity in multi-functional accountability during fast-paced launch cycles.

3. Supply Chain Readiness Phase-Gate Management & SCPM Enablement
·       Phase-Gate Criteria: Define, standardize, and govern phase-gate criteria specific to supply chain readiness for Silicon One products.
·       SCPM Toolkits & Playbooks: Build standardized toolkits, playbooks, RACI-aligned checklist sign-offs, and templates that enable peer SCPMs to drive operational readiness and landmark exit approvals with minimal administrative friction.
·       Multi-functional Alignment: Partner with Product Management, Silicon Design Engineering, Quality, Sourcing, and Manufacturing Operations to ensure alignment at each achievement gate.
·       Continuous Improvement: Institutionalize post-launch retrospectives and continuous improvement loops to capture lessons learned and refine phase-gate rigor.

4. Readiness Metrics, Executive Dashboards & Analytics
·       Executive Dashboard Suite: Design, automate, and publish the official Silicon One NPI Readiness Dashboard suite, tracking program health, achievement attainment, wafer cycle-time velocity, and supply commit integrity.
·       Metric Governance: Establish and track leading and lagging operational benchmarks, including Achievement & Build Schedule Consistency (%), Clear-to-Build (CTB) Lead-Time Health, Foundry & OSAT Commit-to-Request Accuracy, Yield Ramp Velocity vs. Plan, Handoff Readiness Index, and RACI Sign-off Compliance.
·       Executive Readiness Reviews: Synthesize multi-program operational data into executive-level summaries for leadership reviews and business unit executives.

5. Tooling Evolution & Digital Transformation
·       Digital Transformation: Drive the digitization of NPI planning by evaluating, automating, and integrating workflows within enterprise ERP/APS systems (e.g., Kinaxis RapidResponse, Oracle/SAP, Power BI, JIRA/Confluence).
·       Exception-Based Management: Eliminate manual spreadsheet tracking across SCPM teams by building scalable, automated exception-management mechanisms.

Meet the Team

·       Silicon One SCPMs: You will be their operational lead, providing the RACI frameworks, tools, processes, and governance that make their daily program execution seamless.
·       Silicon Engineering & Product Management: Aligning tape-out schedules, silicon revision plans, and product roadmaps with supply chain capability and explicit decision rights.
·       Global Sourcing & Supplier Management: Synchronizing foundry (wafer fab), substrate, packaging (OSAT), and test hardware supplier forecasts.
·       Manufacturing & Sustaining Operations: Establishing clean, contractual handoff criteria and accountability transitions from ramp stabilization into high-volume manufacturing.
·       Executive Leadership: Presenting program readiness, portfolio-level risk heatmaps, and mitigation strategies.

Required Qualifications

·       Experience: 8–10+ years of experience in semiconductor supply chain, NPI program management, silicon operations, or manufacturing process engineering.
·       Semiconductor Domain Expertise: Knowledge of the silicon development lifecycle (tape-out, wafer fab, bump, probe/CP, OSAT assembly, ATE final test, board-level EVT/DVT/PVT).
·       Process Architecture & Governance: Experience designing, documenting, and implementing enterprise-wide supply chain operating models, SOPs, and multi-functional RACI frameworks from scratch.
·       Analytics & Tooling: D ata analytics and dashboard modeling experience (Power BI, Tableau, Advanced Excel, SQL, or Python) with familiarity in ERP/APS platforms (e.g., Kinaxis, SAP, Oracle).

Preferred Qualifications

·       Master’s degree / MBA or MS in Supply Chain / Engineering.
·       Advanced Semiconductor Technologies: Demonstrated experience in high-performance networking ASICs, advanced packaging (e.g., 2.5D/3D, CoWoS, chiplets), or deep sub-micron process nodes.
·       Certifications: Lean Six Sigma, APICS/ASCM (CSCP/CPIM), or PMP certification.
·       Matrixed Governance: Direct experience establishing governance and RACI structures in matrixed, high-velocity hardware organizations.

Why Cisco?
At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.
Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.
We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

raw.description:
Job Details:

Job Description:
Intel is seeking an experienced APTM NPI (New Product Introduction) Integrator to lead technology transfer, manufacturing readiness, quality improvement, and yield optimization activities for advanced packaging and technology development programs. The successful candidate will drive the integration of new technologies into manufacturing by defining roadmaps, establishing operational strategies, and ensuring product and process readiness from startup through high-volume manufacturing.
This role requires combines deep manufacturing expertise, advanced data analytics capabilities, and strategic influence to accelerate technology deployment, improve manufacturing performance, and drive organizational excellence.

We are seeking a highly motivated and technically skilled Integrator to lead the development and execution of new product/ process introduction and process transfers across factories.

The ideal candidate will play a key role in ensuring that technology, platforms, and products meet certification requirements before transferring to HVM.

The NPI integrator will be responsible for but not limited to:
- Being the logistical coordinator of introducing a new product into the factory by supplying the required process documentation to factory customers.
- Primary information interface between the fab and the upstream/downstream customers.
- Tracking the collateral items, communicating wafer shipping to post fab customers, creating and updating the product codes in the internal systems.
- Setting up lot flows, kicking off NPI Checklists for each module, starting the silicon and monitoring its progress through the process flow for set up, power-on and engineering samples until first production.
- Develop and implement new NPI systems and business processes as they become ready and close any issues identified in a NPI reflection
- Utilize data analytics tools (e.g., SQL, Python) to synthesize insights from structured and unstructured data, driving continuous process improvement and troubleshooting.
- Lead cross-functional teams through model-based problem-solving methodologies to address process excursions and drive operational efficiencies.

The candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits:
- Candidates are expected to have strong understanding of a product’s life cycle, fab processing, and post fab activities.
- Good understanding of key product/ process development milestones.
- Should possess strong experience working with and managing NPI builds in factory environment. Able to drive capacity execution efficiency accordingly.
- Demonstrated ability to learn quickly and apply new concepts to solve complex problems.

This role requires regular onsite presence to fulfill essential job responsibilities.

Qualifications:
Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Relevant experience can be obtained through schoolwork, classes, project work, internships, and/or military experience.

Minimum Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field, plus 2+ years of relevant experience; OR
- Master's degree in one of the fields listed above, plus 1+ year of relevant experience.

The experience listed above should include a combination of the following:

- Engineering fundamentals and manufacturing workflows.
- Data extraction and analysis using tools such as SQL and/or Python.

This position is not eligible for intel immigration sponsorship.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience in more than one process module in a WLA, Die Prep, Sort, or Fab environment.
- Familiarity with manufacturing systems such as MES300 and process flow route creation.
- Knowledge of process improvement methodologies, including Intel's Change Control Process and Model-Based Problem Solving (MBPS).
- Experience with new product introduction (NPI) project management and startup of new technologies.
- Process Integration: Experience in integrating packaging processes with overall product manufacturing workflows.
- Package Design: Experience in designing packaging solutions that meet product specifications, regulatory requirements, and customer needs.
- Previous related work experience in a semiconductor foundry.

A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Technical Program Manager at Google, you’ll use your technical expertise to lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish. You’ll work with stakeholders to plan requirements, identify risks, manage project schedules, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. You're equally comfortable explaining your team's analyses and recommendations to executives as you are discussing the technical tradeoffs in product development with engineers.

As part of the Network Planning team, you will be responsible for enabling various data center networking deployments by working with cross functional teams to develop end to end strategies that connect our demand, supply, inventory, data center labor and deployment planning. Your role will directly enable improving effectiveness of network planning team and overall network domain.

This role requires an individual to leverage strategic and end to end thinking. Successful individuals in this role have strong planning backgrounds with an engineering mindset, while being expert communicators and leaders. They are comfortable with ambiguity and complexity, yet strive to increase maturity in processes. They also have the ability to handle multiple programs at the same time while being highly customer focused.
Behind everything our users see online is the architecture built by the Technical Infrastructure team to keep it running. From developing and maintaining our data centers to building the next generation of Google platforms, we make Google's product portfolio possible. We're proud to be our engineers' engineers and love voiding warranties by taking things apart so we can rebuild them. We keep our networks up and running, ensuring our users have the best and fastest experience possible.
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $163000 - $236000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google .

- Experience in managing technical programs with hardware teams.

raw.title: Silicon NPI Supply Chain Program Manager (SCPM)
raw.description:
The application window is expected to close on: 11/30/2026 Meet the Team

Join Cisco's Silicon Operations Team and play a pivotal role in shaping the future of networking as the NPI Product Supply Chain Program Manager (SCPM) for our innovative Cisco Silicon One™ products. This is an opportunity to be at the forefront of next-generation network technology, working within a dynamic and customer-focused supply chain organization.
As a key member of the Silicon Manufacturing Operations (SMO) team, you will be the end-to-end owner for a product family, ensuring seamless supply chain execution from customer demand to product delivery.

Your Impact
- Production Readiness:  Usher our new products from concept to production release by ensuring core operational checklists are completed supporting manufacturability at high volume.
- Demand & Supply Alignment:  Translate customer demand for prototypes, pilots and production ramp into actionable resource requirements, including raw materials, capacity enablement, and manufacturing schedules.
- Order Management:  Manage supply allocation and sales orders, including assigning Schedule Ship Dates (SSD) for new orders and revisions.
- Managing Planning Parameters:  Proactively analyze and manage system lead times and yields, communicating updates weekly to ensure customer requirements are met.
- Internal Customer Management:  Serve as the primary point of contact for customer inquiries, providing timely responses (within 24 hours). Understand customer demand and translate to resource requirements (raw materials, loading plan, capacity need, etc)
- Materials Management:  Oversee the procurement of materials and purchase order (PO) timing against schedules.
- Manufacturing Execution:  Issue assembly build instructions in collaboration with Assembly Engineering (ASY ENG), manage assembly loading schedules and priorities, and manage testing instructions and schedules with Test Engineering.
- Fulfillment Oversight:  Create weekly assembly loading plans based on committed ship plans, and proactively monitor fulfillment to ensure on-time delivery.
- Inventory Management:  Develop and maintain a rolling 6-month ship plan.

Required Qualifications

- 6+ years in supply planning or supply chain management within the semiconductor industry.
- Experience working with semiconductor manufacturing processes and supply chain principles.
- Experience working with BOM structures, manufacturing routing processes (including alternative routes and materials), and product configurations.
- Experience with ERP systems and advanced planning tools.

Preferred Skills

- Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field - or equivalent education and experience.
- Strong Microsoft Excel skills, specifically working with dynamic scenario planning
- Excellent communication, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills.

raw.title: Technical Program Manager, Factory Infrastructure Deployment
raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

Mission Context

ArsenalOS is the digital backbone of Anduril's hardware enterprise. It connects the full lifecycle—from concept to build to field feedback—into one operating environment built for speed, traceability, autonomy, and continuous improvement. This isn't just software for design and planning; it's the factory-facing infrastructure that connects operators, machines, test systems, and OT networks into a unified, adaptive Build Chain.

This is not a support function. ArsenalOS is a strategic investment in how Anduril out-builds, out-adapts, and out-scales the traditional defense industrial base.

Overview

As our factories scale and operate at increasingly high rates, the complexity of the infrastructure stack is growing just as quickly. We're deploying servers, networking, and compute environments into live production settings that cannot stop—and we need someone to own that execution at the site level.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to act as the central coordination point for factory infrastructure deployment. You'll lead the buildout of system administration, servers, networking, and OT infrastructure while ensuring alignment across internal teams and external vendors.

This is not a passive coordination role. This is a hands-on, technical execution-focused position responsible for ensuring that the foundational infrastructure required to run the factory is deployed correctly, on time, and aligned with production needs. You are the person who ensures the infrastructure layer of the factory is built, integrated, and ready to support operations.

What You’ll Do

You will own the infrastructure deployment layer of the factory.

- Act as the primary point of contact for factory infrastructure deployment at a given site

- Coordinate the end-to-end buildout of servers, networking, and system administration environments

- Drive architecture design reviews through maturity gates from System Requirements Review (SRR) through Preliminary Design Review (PDR) to Critical Design Review (CDR), ensuring designs are reviewed, feedback is incorporated, and infrastructure solutions are ready for deployment

- Drive execution across system administrators, network engineers, systems engineers, and infrastructure teams

- Manage and track work across external vendors and contractors

- Manage and track work through Jira planning tools and Confluence to maintain visibility, drive accountability, and keep execution on track

- Maintain a real-time view of site readiness, risks, and dependencies

- Ensure infrastructure deployments are sequenced correctly and aligned with production schedules

- Work closely with technical architects to ensure deployments meet architectural standards and specifications

- Communicate clearly across technical and non-technical stakeholders to keep execution aligned

- Step in hands-on when needed to support infrastructure buildout and unblock teams

- Track and manage inventory planning, purchasing, and financial awareness and communicate status across engineering leads and factory systems leadership

- Be the onsite customer facing lead for brownfield and greenfield assessments to capture infrastructure, power, and electrical requirements and translate them back to engineering teams for execution. Willing to travel 30 to 50% of the time.

You are the person who ensures that the infrastructure layer of the factory is built, integrated, and ready to support operations.

What This Role Is (and Isn’t)

This role is:

- A multi-level owner of infrastructure deployment and execution

- The point of contact to Production leaders and MEs

- A driver of timelines, vendor coordination, and delivery

- A translator between architecture, infrastructure teams, and production needs

- A hands-on operator who can engage technically when required

- A force multiplier across teams executing complex deployments

This role is not:

- A traditional project manager tracking tickets

- A purely strategic or planning-focused TPM

- A role that avoids technical engagement

- A role that waits for perfect clarity before acting

What You Need

- Experience managing complex infrastructure deployments such as data center buildouts, OT environments, or factory systems bring-ups

- Experience in one or more of the following: standing up new network environments, data center buildouts, or systems configuration from scratch

- Strong understanding of networking, servers, and system administration

- Experience coordinating cross-functional technical teams and external vendors

- Ability to operate in fast-paced, high-stakes production environments

- Comfort making decisions with incomplete information

- High ownership and bias for action

Strong preference if you have experience with:

- Factory or OT (Operational Technology) environments

- Infrastructure buildouts in live production settings

- Baseline IT certifications such as CompTIA Security+, CompTIA Network+, or Cisco CCNA

- Networking (routing, switching, firewalls) and compute environments

- Working alongside technical architects and ensuring adherence to design standards

- Experience leading cross functional technical teams for requirements kick off to execution

What Success Looks Like

- Infrastructure deployments are executed on time and aligned with production needs

- You take 0 to 1 projects from ambiguity to execution by clarifying unknowns, solving problems, and taking initiative without waiting to be told

- Vendors and internal teams are coordinated effectively with minimal friction

- Site bring-up timelines decrease and infrastructure-related delays are minimized

- Systems are built correctly the first time and align with architectural standards

- Production teams have reliable, ready-to-use infrastructure when needed

Why This Role Matters

Our factories are scaling rapidly, and the infrastructure that supports them must keep pace.
Without strong ownership of infrastructure deployment, timelines slip, vendors become misaligned, and production readiness is impacted.
This role ensures that the physical and digital infrastructure foundation of the factory is delivered reliably, enabling everything else to function.

NPI Supply Chain Program Manager (E4)
We are looking for an accomplished NPI Supply Chain Program Manager with a strong sense of accountability to join our CoE NPI Supply Chain Program team. The successful candidate will own commodity strategy, supplier selection, cost performance, and the timely integration of CoE technology innovations into NPI programs. Candidates should have strategic sourcing and supply chain expertise, preferably in semiconductors, and proven experience leading complex sourcing programs independently in a fast-paced, corporate-level environment.
Our Mission
CoE NPI Supply Chain is the strategic enterprise integration layer connecting Centers of Excellence (CoE), Business Units, and Global Supply Chain. The mission is to accelerate new product commercialization through cross-functional synergies, standardized supply-chain strategy and execution, improved cost and gross margin performance, and the timely proliferation of technology innovations into NPI programs.
The NPI SCPM is a success-critical enabler for CoE innovation implementation, driving:
- Product Sourcing Strategy – agile, scalable, resilient product ramp through GSC ecosystems.
- Product Cost Performance – product viability and gross margin performance.
- Corporate Synergies – leverage across CoE teams, BUs, and Global Supply Chain.
- Effective Implementation – deploy technology innovations and cost optimization into new products.
Scope spans Supply Chain Strategy & Resiliency, Lab Qual/Cut-in Management, CM Selection & HVM Readiness, Cost Apportionment Model (CAM), Best BoM Assessment, and Cost Reduction Roadmap & Execution across MCOS.
Required Skills & Responsibilities
1. Strategic Sourcing & Commodity Management
- Commodity strategy: market intelligence, supplier landscape, multi-year sourcing roadmaps.
- Supplier selection and qualification: RFx, technical/commercial evaluation, CM selection for HVM readiness.
- Negotiation and contracting: pricing, SOWs, T&Cs, and TCO optimization.
- CAM, should-costing, Best BoM scenarios, and cost reduction roadmap execution.
- Supply chain resiliency: dual sourcing, risk mitigation, and lab qual / cut-in management.
2. Program & Project Management
- End-to-end planning: scope, schedule, critical path, dependencies, milestones.
- Execution rigor: operating cadence, action tracking, stakeholder readouts.
- Risk & issue management: RAID logs, mitigation, escalation, decision logs.
- Vendor/partner coordination and governance across internal/external teams.
3. Supply Chain & Semiconductor Domain
- NPI to HVM ramp: supply readiness, capacity planning, ramp governance.
- Semi supply chain: lead-times, allocation, shortage management, lifecycle/obsolescence.
- Supplier management: qualification, scorecards, QBRs, corrective actions.
- Manufacturing & logistics fundamentals (MRP concepts, inventory, material flow).
- Preferred Commodity Experience:
- Polymers & Plastics precision machining
- Laser & Sensors – optical, motion, temperature, pressure, and process sensors.
- Solid State Batteries – next-generation energy storage, cell chemistry, and qualification.
- PCBA – CM/EMS engagement, BoM management, component sourcing, HVM ramp.
4. Strategic Initiative Leadership
- Translate strategy into executable workstreams, KPIs, and outcomes.
- Executive governance: steering committees, decision forums, status narratives.
- Cross-functional alignment across engineering, sourcing, operations, finance, quality, legal.
- Benefits realization: track adoption, savings, and operational impact to closure.
5. Data, Analytics & Communication
- Quantitative analysis: business cases, sensitivities, scenarios; KPI design.
- Advanced Excel (pivot tables, Power Query/Power Pivot) and PowerPoint storytelling.
- Influence without authority; concise written and verbal communication.
- Executive presence: present complex topics simply and handle challenging Q&A.
6. Accountability & Execution Mindset
- Thrives in a highly complex, energetic, corporate-level environment with an independent work style.
- High ownership: identifies gaps, proposes solutions, and drives closure.
- Bias for action with quality and compliance; structured problem solving (5 Whys, Fishbone).
- Continuous improvement: Lean/Kaizen, standard work, and process optimization.
Preferred Commodity Experience
- PCBA – Contract Manufacturer/ EMS engagement, BoM management, component sourcing, HVM ramp.
- Precision Metal Machining, Sheet Metal
Competency Expectations
- Interprets business challenges and recommends best practices to improve products, processes, or services.
- Leads cross-functional teams or projects with moderate resource needs, risk, and complexity.
- Solves complex problems using sophisticated analytical thought and innovative solutions.
- Impacts customer, operational, project, or service objectives; guided by functional policies.
- Communicates difficult concepts and negotiates to align stakeholders.
Qualifications
- Education: BA/BS in Business, Engineering, Supply Chain, or related field; MS/MBA preferred.
- Experience: Minimum 6 years in Strategic Sourcing, Program Management, consulting, and/or Supply Chain, preferably in semiconductors.
- Demonstrated ability to work and execute independently in a highly complex, fast-paced, corporate-level environment.

- Supply chain & procurement
- Quality & reliability

- Manufacturing capacity and tooling readiness
- Test and production flows are qualified

- Strong understanding of: - Manufacturing processes and supply chain

- Strong cross-functional influence (matrix organization)

Overall Responsibilities:

This posting is for an MDP New Product Introduction (NPI) instructor based in Austin, TX or Santa Clara, CA. This position is a combination technical instructor and technical expert role on existing and new products. The position requires work to be conducted within the business unit (BU) manufacturing and the development lab to learn the new products under development, gain experience on the startup and sustaining production tasks on the tool, and develop/deliver initial classroom and hands-on training on the tool. Once the tool transitions to volume production, the NPI instructor will train and certify the volume instructor, who then takes over the product from a training ownership standpoint.

The position will require learning, and application of that learning, on three fronts – (1) training fundamentals; (2) existing products; and (3) new product training development.  Training fundamentals will cover the training methodology, tools, materials and confidence to deliver both live distance learning (LDL) and instructor-led hands-on (ILT) course delivery. Existing products start with basic operations and maintenance, followed by trouble shooting and diagnostics, and eventually mastery of the tool. Product training development will require content development and project management skills to help bring a new tool design from concept to reality, through the development of comprehensive training curriculum, student guides, and supporting materials and technologies.

Due to the scheduling of PDP/NPI product development, the NPI instructor will often be researching, gaining knowledge/experience, and developing/delivering for several new tools/chambers at a time, so project management, training/presentation experience, and technical acumen (mechanical, electrical, troubleshooting, etc.) of semiconductor equipment is required.

Basic breakdown of time is:
~45% learning the new tool and gaining knowledge and experience (mechanical, electrical, software, process, etc.) and developing the course materials, structure and updating of existing courses
~35% delivering training or coordinating structured factory OJT
~20% other activities

- Deliver specialized New Product Introduction (NPI) technical training both in-house and at customer locations, requiring domestic and international travel. Manage classroom and lab activities to ensure course objectives are met and adhere to safety procedures. Training may occur during off-shift hours and weekends as assigned.
- Learn and maintain comprehensive technical knowledge of new and improved products to prepare and present defined courses. raw.title: Sr, Technical Program Manager
Technical Program Manager, Factory Infrastructure Deployment
raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

Mission Context

ArsenalOS is the digital backbone of Anduril's hardware enterprise. It connects the full lifecycle—from concept to build to field feedback—into one operating environment built for speed, traceability, autonomy, and continuous improvement. This isn't just software for design and planning; it's the factory-facing infrastructure that connects operators, machines, test systems, and OT networks into a unified, adaptive Build Chain.

This is not a support function. ArsenalOS is a strategic investment in how Anduril out-builds, out-adapts, and out-scales the traditional defense industrial base.

Overview

As our factories scale and operate at increasingly high rates, the complexity of the infrastructure stack is growing just as quickly. We're deploying servers, networking, and compute environments into live production settings that cannot stop—and we need someone to own that execution at the site level.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to act as the central coordination point for factory infrastructure deployment. You'll lead the buildout of system administration, servers, networking, and OT infrastructure while ensuring alignment across internal teams and external vendors.

This is not a passive coordination role. This is a hands-on, technical execution-focused position responsible for ensuring that the foundational infrastructure required to run the factory is deployed correctly, on time, and aligned with production needs. You are the person who ensures the infrastructure layer of the factory is built, integrated, and ready to support operations.

What You’ll Do

You will own the infrastructure deployment layer of the factory.

- Act as the primary point of contact for factory infrastructure deployment at a given site

- Coordinate the end-to-end buildout of servers, networking, and system administration environments

- Drive architecture design reviews through maturity gates from System Requirements Review (SRR) through Preliminary Design Review (PDR) to Critical Design Review (CDR), ensuring designs are reviewed, feedback is incorporated, and infrastructure solutions are ready for deployment

- Drive execution across system administrators, network engineers, systems engineers, and infrastructure teams

- Manage and track work across external vendors and contractors

- Manage and track work through Jira planning tools and Confluence to maintain visibility, drive accountability, and keep execution on track

- Maintain a real-time view of site readiness, risks, and dependencies

- Ensure infrastructure deployments are sequenced correctly and aligned with production schedules

- Work closely with technical architects to ensure deployments meet architectural standards and specifications

- Communicate clearly across technical and non-technical stakeholders to keep execution aligned

- Step in hands-on when needed to support infrastructure buildout and unblock teams

- Track and manage inventory planning, purchasing, and financial awareness and communicate status across engineering leads and factory systems leadership

- Be the onsite customer facing lead for brownfield and greenfield assessments to capture infrastructure, power, and electrical requirements and translate them back to engineering teams for execution. Willing to travel 30 to 50% of the time.

You are the person who ensures that the infrastructure layer of the factory is built, integrated, and ready to support operations.

What This Role Is (and Isn’t)

This role is:

- A multi-level owner of infrastructure deployment and execution

- The point of contact to Production leaders and MEs

- A driver of timelines, vendor coordination, and delivery

- A translator between architecture, infrastructure teams, and production needs

- A hands-on operator who can engage technically when required

- A force multiplier across teams executing complex deployments

This role is not:

- A traditional project manager tracking tickets

- A purely strategic or planning-focused TPM

- A role that avoids technical engagement

- A role that waits for perfect clarity before acting

What You Need

- Experience managing complex infrastructure deployments such as data center buildouts, OT environments, or factory systems bring-ups

- Experience in one or more of the following: standing up new network environments, data center buildouts, or systems configuration from scratch

- Strong understanding of networking, servers, and system administration

- Experience coordinating cross-functional technical teams and external vendors

- Ability to operate in fast-paced, high-stakes production environments

- Comfort making decisions with incomplete information

- High ownership and bias for action

Strong preference if you have experience with:

- Factory or OT (Operational Technology) environments

- Infrastructure buildouts in live production settings

- Baseline IT certifications such as CompTIA Security+, CompTIA Network+, or Cisco CCNA

- Networking (routing, switching, firewalls) and compute environments

- Working alongside technical architects and ensuring adherence to design standards

- Experience leading cross functional technical teams for requirements kick off to execution

What Success Looks Like

- Infrastructure deployments are executed on time and aligned with production needs

- You take 0 to 1 projects from ambiguity to execution by clarifying unknowns, solving problems, and taking initiative without waiting to be told

- Vendors and internal teams are coordinated effectively with minimal friction

- Site bring-up timelines decrease and infrastructure-related delays are minimized

- Systems are built correctly the first time and align with architectural standards

- Production teams have reliable, ready-to-use infrastructure when needed

Why This Role Matters

Our factories are scaling rapidly, and the infrastructure that supports them must keep pace.
Without strong ownership of infrastructure deployment, timelines slip, vendors become misaligned, and production readiness is impacted.
This role ensures that the physical and digital infrastructure foundation of the factory is delivered reliably, enabling everything else to function.
US Salary Range
$132,000 — $175,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits .

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

-
No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

- Please always verify communications:

- Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

- Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com .

-
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

-
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

About the Role

As a member of the DC / Infrastructure Finance team, you will report to the Manager of DC / Infrastructure Finance and serve as a finance partner to Supply Chain and Strategic Sourcing. You will connect equipment purchasing plans, supplier commitments, delivery schedules, and deployment needs to capital spending and cash forecasts, helping Lambda secure infrastructure capacity while managing cost and inventory exposure.



What You'll Do

Equipment Capital Planning

 - Build and maintain equipment capital spending forecasts across GPUs, servers, networking, storage, and spares by supplier, platform, and deployment

In-Service Timing and Depreciation

 - Model the financial impact of supplier alternatives, volume commitments, payment terms, and component cost changes to support sourcing negotiations and recommendations

 - Track negotiated savings and cost increases against approved assumptions, distinguishing expected savings from realized financial impact

Purchase Commitments and Cash Forecasting

 - Own the team’s commitments data across equipment and construction spend, connecting purchase orders, receipts, invoices, and payments into a single source used by DC Finance and Corporate FP&A

 - Maintain financial visibility into open purchase orders, deposits, prepayments, contractual commitments, and remaining equipment spending

 - Own supplier payment forecasts using contractual terms, delivery and acceptance dates, and invoice status as inputs to the consolidated cash forecast for Corporate FP&A and Treasury

 - Assess the cost and cash implications of order changes, delivery delays, expedited shipments, and cancellation or rescheduling provisions

 - Partner with Supply Chain to track the financial exposure associated with equipment on order, in transit, in storage, and awaiting deployment

 - Work with capacity planning, DC Finance, and Business / Commercial Finance to align purchasing assumptions with site readiness and demand forecasts, highlighting mismatches and cash tied up in idle equipment

 - Partner with Accounting and Supply Chain to reconcile purchase orders, receipts, invoices, deposits, and accrual inputs; support consistent project and asset cost attribution

 - Coordinate equipment cost assumptions with DC Finance and provide financial analysis to Treasury and Capital Markets for equipment funding evaluations

 - Prepare supplier, equipment cost, commitment, and inventory reporting for business reviews, executive discussions, and investment recommendations

 - Provide equipment cost inputs and analysis for investment committee reviews, and compare realized equipment costs and delivery timing with approved assumptions after deployment

 - Build and maintain repeatable models and workflows in Pigment and AI-assisted tools, reducing manual spreadsheet work

Applied Materials is seeking an experienced Supply Chain Project Manager. The role will be at the Austin office and is onsite (not remote or hybrid).

As a key member of the Global Supply Chain Strategy Office, you will manage projects that protect continuity of supply as Applied accelerated material innovations. Working within the Transitions and Compliance team, you will run assigned continuity projects — supplier moves, dual-sourcing, supplier exits, and integration activity — from intake through closure: building the cross-functional team, maintaining the plan, and driving deliverables and risks to resolution. This role suits a proactive, organized supply chain professional who manages detail well, communicates clearly, and carries commitments to closure across a matrixed global organization.
- Strong supply chain, procurement or sourcing experience.

- Project Management: Manage multiple supply chain continuity projects simultaneously, from intake and scoping through execution and closure — defining outcomes, milestones and resource needs, and delivering to plan.
- Supplier Transitions: Manage assigned supplier transitions — site moves, dual-sourcing, supplier exits and integration activity — ensuring complete part lists are captured, qualification and audit activity is scheduled, and supply is protected throughout.
- Change Management: Manage supplier change notifications for assigned continuity projects — confirming incoming changes are accurate and complete, resolving conflicts, and routing and expediting approvals to meet Applied change management requirements.
- SNF Administration: Support the SNF program team with day-to-day administration of the Supplier Notification Form process — reviewing incoming supplier submissions for completeness, routing them to the correct approvers, and following up on aging tasks.
- Material Movement: Plan and track the movement of material between suppliers, Applied sites and qualification locations — coordinating shipments, documentation and delivery commitments so material arrives when the project plan requires it.
- Collaboration & Communication: Build and maintain strong working relationships across Global Supply Chain, Quality, Engineering, the Business Units and supplier contacts. Convene working meetings, document decisions, hold owners to their commitments, and provide clear and timely status to stakeholders at all levels.
- Risk & Issue Management: Identify risk early, confirm ownership with the responsible functions, track dependencies and open decisions, and escalate through established channels to limit downstream delay.
- Analytics & Reporting: Pull and validate part, supplier and project data, analyze, and develop the reporting used to track material status and risk reporting that drives decisions.
- Continuous Improvement & Documentation: Ensure all phases of project, program and process development are documented and disseminated to the relevant functional areas, and contribute improvements to team templates, playbooks and standards.

- Proven ability to influence and build relationships across diverse teams and geographies.

This role is pivotal in protecting continuity of supply as Applied’s supply base evolves. The projects you deliver keep material flowing and factories building.

raw.description:
Who We Are

Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits .

This posting is for a New Product Introduction (NPI) Instructor based in Santa Clara, CA; Austin, TX; Hillsboro, OR; or Phoenix, AZ. This position combines the responsibilities of a technical instructor and technical expert for both existing and new products.

The position requires work within the business unit (BU) manufacturing environment and development lab to learn new products under development, gain experience with tool startup and sustaining production tasks, and develop and deliver initial classroom and hands-on training for the tool.
Once the tool transitions to volume production, the NPI Instructor will train and certify the volume instructor, who will then assume training ownership of the product.

The position requires learning and applying knowledge across three areas:
(1) training fundamentals;
(2) existing products; and
(3) new product training development.

Training fundamentals will cover the methodology, tools, materials, and confidence needed to deliver both Live Distance Learning (LDL) and Instructor-Led Training (ILT), including hands-on course delivery.

Existing product training begins with basic operations and maintenance, followed by troubleshooting and diagnostics, and eventually progresses to mastery of the tool. New product training development requires content development and project management skills to help bring a new tool design from concept to reality through the development of comprehensive training curricula, student guides, and supporting materials and technologies.

Due to PDP/NPI product development schedules, the NPI Instructor will often be researching, gaining knowledge and experience, and developing and delivering training for several new tools/chambers simultaneously. Therefore, project management skills, training/presentation experience, and strong technical acumen in semiconductor equipment, including mechanical, electrical, and troubleshooting skills, are required.

Basic Breakdown of Time
~45%: Learning new tools and gaining knowledge and experience in mechanical, electrical, software, process, and related areas; developing course materials and structure; and updating existing courses
~35%: Delivering training or coordinating structured factory OJT
~20%: Other activities

Key Responsibilities:
- Deliver specialized New Product Introduction (NPI) technical training both in-house and at customer locations, requiring domestic and international travel. Manage classroom and lab activities to ensure course objectives are met and adhere to safety procedures. Training may occur during off-shift hours and weekends as assigned.
- Learn and maintain comprehensive technical knowledge of new and improved products to prepare and present defined courses. Disseminate new information to staff, complete certifications on multiple platforms and processes, including safety modules, and actively certify others. Establish new certification requirements.
- Follow and engage in Product Development Process (PDP) for all NPI products at Phase Gate 3 or earlier to ensure completion of NPI course to support the tool immediately prior to shipment of second tool to field.
- Utilize Technical Publications and System Product Business Groups to maximize documentation efficiencies. Create and augment documentation to address gaps in released materials, evaluate instructor performance, train others in standard course development processes (Instructional System Design), and oversee course design approval.
- Provide technical expertise and troubleshooting skills to assist with system repairs; ensures system functionality can support course objectives; ensures all safety retrofits are installed on the training systems.
- Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the Global Technical Training organization and operations, as well as the Applied Global Services (AGS) organization. Inform customers of additional Global Technical Training (GTT) courses and products, assist marketing in building customer relationships and selling GTT products, analyze customer issues and needs to identify future training opportunities, and present comprehensive training solutions.
- Provide coaching and leadership to other instructors, serving as a mentor to less senior instructors for class delivery, technical development, and certification. Anticipate, prevent, and resolve customer satisfaction issues.
- Manage multiple projects of diverse scope and complexity, directing project team members.
- Support Early Learning System (ELS) / Alpha Site engineering in-house or on engineering tools, review ECOs, and communicate with the field.
- Assist Global Product Support (GPS) in the generation of documentation.
- Develop new procedures and Best Known Methods.
- Collaborate with Engineering and Manufacturing on the first chamber build and participate in new product final testing.
- Develop technical materials working directly with Instructional Designers (ID).
- Observe technical activities to determine operating procedure and detail.
- Interview personnel to become familiar with products & methods
- Study technical documents to integrate technology, operating procedures, production sequences, and details.
- Review published materials and recommend revisions.
- Communicate with Business Units to obtain current product information for course updates and represent GTT at product NPI meetings.

Qualifications/Experience:
- Bachelor's degree in engineering, education, or training, or equivalent military experience
- Preferred: Professional semiconductor equipment experience in installation, programming, safety, maintenance, operation, troubleshooting, and repair of semiconductor machinery equipment (such as robots, programmable controllers, power supplies, pneumatics, vacuum systems, power distributions, facilities, high voltage systems, high current systems, and robot controllers), following manuals, specifications, blueprints, and schematics, and using hand tools, measuring instruments, and testing equipment
- Preferred: Nationally recognized certification in Instructional Design or 2 years of formal or informal experience in curriculum development and/or instructional design. Friesen, Kaye and Associates (FKA) instructional design certification is a plus.

raw.title: Materials Program Manager
Senior Asset Analyst, Supply Chain
raw.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

Crusoe is seeking a Senior Asset Analyst to own asset data integrity, reporting, and disposition across our AI cloud data center hardware fleet. You will keep records for GPU servers, networking, storage, and optics accurate across every system of record, build the reporting that Operations, Finance, and leadership rely on, and take end-to-end ownership of asset disposition as the program matures.



You will work alongside the Asset Manager and partner directly with Procurement, Fleet, Site Operations, Accounting, and Security. This role has real autonomy: you run your own workstream, and you automate the manual work instead of living with it.



This role will be fully onsite at our Denver, CO office.



What You Will Be Working On:

 - Data Integrity and Reconciliation: Audit and reconcile asset records across systems of record, resolve discrepancies, and establish one reliable source of truth.

 - Root Cause and Data Standards: Diagnose data gaps, close them at the source with upstream teams, and define required fields, standards, and validation rules.

 - Reporting and Dashboards: Build and maintain dashboards covering inventory position, deployment status, warranty coverage, and end-of-life exposure. Deliver recurring and ad hoc reporting for Operations, Finance, and leadership.

 - Finance and Planning Support: Provide asset data for budget planning and forecasting (spares, warranty renewals, refresh cycles) and support depreciation, audit, and compliance reporting with Accounting and Security.

 - Risk Flagging: Surface aging hardware, coverage gaps, and unaccounted assets before they become problems.

 - Asset Disposition (growing scope): Own disposition from identification through decommissioning handoff, vendor coordination, and closure. Maintain chain of custody and sanitization evidence, reconcile remarketing proceeds and credits, and manage disposal vendors and certificates of destruction.

 - Lifecycle Operations Support: Support assets from receiving through deployment, transfer, and decommissioning. Work with  suppliers on shipment data, part numbers, and warranty records.

 - Automation and Process: Automate recurring reconciliation and reporting with SQL, scripting, and AI tools. Write and maintain SOPs in Confluence as workflows evolve, and partner with cross-functional teams to put processes in place, gather feedback and refine them over time.

 - Systems Readiness: Support data validation and cutover when asset tooling and systems change.



What You Will Bring to the Team:

 - Experience: 5 to 7 years in data center operations, hardware asset management, inventory management, or a data-focused operations role.

 - Data Skills: Advanced Excel required. SQL strongly preferred.

 - Reconciliation: Proven experience reconciling data across multiple systems of record and resolving conflicting sources of truth.

 - Platforms: Hands-on experience with asset management, ITAM, ERP, or DCIM platforms.

 - Reporting: Experience building dashboards in a BI tool such as Sigma, Tableau, or Power BI.

 - Automation and AI: Active use of scripting or AI tools to remove manual work from your own workflow.

 - Ownership: Track record of running a workstream end to end with minimal direction in a fast-moving environment where process evolves alongside the fleet.

 - Communication: Clear communicator across engineering, finance, and operations, with the written skill to turn a process into documentation someone else can follow.



Bonus Points:

 - Hands-on familiarity with data center hardware: servers, GPUs, storage, networking, PDUs, and CDUs.

 - Experience with hardware disposition, remarketing, or e-waste vendor management.

 - Exposure to procurement systems, purchase order workflows, or fixed asset accounting and depreciation.

 - Experience supporting budget planning, forecasting, or capital expenditure processes.

 - Familiarity with hardware lifecycle concepts: EOL, RMA, warranty management, and secure data sanitization.

 - Experience in hyperscale or cloud infrastructure environments.

 - Professional certification such as CHAMP, CSAM, or ITIL.



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $95,000 - $115,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE: Join Supply Chain Operations in Austin, TX and help accelerate AMD product revenues. As a Supply Chain Program Manager, Rack Supply, you'll partner with AMD Business Units and rack manufacturers (ODMs) to provision capacity and supply ahead of end-customer orders. Own rack supply planning, including validated demand inputs, clear-to-build (CTB) material readiness, and factory capacity/throughput, and serve as the central source for rack supply commitments. THE PERSON: You are analytical, action-oriented, and comfortable operating at pace amid ambiguity. You turn demand signals into executable plans, align cross-functional partners (Business Units, Procurement, Engineering, and Operations), and drive closure with external manufacturers. You communicate clearly, translate constraints into options, and follow through to protect commitments and revenue. You have the ability to influence cross-functional partners across Engineering, Program Management, Procurement, Operations, Business Units, suppliers, and external manufacturers to secure commitments and drive issue closure. You have strong analytical and communication skills, with the ability to translate technical constraints into clear options, risks, recovery actions, and decision-ready updates for senior stakeholders. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Technical Demand, BOM & Design-for-Supply Alignment Translate Business Unit demand signals into technically executable rack-level supply plans across ODMs, suppliers, AMD procurement, engineering, and program teams. Partner with rack architects, system engineers, BOM owners, and technical program managers to identify and resolve supply blockers through design-for-supply decisions. Use Agile BOM fluency to interpret complex rack bills of material, assess supply risk across more than 150 unique part numbers, and drive closure on BOM readiness, alternates, and supplier enablement. Compare AMD forecasts to customer order coverage and material readiness; highlight gaps, deltas, technical constraints, and timing risk. Maintain an end-to-end demand-to-supply view across the S&OP horizon, including demand, build and ship plans, CTB status, factory capacity, engineering changes, constraints, and recovery actions. NPI and Production Supply Readiness, CTB & Material Planning Lead NPI supply planning in a dynamic design environment, adapting plans for constant engineering changes, factory cut-ins, supplier lead times, and new product improvements. Analyze material availability across rack-level BOMs, including AMD consigned components and supplier-controlled parts, and convert CTB findings into executable build priorities and escalation plans. Secure rack supply commitments from ODMs based on verified CTB, documented constraints, and cross-functional recovery actions. Drive supply allocation decisions for constrained AMD components to support internal and external build priorities while protecting revenue and program milestones. Contribute to breakthrough planning capabilities with Supply Chain Transformation, including supplier-data feeds and parallel MRP/CTB modeling in tools such as Kinaxis. Factory Planning, Operational Execution & Leadership Readouts Interface directly with rack manufacturers and system integrators to manage factory capacity, throughput assumptions, tactical build priorities, material shortages, test enablement, yield, and cycle-time constraints. Coordinate simultaneous NPI ramps across multiple system integrators and prepare planning processes for future ODM/SI expansion. Lead daily and weekly operating cadences to resolve supply gaps, remove administrative blockers, and align factories, procurement, engineering, program management, and Business Units on recovery actions. Develop decision-ready status, risk, and escalation materials for senior leadership reviews, including program, operations, and executive-level updates. Publish consolidated rack supply views that connect demand, CTB, capacity, build priorities, and revenue risk into one actionable operating model. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Experience working in technical supply chain, engineering program management, NPI, manufacturing operations, or a related cross-functional planning role. Ability to interpret complex technical inputs, including BOM structure, engineering changes, material readiness, factory constraints, and customer or program requirements. Experience connecting demand signals to supply plans across multiple planning horizons, including short-term execution, mid-range recovery planning, and long-range capacity or material readiness. Background in supporting rack-scale systems, server/data center hardware, AI infrastructure, or other complex, multi-level BOM environments. Expertise in engineering, technical program management, or NPI program management in a hardware development or manufacturing environment. Track record of partnering with system engineers, rack architects, BOM owners, commodity teams, and technical program managers to resolve design, material, or manufacturing readiness issues. Hands-on familiarity with Agile BOM processes, engineering change control, CTB analysis, supplier enablement, and material shortage resolution. Experience with contract manufacturers, ODMs, or system integrators, including capacity planning, factory constraints, build prioritization, test readiness, and delivery commitments. Working knowledge of ERP/MRP and planning tools; strong Excel skills, with Power BI, Kinaxis, or similar planning/analytics tools as a plus. APICS/ASCM certification (CPIM/CSCP), PMP, or a similar supply chain/program management certification is a plus. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Engineering Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or related field is preferred. Advanced degree (MBA/MS) is a plus. Build and maintain well-developed program plans, risk assessments, dependency tracking, reporting mechanisms, and decision frameworks throughout the program lifecycle. Identify opportunities to improve deployment processes, validation methodologies, release coordination, system reliability, and overall customer program execution. Plan proactively for development and deployment risks, identify prevention and mitigation methods, and address issues early to reduce schedule disruption and engineering cost. Experience supporting data center GPUs, accelerators, servers, AI infrastructure, or other complex compute platforms. Experience managing programs involving platform validation, system debug, post-silicon activities, cluster bring-up, software release coordination, and production ramp. Strong customer-facing verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical issues into clear program status, risks, decisions, and actions.
