raw.description:
Who We Are

Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.

What We Offer

Salary:
$88,000.00 - $121,000.00
Location:
Austin,TX, Santa Clara,CA
You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits .

Key Responsibilities
- Forecasts and communicates engineering, materials, and manufacturing requirements to suppliers.  Provides input to outsourcing decisions by performing make versus buy analysis. Coordinates demand signals through MRP to minimize inventory exposure.
- Leads Materials Core Team and coordinates product development process deliverables through matrix management of buyers, planners, and production control.  Collaborates with engineering team to interpret engineering requirements.
- With limited/ no supervision, creates, releases and updates new project materials strategy.
- Sourcing:  Assists in supplier price and delivery negotiations; under direct supervision may negotiate contracts as necessary.  Utilizes the preferred supplier selection and assessment process when selecting suppliers.  Completes supplier risk assessment on critical and unique parts.  Monitors supplier performance (delivery, quality, cost).
- Materials: Coordinates activities around source selection, specification creation and price negotiation with appropriate team members.
- Executes commercialization (transition) materials plan).
- Manages materials change control process. Meets cost objectives and resolves quality issues.  Generates and publishes Key Process Indicators . Tracks total landed costs targets.
- Works with engineering to identify preliminary critical parts, long-lead parts and inspection requirements.  Assists and/ or leads in developing supplier and commodity road maps to engineering.  Utilizes value analysis on build-to-print components in support of Should Cost analysis.

You can communicate effectively with engineers working through detailed system issues as well as senior leaders who need concise, data-driven program updates. You are also excited about finding new ways to improve engineering workflows through automation, Agentic AI, and AI-driven operational tools. Drive alignment across GPU, CPU, firmware, BIOS/BMC, systems, networking, lab infrastructure, validation, and other engineering teams. Provide clear, data-driven program updates to engineering teams and senior leadership while proactively escalating risks, dependencies, and critical tradeoffs. Familiarity with rack-level bring-up and system dependencies including power, cooling, networking, cabling, and infrastructure readiness. Experience working through hardware and firmware debug cycles in pre-production, validation, deployment, or customer-facing environments. Experience coordinating cross-functional engineering teams and driving technical issues to closure without direct authority. raw.description:
The application window is expected to close on: 11/29/2026 This position will be a hybrid role based in our San Jose, CA office.

Meet the team

The Energy Networking System Team is new and highly visible group dedicated to driving innovative energy management and power distribution solutions developed to improve sustainability, efficiency, and reliability in data centers, smart buildings, and IT infrastructure. You will work closely with key hardware engineers within the Business Unit, as well as external suppliers, Global Supply Management (GSM), and Supply Chain Finance. This collaborative environment is crucial to ensuring that product portfolio readiness, cost savings and gross margin performance expectations are met and fully aligned with our broader Business Unit strategy.

Your Impact

As a Supply Chain Program Manager (SCPM), you will serve as the primary driver for supply chain readiness, total cost management, and BOM resiliency for all hardware programs from pre-concept through First Hardware Ship (FHS), holding accountability for the assigned product portfolio’s total cost and margin management, cost optimization programs, and risk mitigation. You will validate the integrity of costed BOMs and forward costing to articulate main cost drivers, support standard and gross margin management through commodity analysis, and BOM optimization, and lead ramp plans to ensure continuity of material supply and delivery between prototype and early production phases.

Minimum Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration or related field (or equivalent experience)
- 3+ years of professional experience in Supply Chain and Cost Management or an equivalent field.
- Previous experience with cost avoidance, cost reduction, and value engineering.
- Applied experience in understanding, analyzing, and managing product Bills of Material (BOM) and costing structures.
- Experience with root cause analysis and complex problem-solving within a technical (manufacturing) environment.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in manufacturing and process improvements to drive cost-down and lead-time improvements.
- Knowledge of PLM processes and experience with the Agile PDM system.
- Analytical capabilities and strong presentation skills to communicate effectively with stakeholders.
- Effective verbal and written English communication skills.
- Efficient organizational and multi-tasking abilities to manage multiple high-priority projects simultaneously.
- Knowledge and application of industry innovations and trends as they relate to product or program development.

Why Cisco?
At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.
Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.
We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

The Role and Impact
As a Supply Chain Planning Analyst, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and optimizing Intel's supply chain strategies. You will lead the development, integration, and execution of planning schedules, materials requirements, forecasts, and inventory strategies to ensure seamless operations and alignment with customer needs. Your contributions will directly impact Intel's ability to deliver high-quality products on time, driving operational excellence and business success.

Business Group
You will join Intel's Corporate Planning Group (CPG), which focuses on optimizing supply chain planning activities across diverse domains. The team partners with stakeholders across engineering, marketing, finance, and manufacturing to develop strategies that support Intel's broader goals of innovation and operational efficiency. This role is part of the DCG_HVM Server Planning team, contributing to Intel's efforts in delivering cutting-edge products and solutions to meet customer demands.

Key Responsibilities
- Develop, integrate, and execute supply chain planning schedules, forecasts, and inventory strategies to meet business needs.
- Conduct scenario and what-if planning for processes, engineering, and inventory strategies.
- Analyze and optimize supply versus demand balancing, applying quantitative and qualitative inputs for decision-making.
- Coordinate with suppliers to ensure uninterrupted material management and delivery timelines.
- Monitor and resolve inventory issues to support short-term and long-term business objectives.
- Collaborate with stakeholders across supply chain functions to drive alignment on business strategies.
- Evaluate capacity needs and capabilities within the supply chain to ensure smooth operations.
- Lead continuous improvement initiatives for processes and tools, driving efficiency and effectiveness.

-Incorporate BI reporting to convert raw data into accurate, meaningful visuals that facilitate automated monitoring and strategic decision-making.

- 4+ years of relevant supply chain experience.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office tools, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint.

- Master's degree in a related field.
- Experience using analytical and data visualization tools such as Power BI.

raw.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all .
Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

About our Team:
The Smart Manufacturing AI Pathfinding & Innovation (AIPI) team sits at the absolute forefront of technological discovery, exploring unproven AI architectures, next-generation large language models (LLMs), speculative multimodal systems, and emerging agentic frameworks. Our mission is to guide initiatives from speculative research concepts into functional proofs-of-concept (PoCs) while systematically de-risking and validating the future of our AI technical roadmap.

Position Overview:
We are seeking a highly strategic and technically fluent Technical Program Manager (TPM) to join our Smart Manufacturing AI Pathfinding & Innovation (AIPI) team. In this role, you will thrive in deep ambiguity, bridging the gap between research, machine learning engineers, infrastructure teams, and executive leaders to structure the discovery process itself and transform exploratory ideas into actionable, measurable programs.

Responsibilities:
- Drive the daily work and enable the long-term strategy of AIPI programs; develop and document processes and methodologies to drive consistency across AIPI initiatives; act as a central point of contact and single source of truth for AIPI programs.
- Oversee all aspects of AI pathfinding projects, including resourcing and timeline; design and maintain scalable project roadmaps aligned with strategic goals; identify and work to close any technical gap or barrier stalling project achievement.
- Represent the AIPI function in cross-functional operations initiatives, working teams, and meetings to further priorities, establish relationships, and act as liaison between organizations; partner closely with collaborators and SMEs to develop meaningful, measurable objectives and actions.
- Advise leadership on technical feasibility, risk mitigation, and resource allocation to optimize outcomes; communicate high-level technical risks and breakthroughs clearly to non-technical executives; develop, coordinate, and sustain top-level organizational objectives with regular read-outs to senior/executive partners.
- Partner to identify technical bottlenecks, evaluate trade-offs, and decide when to adjust, scale, or end experimental paths. Remove technical and operational barriers so research teams can move quickly. Establish quick learning loops, checkpoints, and measures for unproven technologies. Implement and lead all aspects of important measures to ensure deliverables are achieved and have the desired impact.

Minimum Qualifications:
- Computer Science, Engineering, or other related technical degree.
- 5+ years experience in complex program management and demonstrated success in global program execution.
- Proven ability to manage sophisticated technical programs, coordinate cross-functional teams, and drive projects to successful completion while balancing competing priorities and constraints.
- Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to make data-driven decisions in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
- Extensive experience interacting with senior executives.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Expertise in program management, project management, and vendor relationship management.
- Ability to navigate ambiguity, and shape unstructured, exploratory ideas into defined experimental roadmaps.
- AI Literacy: Solid foundational understanding of AI concepts, including deep learning, neural network architectures, transformers, training vs. inference lifecycles, and modern data processing workflows.
- Hands-on experience managing complex AI/ML and data-driven projects involving data scientists, engineers, SMEs, and senior leadership.
- Experience translating functional objectives into actionable plans and ensuring seamless execution across cross-functional technical teams.

raw.title: Senior Asset Analyst, Supply Chain
raw.location: San Francisco, CA - US; Sunnyvale, CA - US; Bellevue, WA - US
raw.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

Crusoe is seeking a Senior Asset Analyst to own asset data integrity, reporting, and disposition across our AI cloud data center hardware fleet. You will keep records for GPU servers, networking, storage, and optics accurate across every system of record, build the reporting that Operations, Finance, and leadership rely on, and take end-to-end ownership of asset disposition as the program matures.



You will work alongside the Asset Manager and partner directly with Procurement, Fleet, Site Operations, Accounting, and Security. This role has real autonomy: you run your own workstream, and you automate the manual work instead of living with it.



This role will be fully onsite in any of our west coast offices: San Francisco, CA, Bellevue, WA, or Sunnyvale, CA.



What You Will Be Working On:

 - Data Integrity and Reconciliation: Audit and reconcile asset records across systems of record, resolve discrepancies, and establish one reliable source of truth.

 - Root Cause and Data Standards: Diagnose data gaps, close them at the source with upstream teams, and define required fields, standards, and validation rules.

 - Reporting and Dashboards: Build and maintain dashboards covering inventory position, deployment status, warranty coverage, and end-of-life exposure. Deliver recurring and ad hoc reporting for Operations, Finance, and leadership.

 - Finance and Planning Support: Provide asset data for budget planning and forecasting (spares, warranty renewals, refresh cycles) and support depreciation, audit, and compliance reporting with Accounting and Security.

 - Risk Flagging: Surface aging hardware, coverage gaps, and unaccounted assets before they become problems.

 - Asset Disposition (growing scope): Own disposition from identification through decommissioning handoff, vendor coordination, and closure. Maintain chain of custody and sanitization evidence, reconcile remarketing proceeds and credits, and manage disposal vendors and certificates of destruction.

 - Lifecycle Operations Support: Support assets from receiving through deployment, transfer, and decommissioning. Work with  suppliers on shipment data, part numbers, and warranty records.

 - Automation and Process: Automate recurring reconciliation and reporting with SQL, scripting, and AI tools. Write and maintain SOPs in Confluence as workflows evolve, and partner with cross-functional teams to put processes in place, gather feedback and refine them over time.

 - Systems Readiness: Support data validation and cutover when asset tooling and systems change.



What You Will Bring to the Team:

 - Experience: 5 to 7 years in data center operations, hardware asset management, inventory management, or a data-focused operations role.

 - Data Skills: Advanced Excel required. SQL strongly preferred.

 - Reconciliation: Proven experience reconciling data across multiple systems of record and resolving conflicting sources of truth.

 - Platforms: Hands-on experience with asset management, ITAM, ERP, or DCIM platforms.

 - Reporting: Experience building dashboards in a BI tool such as Sigma, Tableau, or Power BI.

 - Automation and AI: Active use of scripting or AI tools to remove manual work from your own workflow.

 - Ownership: Track record of running a workstream end to end with minimal direction in a fast-moving environment where process evolves alongside the fleet.

 - Communication: Clear communicator across engineering, finance, and operations, with the written skill to turn a process into documentation someone else can follow.



Bonus Points:

 - Hands-on familiarity with data center hardware: servers, GPUs, storage, networking, PDUs, and CDUs.

 - Experience with hardware disposition, remarketing, or e-waste vendor management.

 - Exposure to procurement systems, purchase order workflows, or fixed asset accounting and depreciation.

 - Experience supporting budget planning, forecasting, or capital expenditure processes.

 - Familiarity with hardware lifecycle concepts: EOL, RMA, warranty management, and secure data sanitization.

 - Experience in hyperscale or cloud infrastructure environments.

 - Professional certification such as CHAMP, CSAM, or ITIL.



Benefits:

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $110,000 - $135,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

- Identify opportunities for automation and workflow simplification.
- Contribute to adoption and enhancement of SAP IBP capabilities.

Job Profile Summary
- Leads day-to-day execution of Field Readiness Enablement, ensuring field service organizations are prepared to support new product introductions (NPI) and technology ramps. Coordinates readiness across training, field service organization (FSO) capacity, capability development, technical documentation, and spare parts so that critical support elements are in place before product release or ramp milestones.

- Readiness Planning: Ensures that readiness objectives, milestones, and sign-off criteria are defined for each assigned product ramp or NPI, and that preliminary activities (e.g., forecast review, resource demand planning, training and documentation planning) begin at forecast notification rather than at shipment, allowing for effective execution at install.
- Training Readiness: Coordinates training readiness plans for new products, upgrades, and technology releases; ensures training materials and certification paths are available and aligned with engineering releases; tracks training completion and certification status.
- Capacity Planning: Supports assessment of current and future customer engineer (CE) resource requirements based on business forecasts and customer demand; maintains capacity models and headcount gap analyses; partners with management on hiring, onboarding, and deployment strategies.
- Capability Development: Tracks technical competency levels and capability gaps for new technologies and products; supports development plans, certification programs, and readiness scorecards that increase workforce flexibility.
- Documentation Readiness: Ensures service procedures, troubleshooting guides, maintenance and installation documentation, and knowledge base articles are released and available before ramp; facilitates documentation readiness reviews and checklists.
- Spares Readiness: Collaborates with Regional Planning and Global Product Support to define spare parts requirements, recommended and targeted stocking levels, and stocking strategies; monitors spares readiness.
- Governance & Reporting: Coordinates readiness reviews and governance meetings; keeps readiness status visible in dashboards and trackers; escalates risks with owners and mitigation plans; prepares readiness status reporting for leadership.
- Documentation & Compliance: Ensures readiness execution is documented and information required by other functions is reported or transferred as appropriate; ensures compliance with Company policies regarding confidentiality, data privacy, and safety.
- Continuous Improvement: Captures post-install feedback on training gaps, documentation issues, and execution challenges, and incorporates lessons learned into standard readiness processes for the next cycle

- Bachelor's Degree – Business Administration, Logistics Management, Operations Management, Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Computer Science, or related field

Overview
MCAPS-Core accelerates customer outcomes and business growth. By uniting product, engineering, marketing, sales, customer success, and partners around a common customer mission, we help customers realize value faster and turn innovation into measurable business impact. Through deep technical expertise and differentiated go-to-market execution, we win competitively, capture market share, and scale repeatable growth motions. We differentiate through value creation - delivering world-class, AI-powered customer experiences that accelerate adoption, strengthen loyalty, and create sustainable competitive advantage, driving growth that outpaces the market.

Within MCAPS - Core, the Customer Service & Support (CSS) organization builds trust and confidence for every person and organization through delivering a seamless support experience. In CSS, we are powered by Microsoft’s AI technology to help consumers, businesses, partners, and more, resolve their issues quickly and securely, helping prevent future problems from occurring and achieving more from their Microsoft investment.

To ensure customers can expand their consumption of Microsoft cloud services without any constraints, we established a specialized program that gathers customer-based intelligence in coordination with Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Engineering teams. This Technical Program Manager/Sr Technical Program Manager role, housed within the Worldwide MCAPs Team, works to develop strong ties with field and Customer Success Account Managment (CSAM) leadership and a broad network of contacts focused on solving capacity-related challenges. This two-way exchange of information enables us to develop an early deal pipeline and more effectively plan resource-specific capacity that shapes our cloud data center growth strategy for each region.

We’re now seeking to hire a talented program manager based in the Puget Sound, to support the Americas. This role reports to the Global Director of Business Programs QEI and Insights Excellence and will partner closely with subsidiary leadership teams (Area Vice President and LT, Business Group Leads, Technical advisers, etc.) across the United States, Canada, and Latin America. The role will help Microsoft align cross-company sales initiatives, cloud capacity expansion, deal orchestration, revenue performance, and gross margin targets to our capacity plans.  More importantly, this role will help us plan for and enable some of our most important Customer solutions through strong partnerships and cloud co-planning efforts.  We’re encouraging a diverse cross-section of individuals with cloud sales, engineering/capacity planning, and program management experience to apply!

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Responsibilities
- Work closely with cross organizational teams, including analysis of the opportunity pipeline to develop leading indicators that predict business opportunities and expansion challenges with accuracy. Act as a capacity ‘Account Manager’ for all regional capacity opportunities and challenges.
- Become a trusted advisor to regional leadership teams for infrastructure planning, execution, and resolution of capacity-related issues.
- Synthesize key feedback from customers, partners, and field to HQ with the goal of identifying sales blockers and best practice process improvements to enhance worldwide selling capability and efficiency.
- Develop regular RoB customer engagements for Microsoft’s Strategic Customers and Partners.
- Communicate progress, isolate key challenges and opportunities, and accelerate decision making.
- Assist with Resiliency architecture and long term planning strategy around capacity.

Qualifications

raw.title: Demand & Supply Planning Manager
raw.location: San Francisco Office (Fremont St); San Jose Office (Zanker); Remote
raw.description:
Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.



If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.



Note: This position requires presence in our San Francisco or San Jose office location 4 days per week; Lambda's designated work from home day is currently Tuesday.


About the Role

We are seeking experienced Demand & Supply Planning Managers to help build a brand-new planning function for Lambda's data center hardware, as part of Lambda's Supply Chain team, which makes sure the right systems, racks, and networking equipment are in the right place at the right time to power our rapidly growing AI cloud footprint.

You will own the planning process that connects what our customers and data center deployments need with what our ODM/OEM partners and component suppliers can deliver: building and maintaining demand forecasts, translating them into supply and build plans, balancing capacity and inventory against deployment schedules, and surfacing constraints early enough for the business to act on them.

The ideal candidate has planned complex, long-lead-time hardware in a high-growth environment. You are comfortable pressure-testing a forecast, building a supply plan from the bill of materials up, running a rigorous S&OP cycle, and telling leadership clearly where the risks are and what trade-offs are on the table, while moving fluidly between strategic planning and the details that make or break a deployment.

Because this is a net-new team, you will have a real hand in defining how planning works at Lambda: the processes, the cadence, the metrics, and the tools. You will work closely with Sourcing (ODM/OEM), Commodity Management, Operations and Logistics, Data Center Engineering, Finance, and Go-to-Market to bring capacity online on schedule.


What You'll Do

Demand Planning & Forecasting

 - Own the demand forecast for your assigned portfolio, translating data center deployment plans, customer commitments, and capacity roadmaps into a unit-level, time-phased view of what we need and when.

 - Build and maintain forecast models, assumptions, and scenarios (base, upside, downside), and track forecast accuracy and bias over time.

 - Partner with Go-to-Market, Project Management, Finance, and Data Center Engineering to keep the demand signal current as customer commitments, cluster designs, and site readiness change.

 - Establish clear forecast input ownership, cadence, and change-control so that upstream changes are visible and acted on quickly.

Supply Planning & Capacity Alignment

 - Convert demand into supply and build plans for finished systems, racks, and networking equipment, including ODM/OEM build slots, integration capacity, and delivery schedules.

 - Align partner manufacturing capacity and lead times with the demand forecast, and drive resolution when supply and demand do not match.

 - Work with Commodity Management to understand component availability and allocation (accelerators, memory, storage, optics, power, cooling) and reflect those constraints in the supply plan.

 - Lead execution timing across the supply chain, setting and driving the schedule so that material procurement is placed and delivered on time to support build and deployment commitments.

 - Plan for new platform introductions and transitions, coordinating build schedules, ramp timing, and cutover so that new and legacy platforms are supplied without gaps or excess.

 - Coordinate with Operations and Logistics on inbound flow, staging, and delivery so that supply lands when data centers are ready to receive it, either through direct ship or hub-spoke delivery models.

Integrated Planning (S&OP)

 - Run or contribute to the Sales & Operations Planning cycle for infrastructure: demand review, supply review, and executive alignment on trade-offs.

 - Produce clear, decision-ready views of supply versus demand, gaps, risks, and recommended actions for leadership.

 - Drive consensus across functions, and escalate constraints with options and a recommendation, not just a problem statement.

 - Keep the plan of record accurate, and make plan changes and their downstream impacts transparent.

Inventory & Working Capital

 - Leverage analytical models to define and manage inventory targets, buffer strategies, and safety stock for long-lead and critical items, balancing deployment risk against capital and obsolescence exposure.

 - Monitor on-hand, in-transit, and committed inventory, and flag excess, shortage, and aging exposure early.

Supply Risk & Resilience

Identify, quantify, and help mitigate risks to deployment schedules, including:

 - Lead-time changes and long-lead component exposure

 - Manufacturing capacity constraints and build slot risk

 - Component allocation and shortages

 - Single points of failure across partners, sites, and regions

 - Tariff, trade compliance, and geopolitical impacts on flow and timing

 - Demand volatility and forecast error

 - Build contingency and recovery plans, and run scenario analysis so leadership can see the options before a constraint becomes a delay.

Planning Processes, Data & Tools

 - Help design and stand up the planning processes, cadence, and governance for a new team.

 - Define and report the metrics that matter, such as forecast accuracy, plan adherence, days of supply, inventory turns, on-time delivery, and shortage exposure.

 - Build the data foundation and reporting needed to plan at scale, and contribute to selecting and implementing planning systems and automation.

 - Document processes and playbooks so the function scales as Lambda grows.

Cross-Functional Partnership

 - Partner with Sourcing (ODM/OEM) so commercial commitments, capacity reservations, and ramp terms line up with the plan.

 - Partner with Commodity Management on component supply, allocation, and long-lead procurement.

 - Partner with Operations and Logistics on inbound execution, delivery timing, and exceptions, as tactical execution increasingly sits with Operations over time.

 - Partner with Hardware, Network, and Data Center Engineering on platform roadmaps, site readiness, and configuration changes that affect supply.

 - Partner with Finance on capex forecasting, inventory reserves, and the cost impact of planning decisions, and to understand commitment, cash flow, and liability curves that inform top-line financial reporting.

 - Provide leadership with market insight, risk visibility, and clear recommendations on supply, cost, and timing trade-offs.

You

 - 8+ years of experience in Demand Planning, Supply Planning, S&OP, Supply Chain, or Materials Planning for hardware and direct experience planning at the system, rack, or complex-assembly level (compute, storage, networking, or integrated hardware platforms).

 - Demonstrated experience building demand forecasts and translating them into supply, build, and inventory plans in a long-lead-time, supply-constrained environment.

 - Strong understanding of BOM structures, lead times, and how component constraints flow through to finished-goods availability.

 - Experience working with ODMs, OEMs, or contract manufacturers on capacity, build schedules, and ramp planning.

 - Hands-on experience running or contributing to S&OP or an equivalent integrated planning process.

 - Strong analytical and financial acumen, with the ability to combine mathematical models and advanced spreadsheet skills, such as statistical forecasting, inventory and safety stock optimization, and scenario modeling, to produce outputs in a structured, scalable, and repeatable manner, and comfort working with large datasets.

 - Experience with ERP and planning systems and a track record of improving planning processes and tooling.

 - Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, drive alignment across functions, and communicate risk and trade-offs clearly.

 - Comfort operating with a high degree of ownership in a fast-growth, ambiguity-rich environment, including building processes from scratch.

Nice to Have

 - Experience supporting hyperscale data center or AI infrastructure build programs.

 - Experience planning through new product introductions, platform transitions, and rapid capacity ramps.

 - Experience managing allocation and shortage scenarios for constrained components such as accelerators, memory, optics, power, and cooling.

 - Familiarity with the ODM/OEM ecosystem and how build and supply models (turnkey, consigned, disaggregated) affect planning.

 - Experience implementing or scaling planning tools and platforms, and working fluency in SQL, Python, or BI tools.

 - APICS/ASCM certification (CPIM, CSCP) or equivalent.

 - Willingness to travel domestically and internationally as needed.

 - Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or related field; advanced degree a plus.

For the ODM Racks role:

 - Experience planning AI/ML compute systems, GPU servers, or accelerated computing platforms at scale.

 - Experience planning finished racks and systems with ODM partners, including build slot, integration capacity, and ramp planning.

 - Experience with liquid-cooled and high-power rack architectures and cluster-level deployment models, including the power and cooling infrastructure that gates them.

For the Network Hardware Equipment role:

 - Experience planning data center switching, routing, or high-speed fabric hardware at scale, including scale-up and scale-out AI fabrics.

 - Familiarity with optical transceiver and cable supply markets (400G/800G and beyond, DAC/AOC, structured cabling) and their distinct lead-time and allocation dynamics.

 - Experience planning network equipment deployments alongside compute and storage so that clusters are delivered complete.

For the Critical Rack Commodity Planning role:

 - Experience planning long-lead, allocation-constrained components such as accelerators, memory, storage, power, or cooling.

 - Experience with BOM explosion and managing component-level supply and demand, including allocation, buffer strategy, and shortage mitigation, and connecting it to finished-goods build plans.

 - Experience working with commodity or component sourcing teams to align procurement commitments with the demand forecast.

We Are Looking for Someone Who Is:

 - Analytical and commercially minded, able to move between a detailed forecast model and an executive conversation about trade-offs

 - Data-driven, decisive, and execution-oriented

 - Comfortable with leveraging AI tools in everyday workflows

 - A clear communicator and strong collaborator who builds trust with partners and internal stakeholders

 - Comfortable building process and structure in a fast-growth, ambiguity-rich environment

 - Proactive at finding risk early and bringing options, not just problems

Salary Range Information

The annual salary range for this position has been set based on market data and other factors. However, a salary higher or lower than this range may be appropriate for a candidate whose qualifications differ meaningfully from those listed in the job description.




About Lambda

 - Founded in 2012, with 500+ employees, and growing fast

 - Our investors notably include TWG Global, US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Andra Capital, SGW, Andrej Karpathy, ARK Invest, Fincadia Advisors, G Squared, In-Q-Tel (IQT), KHK & Partners, NVIDIA, Pegatron, Supermicro, Wistron, Wiwynn, Gradient Ventures, Mercato Partners, SVB, 1517, and Crescent Cove

 - We have research papers accepted at top machine learning and graphics conferences, including NeurIPS, ICCV, SIGGRAPH, and TOG

 - Our values are publicly available: https://lambda.ai/careers

 - We offer generous cash & equity compensation

 - Health, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents

 - Wellness and commuter stipends for select roles

 - 401k Plan with 2% company match (USA employees)

 - Flexible paid time off plan that we all actually use

We will do this primarily by building software and mathematical optimization models, not manual planning. The team is uniquely positioned to develop and optimize these capacity plans and scalably manage exceptions at the most strategic levels with company level impact.

This role is cross-functional and provides an opportunity to work with a variety of engineering and business teams to power the rapid growth of Meta’s products. This role will help to ensure optimal deployment and operation of our infrastructure from both a cost and technology perspective, with millions of servers, gigawatts of data center capacity, and cutting-edge technology, including advanced artificial intelligence.

raw.description:
ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE: You will serve as the technical program leader for large-scale compute clusters across their full lifecycle. That spans bring-up and delivery through sustained operation and administration. You will lead the engineering and operations teams that deliver clusters on schedule, then keep them healthy, available, and efficiently utilized in production. You will drive the processes and execution rhythms that turn build plans into operational environments, and the discipline that keeps them running. Success requires strong analytical, problem-solving, and risk-management skills. You must also build effective relationships and drive alignment across a complex, fast-moving engineering organization. You must be self-directed and comfortable operating in dynamic environments with cross-functional dependencies and live production constraints. THE PERSON: As the Cluster Build and Operations Program Manager, you are the accountable leader for the cluster from concept through delivery and into steady-state service. You partner with engineering teams to define build strategies, assess technical feasibility, sequence dependencies, and drive execution against program objectives. Once clusters are live, you own the operating model and the escalation paths that keep workloads running. When issues arise — during bring-up or in production — you lead cross-functional triage, push investigations to root cause, and ensure resolution through closure. The ideal candidate has delivered and operated complex hardware and software programs, and thrives in matrixed organizations. That record includes predictable, on-time delivery and dependable day-to-day operation of business-critical infrastructure. This is a program leadership role rather than a hands-on engineering or site reliability position. You are accountable for the plan, the operating cadence, and the outcome, and you drive the specialist teams who perform the technical work. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Build and Delivery Lead cluster bring-up — from concept and planning through delivery and operational handoff. Direct and coordinate cross-functional teams across hardware, infrastructure, software, firmware, validation, and site/datacenter operations. Assess technical feasibility with software and hardware architects, technical leads, and engineering teams, clarifying requirements and dependencies. Develop integrated program schedules covering hardware, firmware, software, infrastructure, and bring-up dependencies, and align milestones to delivery objectives. Lead bring-up debug by triaging blockers, convening subject-matter experts, and driving fixes to closure before production handoff. Build, maintain, and execute program plans, including plans of record (the agreed baseline), statements of work, schedules, scope, budgets, and key performance indicators (KPIs). Define and enforce the acceptance criteria and exit gates a cluster must meet before it is released from bring-up into production service. Operations Own cluster availability and utilization targets in production, report performance against them, and hold the responsible engineering and operations teams accountable. Establish and run the operating cadence for the fleet, including maintenance windows, change management, firmware and software update campaigns, and scheduled downtime planning. Establish and manage on-call rotation and escalation coverage, including hand-off procedures, severity definitions, and response-time expectations. Lead production issue response, run post-incident reviews, and track preventive actions to closure. Partner with datacenter and site operations on power, cooling, cabling, spares, Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) flow, and field service. Direct capacity planning and lifecycle management across the fleet — expansion, re-provisioning, hardware refresh, and decommission. Define the monitoring and reporting leadership needs to manage the fleet, and work with engineering to close gaps. Administration Oversee cluster administration, including workload scheduling and queue policy, node and partition configuration, image and software stack management, and onboarding of new user teams. Govern access, entitlement, and quota management across teams and workloads, in partnership with security and IT. Establish and maintain the runbooks, standard operating procedures, and operational documentation that make cluster administration repeatable and transferable. Define and track support expectations for cluster users, and manage the intake and prioritization of user-facing operational requests. Across the Lifecycle Provide clear executive and operational visibility into build status and fleet health while facilitating dependency management and communication across teams. Anticipate risks throughout the lifecycle, identify mitigation strategies, and proactively address issues to protect schedules, availability, and engineering resources. Partner with core and execution teams to identify areas needing escalation, and see them resolved. Collect, analyze, organize, and publish build and operational performance data through dashboards, metrics, and recurring status reviews. Drive continuous improvement of build, operations, and administration processes, tools, and automation to increase throughput, repeatability, and operational efficiency. Work effectively with senior leaders across Engineering, Product Management, Customer Engineering, IT, and Program Management to align on priorities, risks, and objectives. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience with artificial intelligence (AI) and high performance computing (HPC) cluster builds, and with programs that carry clusters into sustained production operation. Working familiarity with cluster administration — workload schedulers such as Slurm or Kubernetes, node provisioning and imaging, fabric and interconnect health, and fleet monitoring. Depth sufficient to lead technical discussions and judge trade-offs, not to administer the cluster directly. Experience establishing or managing operational disciplines such as incident and change management, maintenance planning, on-call coverage, and post-incident review. Detail-oriented and self-motivated, with a strong sense of accountability and pride in delivering results through cross-functional teams. Proven ability to lead and coordinate cross-functional technical teams through complex, multi-stage cluster bring-up, integration, or infrastructure deployment efforts. Comfortable leading technical debug discussions and guiding engineering teams to root cause. Ability to quickly grasp technical concepts and convert meeting discussions into clear, actionable outcomes. Excellent organizational, analytical, problem-solving, presentation, written, and verbal communication skills. Results-oriented and highly organized, able to manage multiple priorities without losing momentum. Builds productive relationships across organizations and operates as a self-starter. Strong executive communication skills, including program reviews, status reporting, and escalation management. Strong proficiency with project and productivity tools, including Microsoft Project, Jira, Confluence, and Microsoft Office Suite applications. Success requires strong analytical, problem-solving, and risk-management skills. You must also build effective relationships and drive alignment across a complex, fast-moving engineering organization. You must be self-directed and comfortable operating in dynamic environments with cross-functional dependencies and live production constraints. THE PERSON: As the Cluster Build and Operations Program Manager, you are the accountable leader for the cluster from concept through delivery and into steady-state service. You partner with engineering teams to define build strategies, assess technical feasibility, sequence dependencies, and drive execution against program objectives. Once clusters are live, you own the operating model and the escalation paths that keep workloads running. When issues arise — during bring-up or in production — you lead cross-functional triage, push investigations to root cause, and ensure resolution through closure. The ideal candidate has delivered and operated complex hardware and software programs, and thrives in matrixed organizations. That record includes predictable, on-time delivery and dependable day-to-day operation of business-critical infrastructure. This is a program leadership role rather than a hands-on engineering or site reliability position. You are accountable for the plan, the operating cadence, and the outcome, and you drive the specialist teams who perform the technical work. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Build and Delivery Lead cluster bring-up — from concept and planning through delivery and operational handoff. Direct and coordinate cross-functional teams across hardware, infrastructure, software, firmware, validation, and site/datacenter operations. Assess technical feasibility with software and hardware architects, technical leads, and engineering teams, clarifying requirements and dependencies. Develop integrated program schedules covering hardware, firmware, software, infrastructure, and bring-up dependencies, and align milestones to delivery objectives. Lead bring-up debug by triaging blockers, convening subject-matter experts, and driving fixes to closure before production handoff. Build, maintain, and execute program plans, including plans of record (the agreed baseline), statements of work, schedules, scope, budgets, and key performance indicators (KPIs). Define and enforce the acceptance criteria and exit gates a cluster must meet before it is released from bring-up into production service. Operations Own cluster availability and utilization targets in production, report performance against them, and hold the responsible engineering and operations teams accountable. Establish and run the operating cadence for the fleet, including maintenance windows, change management, firmware and software update campaigns, and scheduled downtime planning. Establish and manage on-call rotation and escalation coverage, including hand-off procedures, severity definitions, and response-time expectations. Lead production issue response, run post-incident reviews, and track preventive actions to closure. Partner with datacenter and site operations on power, cooling, cabling, spares, Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) flow, and field service. Direct capacity planning and lifecycle management across the fleet — expansion, re-provisioning, hardware refresh, and decommission. Define the monitoring and reporting leadership needs to manage the fleet, and work with engineering to close gaps. Administration Oversee cluster administration, including workload scheduling and queue policy, node and partition configuration, image and software stack management, and onboarding of new user teams. Govern access, entitlement, and quota management across teams and workloads, in partnership with security and IT. Establish and maintain the runbooks, standard operating procedures, and operational documentation that make cluster administration repeatable and transferable. Define and track support expectations for cluster users, and manage the intake and prioritization of user-facing operational requests. Across the Lifecycle Provide clear executive and operational visibility into build status and fleet health while facilitating dependency management and communication across teams. Anticipate risks throughout the lifecycle, identify mitigation strategies, and proactively address issues to protect schedules, availability, and engineering resources. Partner with core and execution teams to identify areas needing escalation, and see them resolved. Collect, analyze, organize, and publish build and operational performance data through dashboards, metrics, and recurring status reviews. Drive continuous improvement of build, operations, and administration processes, tools, and automation to increase throughput, repeatability, and operational efficiency. Work effectively with senior leaders across Engineering, Product Management, Customer Engineering, IT, and Program Management to align on priorities, risks, and objectives. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience with artificial intelligence (AI) and high performance computing (HPC) cluster builds, and with programs that carry clusters into sustained production operation. Working familiarity with cluster administration — workload schedulers such as Slurm or Kubernetes, node provisioning and imaging, fabric and interconnect health, and fleet monitoring. Depth sufficient to lead technical discussions and judge trade-offs, not to administer the cluster directly. Experience establishing or managing operational disciplines such as incident and change management, maintenance planning, on-call coverage, and post-incident review. Detail-oriented and self-motivated, with a strong sense of accountability and pride in delivering results through cross-functional teams. Proven ability to lead and coordinate cross-functional technical teams through complex, multi-stage cluster bring-up, integration, or infrastructure deployment efforts. Comfortable leading technical debug discussions and guiding engineering teams to root cause. Ability to quickly grasp technical concepts and convert meeting discussions into clear, actionable outcomes. Excellent organizational, analytical, problem-solving, presentation, written, and verbal communication skills. Results-oriented and highly organized, able to manage multiple priorities without losing momentum. Builds productive relationships across organizations and operates as a self-starter. Demonstrated horizontal leadership and matrix-management experience, with the ability to drive execution without direct authority. Strong executive communication skills, including program reviews, status reporting, and escalation management. Demonstrated ability to solve complex cross-organizational problems and mitigate risk at program scale. People-management experience is desirable. Experience in Agile development environments. Strong proficiency with project and productivity tools, including Microsoft Project, Jira, Confluence, and Microsoft Office Suite applications. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience). Formal project management education and Project Management Professional (PMP), Scrum Master, or equivalent certification/training. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

The Meta Hardware Design and Release to Production (Hardware Design and Release to Production) team ensures that the hardware running in Meta's production fleet is stable, secure, performant, and delivers the most value. Within this organization, the Release to Production New Product Introduction (Release to Production NPI) team finds, debugs, and remediates hardware failure modes before certifying new platforms for mass production, and then sustains them across the deployed lifecycle.

We are looking for an Optical Engineer to drive optics validation within Release to Production NPI — pairing deep optical-transceiver expertise with Python scripting skills to automate the testing that qualifies optical communications modules and to lead optical transceiver NPI programs end to end. In this role, you will develop optics test automation using Python scripts, drive hands-on NPI execution with vendors and ODMs through EVT/DVT/PVT to mass production, and contribute to optical networking standards and engage with ecosystem partners.

Develop and maintain Python scripts and test automation for qualification of optical transceivers and subsystems across EVT, DVT, PVT, and characterization, using the team's existing test frameworks, instrument drivers, switch and host abstractions, and results pipelines
Lead optics NPI programs end to end, working closely with optics vendors and ODMs from RFI / RFP through EVT / DVT / PVT to mass production ramp and sustaining
Find, debug, and remediate optical hardware failure modes before certifying modules for mass production; drive root-cause analysis and corrective action with vendors and ODMs

Ensure new optical platforms are supported by production and fleet health tooling, and contribute to production-readiness documentation, including production-readiness review documentation, best-known configuration guides, and design-for-test specifications

Provide sustaining support after deployment — validate stability, security, and performance under production workloads, and refine understanding of failure characteristics at scale
Contribute to engineering standards for test automation — code review, version control, documentation — and mentor engineers and technicians on Python scripting best practices and optical test methods
Collaborate across Software, Thermal, Mechanical, Electrical Engineering, Signal Integrity, TPM, and Production Engineering teams to integrate optics into systems
Interface with the industry, contribute to the RFI / RFP process, and shape product requirements, test plans, and data sheets

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, a relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience

Experience in creating or influencing product requirement documents, test plans, and data sheets

Experience with optical integration, including InP PICs, silicon-photonic PICs, PIC-IC integration, and 3D optical packaging technologies

Track record of mentoring engineers, improving engineering standards and practices for test automation quality, and influencing without direct authority

- Mentor team members by sharing knowledge and best practices to elevate the overall functional capabilities of the team.

- Collaborate across the matrix organization and influence decisions affecting sourcing strategy, supply chain risk, and material cost.

- Develop and implement effective supply chain strategies—from NPI through High Volume—that meet performance requirements and enable the Business Unit’s product strategy.

- Lead high‑value, complex negotiations with key suppliers to ensure a reliable and cost‑effective supply of materials and components.

- Extensive knowledge of various fabrication commodities and processes.

- Demonstrated experience in cost negotiation and driving cost‑reduction plans.

Reporting, Dashboards & Automation: Build and operationalize executive reporting — status dashboards, utilization and issue metrics, and pipeline views in Power BI, SharePoint, and internal CSP systems — eliminating manual consolidation and replacing spreadsheet sprawl with automated, governed data flows. Stakeholder & Executive Communication: Serve as the primary program contact across Engineering, Business Development, Product Management, Supply Chain, Operations, and IT; run status reviews, drive cross-functional decisions, and present progress, risks, and tradeoffs to senior leadership and customers with precision and clarity. Governance & Process Improvement: Establish and sustain consistent program governance — intake, prioritization, planning, change management, reporting cadence, and escalation paths — across Waterfall, Agile, and hybrid delivery models, and continuously improve the process through automation and analytics. Risk Management: Proactively identify risks, execution gaps, and systemic bottlenecks across supply, schedule, technical readiness, and partner performance; build and drive mitigation and recovery plans. AI-Enabled Productivity: Identify, promote, and adopt practical AI and AI-powered program management tooling to draw program insights, improve productivity, simplify processes, and increase execution velocity. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Multiple and recent years of progressive program management experience leading complex, large-scale, multi-site technology programs end-to-end in a matrixed organization. Direct experience with data center, cloud service provider, or large-scale infrastructure deployment programs — site readiness, power and energization, rack build and validation, deployment, and sustaining operations. Demonstrated ability to manage delivery plans, schedules, resource needs, risks, dependencies, budgets, and stakeholder communications across many concurrent workstreams. Experience managing OEM/ODM, hyperscaler, and CSP partner relationships, including acceptance criteria, handover, and escalation management. Strong data and reporting skills — building standardized data models, executive dashboards, and metrics; hands-on experience with Power BI, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and program tracking systems (MS Project, Jira, or equivalent). Thrives in “responsibility without line authority” leadership; able to build relationships, network across functions and levels, and drive effective decision-making without direct reports. Ability to structure and execute complex analysis, draw insights, and communicate summary findings and recommendations to senior management and AMD customers. Strong understanding of project delivery life cycles, including Waterfall, Agile, and hybrid approaches. Precise, direct communication tailored to the audience. Ability to identify, promote, and evangelize practical AI opportunities that improve productivity and support responsible adoption across teams and stakeholders. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.. raw.title: Senior Technical Program Manager - Data Center Infrastructure Delivery
raw.description:
Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.



If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.





Role Overview

Lambda is seeking a Technical Program Manager (TPM) to own the integrated delivery program for new data center builds, from the handoff of a selected site by Real Estate through construction, commissioning, operational readiness, and turnover to Network Deployment. You will be the single source of truth for milestones, risks, and dependencies on your sites, leading internal teams and external partners (GCs, design firms, utilities, and vendors) across site work, utilities, shell, MEP, controls, white space, inspections, and commissioning.

Ambiguity is high, timelines are compressed, and the stakes are central to company growth. As we scale beyond our first sites, you will help build the playbooks and governance that let us run many concurrent deployments well.


What You’ll Do

 - Own the integrated schedule from site handoff to Operations; break builds into workstreams with clear owners and milestones, and actively manage the critical path and schedule compression.

 - Drive the delivery sequence from rack requirements to engineering criteria, design, plan set, permitting, construction, commissioning, and turnover for MW-scale, high-density (including liquid-cooled) capacity.

 - Lead cross-functional execution with Real Estate (site assumptions, fiber, permit path), Energy and Utilities (interconnection, substation, power delivery), Engineering (requirements in the design and plan set), Procurement (long-lead equipment), Construction Management (GC schedule, field progress, inspections), Commissioning (test plans, acceptance), Operations (staffing, procedures, access), and Security, and Finance (requirements, budget, CapEx), and Legal.

 - Manage risk and governance: maintain risk registers, dependency logs, decision trackers, and schedule variance reports; surface permitting, utility, design, procurement, sequencing, and commissioning risks early.

 - Escalate with facts: status, baseline vs. forecast date, variance, impact, owner, mitigation options, and decision date. Lead schedule recovery when milestones slip.

 - Hold partners accountable to contractual milestones, production and shipping schedules, and commercial commitments while maintaining productive relationships.

 - Communicate to leadership through program reviews and concise, high-signal status updates.

 - Deliver clean turnover: define handover criteria and ensure white space, power, cooling, controls, cable pathways, access, and documentation are ready for Network Deployment.

 - Scale the function: build repeatable playbooks, dashboards, and lessons-learned loops across concurrent deployments.

 - Travel (~40%) to sites to validate progress and build partner relationships.

Scope of Ownership

 - Owns: site-level delivery program management; the integrated schedule; cross-functional coordination; milestone, risk, dependency, and decision tracking; variance reporting and escalation; Operations readiness.

 - Partners on, but does not own: site selection and real estate; engineering design authority; construction means and methods and GC management; commissioning authority; procurement commercial strategy; network and services deployment; steady-state operations.

You

 - Have 7+ years in data center delivery, infrastructure or construction program management, mission-critical facilities, or large capital projects.

 - Have delivered ground-up data centers or comparable mission-critical, industrial, semiconductor, or energy facilities, ideally multi-site on compressed timelines.

raw.title: Data Engineer , AWS Infrastructure Supply Chain Intelligence
raw.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
  
  
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.  
  
We are looking for a talented Data Engineer to join the Manufacturing Operations, Transportation Operations, and Reverse (MOTOR) organization in support of our Supply Chain Intelligence team. MOTOR manages the manufacturing of datacenter racks and the movement of racks/parts through the supply chain, consisting of transportation, warehousing, and reverse logistics into and out of the data centers. This role performs helps connect the different systems across the supply chain together so operational teams have clean, actionable data to work with. This requires someone with strong analytic skills and business acumen who can work with stakeholders on strategic projects across MOTOR.
  
  
The ideal candidate relishes working with large volumes of data, enjoys the challenge of highly complex technical contexts, and, above all else, is passionate about data and analytics. Must be an expert working with data modeling with un/structured data, ingestion pipelines and ETL design and business intelligence tools with the business to identify strategic opportunities where improvements in data infrastructure creates out-sized business impact. Candidate is a self-starter, comfortable with ambiguity, able to think big (while paying careful attention to detail), mentors other engineers in team on high quality tech, and enjoys working in a fast-paced team. Candidate will have a chance to architect the data pipelines needed for optimization and predictive analysis. We're excited to talk to those up to the challenge!  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Build and maintain the infrastructure to answer questions with data, using software engineering best practices, data management fundamentals, data storage principles, recent advances in distributed systems, and operational excellence best practices. Build datasets that analysts and scientists use to generate actionable insights.
* Define the data engineering processes that leverage various AWS services to improve accessibility, redundancy, data integrity, cost, and storage requirements.
* Develop high quality solutions for the faster development of the products/models that solve the business needs in a scalable format, while also anticipating future requirements.
* Collaborate with Research/Applied Scientists, Data Engineers, Business Intelligence Engineers, Data Scientists, Business Analysts, and Product/Program Managers to understand the business and technical requirements, and make decisions that help make the products/programs smoother.
* Interface with other technology/data engineering teams to extract, transform, and load data from a wide variety of data sources using and AWS data technologies.
* Lead the technical design and implementation of the data infrastructure.
* Design and manage data audit, quality, and reconciliation processes in collaboration with various stakeholders.

  
About the team  
This team provides data engineering and business intelligence engineering services to the rest of MOTOR. We are the data experts behind the scenes helping the operational teams focus on operations by ensuring they have accurate, timely data and provide business insights to help improve operational excellence.  
  
\*Why AWS\*  
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.  
  
\*Diverse Experiences\*  
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.  
  
\*Work/Life Balance\*  
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.  
  
\*Inclusive Team Culture\*  
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.  
  
\*Mentorship and Career Growth\*  
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* 3+ years of data engineering experience
* 1+ years of developing and operating large-scale data structures for business intelligence analytics using ETL/ELT processes experience
* 1+ years of SQL (Structured Query Language) experience
* Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Mathematics, or a related field
* Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines
* Experience in at least one modern scripting or programming language, such as Python, Java, Scala, or NodeJS

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* Experience with AWS technologies like Redshift, S3, AWS Glue, EMR, Kinesis, FireHose, Lambda, and IAM roles and permissions
* Experience with non-relational databases / data stores (object storage, document or key-value stores, graph databases, column-family databases)

  
Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.  
  
Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

The positions will support the Supply Chain group in strategic planning, long-term supplier selection and negotiations. This position requires the ability to work with procurement, engineering, finance and legal teams and third parties such as suppliers. Domain Areas and Key Responsibilities – Collaborate and support in the development and rollout of various business solutions within the following areas:

- Demand & Material Planning – Support enhancement and optimization of our MRP system inputs/outputs/engine-logic and integration into all ERP modules, develop analytics/dashboards. Identifying material gaps and supplier risk, aid the configuration team with BOM errors, sparing contract requirements and SC master data requirements, support the Program team with right-to-left planning and supply chain milestone checkoff procedures.

- Procurement – Optimize an RFQ system and upstream data flows into the Supply Chain landscape. Develop tools to support multi-tier quoting, advanced sourcing, enhanced Supplier Collaboration and Interaction. Build Sourcing & Cost Trajectory analyses and insight tools.

- Logistics, Warehouse & Supplier Quality – Optimize WMS/QMS systems and associated integrated processes to enhance inventory accuracy and build readiness. Support compliance and sparing audits. Work with System teams with Inventory analytics for period-end/ad-hoc requests.

- Operational Scale & Supply Chain Health – Document Supply Chain processes (both for internal SMEs and external Supplier collaborators) and develop Doc change control and rollout procedures, support in developing a comprehensive Supplier Scorecard and integrate it into the Supplier Portal system landscape, develop a risk assessment supplier profile and health-check mechanism to enable scale and risk mitigation, aid the development of Compliance Requirements related to Federal and/or Industry-specific regulations and guidelines. Develop and Manage Supply Chain Onboarding material and checklists.

- Liaise between Business and IT groups to gather and clarify requirements, support sprint planning and end-user testing and training.

- Perform end-user application/system/process testing and report out.

- Support the effort to develop a global and comprehensive Supply Chain digital ecosystem pipeline and capability roadmap.

- Collaborate with Data team with data flow triage and issue-resolution intended to enable streamlined and accurate analytics.

- Develop a strong familiarity with the Supply Chain end-user base and their data and system usage and feedback to gather enhancement requirements for ad-hoc problem solving and building into the overall roadmap.
