raw.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Cloud Infrastructure
Senior Product Operations Engineer, Space
raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Space team is dedicated to expanding our AI-powered capabilities into the final frontier, enhancing Space Domain Awareness, Space Control, and Command and Control for U.S. military and allied partners. We're developing fully integrated hardware and software systems, including Lattice for Space Missions and modular payloads, to address growing threats in space and ensure our Guardians maintain a decisive advantage in this contested warfighting domain.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Senior Product Operations Engineer to join our Space team in Costa Mesa, CA someone who brings deep technical credibility and the leadership presence to match. This is not a management role, but it is a senior one: you'll be a technical anchor on a tight-knit team, the kind of engineer others look to when something breaks, when architecture decisions need to be made, and when the room needs someone who can cut through noise and drive clarity.

You will operate, maintain, harden, and evolve a classified networking capability that delivers operational Space Domain Awareness data for the United States Space Force. You'll own the reliability and security posture of globally distributed infrastructure in air-gapped environments standing up new sites, hardening systems to STIG compliance, building and maintaining infrastructure as code, and ensuring observability across the stack.

You'll work hand in hand with Mission Software Engineers, Product Operations teammates, Mission Operations Engineers, and Technical Program Managers to deploy new capabilities on operationally relevant timelines. You'll also be the connective tissue between engineering and the end-users at customer sites worldwide providing clear documentation, training remote staff, and serving as a first point of contact when issues arise.

This role is directly tied to an ongoing, funded program within Anduril’s Space Business Line. The program requires building and fielding a resilient, software-defined, distributed mesh networking layer for critical Space Domain Awareness data. We work with mission partners and operators to deploy reliable and robust capabilities on operationally-relevant fielding timelines to meet complex challenges across the DOD and IC.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Serve as a senior technical subject matter expert on a growing Product Operations team supporting a live, operational DoD system, helping set the standard for how the team operates, communicates, and solves problems

- Stand up, harden, and maintain classified Linux-based infrastructure across globally distributed sites in air-gapped environments

- Apply and enforce STIG compliance and system hardening standards across all deployed environments this is not checkbox work, you will own the security posture

- Build, maintain, and evolve infrastructure as code using Ansible/Puppet automating provisioning, configuration management, and deployment pipelines

- Write and maintain operational tooling, automation scripts, and workflow optimizations in Bash and Python

- Architect and maintain comprehensive observability across the stack using Splunk/ELK/Open Search logging, alerting, and tracing for distributed systems

- Manage and operate containerized workloads in Kubernetes at scale in production, classified environments

- Provide real-time incident response, rapid root-cause analysis, and resolution of complex issues spanning application code and backing infrastructure

- Collaborate cross-functionally with Software Engineering, Mission Ops, and TPMs to validate operational readiness of new deployments, features, and integrations

- Provide 24x7 on-call support as part of a team supporting the Space Domain Awareness mission on behalf of the United States Space Force

- Drive continuous improvement proactive automation, system optimization, and process refinement with minimal supervision and strong judgment on when to escalate

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Active U.S. Secret security clearance (non-negotiable must currently hold and be able to maintain- preferred TS/SCI clearance)

- 5+ years of hands-on experience with Kubernetes in production environments deploying, scaling, debugging, and managing containerized workloads. This is core to the role, not adjacent.

- Expert-level Linux proficiency you live in the terminal, you understand the OS deeply (networking, filesystems, systemd, SELinux, kernel tuning) but this is an engineering and operations role, not a sysadmin role. You build and automate, not just maintain.

- Proven experience with STIG compliance and system hardening you've applied STIGs, remediated findings, and understand the "why" behind the controls, not just the checklist

- Strong experience standing up infrastructure in air-gapped/classified environments you understand the unique constraints and have operated in them

- Proficiency with Ansible Puppet and Terraform for building, managing, and versioning infrastructure as code at scale

- Strong scripting ability in Bash and Python writing production-grade automation, tooling, and operational scripts

- Hands-on experience with observability tooling Prometheus, Grafana, and ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) for monitoring, logging, alerting, and tracing distributed systems

- Leadership presence without the title you command respect through competence, directness, and reliability. You can walk into a room, align a group of strong engineers, and drive decisions. You are not a manager, but people follow your lead because you've earned it.

- Strong communication and documentation skills you can translate complex technical problems into clear, actionable language across audiences

- Strong initiative and self-direction in isolated, secure environments

- Understanding of software development practices including version control (Git), code review, testing, and agile methodologies

- Enthusiasm for transforming U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology in space environments

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Military background particularly veterans who understand the operational environment, the mission, and how to work within DoD culture. This carries real weight for this role.

- Experience with COMSEC and HAIPE-compliant inline Type-1 network encryptors

- Networking certifications (CCNA or equivalent)

- Familiarity with Space Domain Awareness data and systems

- Knowledge of Anduril's Lattice OS and its capabilities

- Proficiency in additional languages (Go, Rust, Java) and contributions to open-source projects

US Salary Range
$183,000 — $243,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits .

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

-
No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

- Please always verify communications:

- Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

- Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com .

-
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

-
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ .

raw.title: Principal Technical Program Manager
raw.description:
Overview
The Cloud & AI organization accelerates Microsoft's mission to ensure that our company and industry is securing digital technology platforms, devices, and clouds in our customers' heterogeneous environments, as well as ensuring the security of our own internal estate. Our culture is centered on embracing a growth mindset, inspiring excellence, and encouraging teams and leaders to bring their best each day. In doing so, we create life-changing innovations that impact billions of lives around the world.

Are you passionate about offensive security, emerging AI technologies, and solving complex technical problems at scale? Join the Microsoft Red Team (MRT), where we emulate real-world advanced persistent threats to ensure Microsoft, and the customers who depend on us, are prepared to face and respond to even the most determined adversaries.

CyberShield is the MRT program that extends our red team capability beyond Microsoft's own estate to select external customers. Our mandate is to shift red teaming from point-in-time, human-led engagements to a software-driven, continuous model powered by agentic, AI-driven red teaming. CyberShield works across Microsoft's own environment and customer environments spanning cloud, identity, network, endpoint, hardware, and operational security domains.

We are looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to drive the engineering and operational programs that enable CyberShield. You will partner with red team operators, security engineers, platform teams, and the CyberShield Engagement Lead Program Manager to build infrastructure and capabilities for customer operations, advance AI-driven offensive security, and translate emerging tradecraft into scalable technical solutions. You will own cross-functional technical planning, requirements, dependencies, risks, milestones, and measurable outcomes while ensuring that customer feedback and operational lessons shape engineering priorities. You will drive alignment across MRT, the CISO organization, and other Microsoft stakeholders so that engineering investments translate into impactful offensive capability and measurable security impact.

You will operate at the intersection of offensive security, engineering, AI, customer delivery, and technical program management. You will define and drive complex technical plans, partner with engineers to deliver solutions, manage dependencies and risks, establish measurable objectives and key results, and communicate technical strategy, progress, and outcomes to Microsoft leadership.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.

Responsibilities
- Drive complex, cross-functional engineering programs that enable CyberShield red team operations across Microsoft and select external customer environments.
- Partner closely with security engineers, red team operators, and platform engineers to define technical requirements and drive development of infrastructure, tooling, and AI capabilities that scale offensive security operations.
- Partner closely with the CyberShield Engagement Lead Program Manager to align customer needs, engagement execution, and technical delivery.
- Work directly with customers to understand and execute their technical and operational needs, ensure operations are delivered successfully, and drive feedback and lessons learned into actionable improvements.
- Translate novel red team tradecraft and operational requirements into actionable engineering plans, technical designs, milestones, and execution strategies.
- Drive programs that advance agentic, AI-driven red teaming, including capabilities that accelerate reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and analysis.
- Partner with individual contributor engineers and technical leads to drive complex technical solutions from concept and design through implementation and operational adoption.
- Establish and manage program objectives, key results, success criteria, engineering milestones, and other metrics that measure program execution and security impact.
- Identify technical, operational, customer, and organizational dependencies and risks, and drive cross-team decisions and mitigation plans.
- Partner across MRT, the CISO organization, and other Microsoft engineering and security teams to build alignment, resolve dependencies, and drive shared security outcomes.
- Develop technical program plans, engineering proposals, strategy documents, and executive-level communications; present technical plans, progress, risks, and outcomes to Microsoft leadership.
- Successfully operate in uncertain, complex, and novel environments, bringing structure to ambiguous technical problems and driving teams toward measurable outcomes.
- Embody our  Culture  and  Values

Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications:
- Bachelor's Degree AND 6+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development OR equivalent experience.
3+ years of experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.

Other Requirements:
- - Citizenship & Citizenship Verification:  This role will require access to information that is controlled for export under export control regulations, potentially under the U.S. International Traffic in Arms Regulations or Export Administration Regulations, the EU Dual Use Regulation, and/or other export control regulations. As a condition of employment, the successful candidate will be required to provide either proof of their country of citizenship or proof of their U.S. permanent residency or other protected status (e.g., under 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)) for assessment of eligibility to access the export controlled information. To meet this legal requirement, and as a condition of employment, the successful candidate’s citizenship will be verified with a valid passport. Lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees may verify status using other documents, where applicable.
-
- - Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
- Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft background and Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
Additional or preferred qualifications
- 6+ years of experience working in security engineering or a closely related technical security field.
- 6+ years of experience driving collaboration across multidisciplinary engineering, security, or technical teams.
- 2+ years of experience working in red teaming, penetration testing, offensive security, or a closely related security domain.
- 2+ years of experience working with complex data and performing analysis to drive technical or program decisions.
- Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, or a related technical field.
- Experience defining and driving complex engineering programs involving security infrastructure, offensive security, or cloud environments.
- Experience partnering closely with engineers to develop technical requirements, evaluate designs, manage engineering dependencies, and drive complex technical solutions through delivery.
- Understanding of red team operations, adversary emulation, penetration testing, offensive security tradecraft, or vulnerability research.
- Experience with AI-driven or agentic systems and an understanding of how AI can be applied to automate or scale complex technical workflows.
- Experience working with cloud technologies such as Azure, AWS, or GCP and familiarity with identity, endpoint, network, or application security.
- Experience establishing OKRs, program metrics, and data-driven measures of success and using those measures to inform technical and program decisions.
- Demonstrated ability to produce clear engineering plans, technical strategy documents, executive communications, and presentations for executive leadership.
- Experience influencing and driving alignment across engineering, security, product, and organizational boundaries without relying on direct authority.
- Experience operating successfully in ambiguous environments and turning emerging or poorly defined technical problems into structured programs and executable plans.
- Active U.S. Government TS//SCI clearance with full-scope polygraph is preferred, enabling work with highly sensitive customer environments.

raw.title: Principal Datacenter Operations Manager
raw.description:
Overview
Microsoft Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers Microsoft’s cloud services. Reporting directly to the Metro Leader, the Principal Datacenter Operations Manager ensures new and retrofitted datacenter infrastructure is ready for safe, reliable operations; orchestrates large-scale deployments; and translates metro-wide strategy into coordinated priorities, plans, and governance across campuses and functions. The role also leads change management and oversees facilities management across the Chicago Metro. Its scope spans design, construction, commissioning, operational readiness, turnover, stabilization, warranty, early-life performance, and modifications within live datacenter environments.
This leader connects the teams that design and deliver Microsoft datacenters with the teams that operate them, providing a coordinated Operations voice across Critical Environments (CE), IT, and Logistics. The role ensures safety, security, reliability, availability, quality, maintainability, and long-term operability are built in from the start. In parallel, the leader partners with the Metro Leader and functional leaders to align metro priorities, coordinate cross-campus planning, manage dependencies, and resolve gaps in ownership while preserving each Director’s accountability for execution and operational outcomes.
In this role, you will establish the organization’s strategy, governance, priorities, operating model, and culture; build and develop a high-performing team; and oversee operational readiness and infrastructure integrity across new datacenter builds, upgrades, retrofits, and live-site modifications. You will lead the planning cadence, decision forums, and cross-functional alignment that turn metro strategy into coordinated action, including change-management governance and facilities-management oversight across the Chicago Metro. Success requires strong organizational leadership, trusted partnerships, disciplined portfolio governance, and the ability to translate technical and operational risk into clear, decision-ready recommendations for leadership.

Responsibilities
1. Organizational Leadership and Strategy
- Build, lead, coach, and develop the Operations integration function across Strategic Design & Construction Operations Coordination, Tactical Construction Site Operations Coordination, and Turnover Deliverables & Post-Operation Coordination.
- Establish organizational strategy, priorities, governance, operating rhythm, performance expectations, resource allocation, and a long-term capability roadmap aligned with CO+I priorities.
- Lead and develop technical and program-management talent, strengthening technical depth, leadership capability, succession readiness, and organizational resilience.
- Lead integrated metro-wide capacity, workforce, and succession planning, allocating resources across campuses, sites, and programs based on business priority, infrastructure complexity, operational risk, portfolio demand, and long-term capability needs.
- Foster a culture centered on safety, security, quality, accountability, inclusion, partnership, operational excellence, continuous improvement, and One Microsoft principles.
- Represent the Operations integration function with Metro, regional, and broader CO+I leadership.
- Partner with the Metro Leader to set metro-wide strategy, priorities, guardrails, and decision rights, and translate that direction into aligned plans across Datacenter IT Operations, Critical Environments (CE), and IAM/Logistics leadership.
- Coordinate a unified planning cadence across campuses and Capacity Clusters, tracking cross-functional dependencies, risks, progress, and ownership gaps against metro priorities.
2. Datacenter Lifecycle Integration and Operational Readiness
- Lead Operations integration across design, construction, commissioning, operational readiness, turnover, stabilization, warranty, and post-turnover lifecycle activities.
- Ensure CE, IT, Logistics, maintainability, reliability, safety, security, and operational requirements are incorporated into infrastructure designs and formal design reviews.
- Establish Operations engagement throughout construction and commissioning, including quality reviews, readiness assessments, L2-L5 commissioning participation, and resolution of operational concerns before turnover.
- Establish standardized operational-readiness governance aligned with site-transition milestones, clear acceptance criteria, and defined decision rights.
- Ensure infrastructure, documentation, procedures, spares, training, tooling, systems, and operational dependencies are ready before operational acceptance, enabling Operations teams to safely and effectively assume ownership on Day 1.
- Support Go/No-Go and readiness decisions with clear, data-driven assessments of infrastructure and operational risk.
- Provide governance for post-turnover stabilization, warranty, and defect resolution, including monitoring early-life performance and driving corrective actions.
3. Infrastructure Integrity, Reliability, and Risk
- Establish a proactive approach to identifying and mitigating infrastructure and operational risk before it affects safety, security, availability, readiness, cost, schedule, or creates long-term technical debt.
- Use reliability data, commissioning findings, defect trends, operational incidents, equipment performance, and field experience to identify systemic risks and recurring issues.
- Partner with engineering, construction, commissioning, Operations, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), and vendors to drive corrective and preventive actions.
- Establish mechanisms for monitoring infrastructure integrity and early-life reliability across the Metro portfolio.
- Ensure lessons learned are converted into measurable improvements in future designs, standards, construction practices, commissioning, and operational-readiness processes.
4. Infrastructure Delivery, Construction Governance, and Live-Site Portfolio
- Provide Principal Datacenter Operations Manager-level governance across new datacenter delivery and a portfolio of Metro Operations construction projects, including infrastructure retrofits, upgrades, corrective work, and design modifications within operating datacenters.
- Maintain portfolio oversight for approved projects ranging from approximately $250K to $100M, with accountability for delivery strategy, prioritization, risk, financial performance, and operational outcomes.
- Ensure construction and infrastructure work in live environments is governed through rigorous change management, risk assessment, Method of Procedure (MOP) and Emergency Operating Procedure (EOP) review, commissioning, and outage planning to protect safety, customer availability, and operational continuity.
- Partner with Datacenter Engineering (DCE), Datacenter Delivery (DCD), Commissioning, and Operations to shape and govern infrastructure changes, ensuring new and modified assets are documented, commissioned, maintainable, and supportable by Operations.
- Drive scalable and cost-effective solutions while reducing rework, warranty exposure, duplicate effort, and avoidable operational cost.
5. Cross-Functional Operations Integration
- Serve as the senior Operations integration leader across CE, IT, Logistics, DCD, DCE, Commissioning, end-to-end organizations, Field Operations, contractors, OEMs, Metro Operations, and other key partners.
- Establish the role as the single integration point and one window into Operations for requirements across electrical, mechanical, controls, IT infrastructure, networking, structured cabling, logistics, spares, receiving, and asset management.
- Build trusted partnerships and establish clear accountability, decision-making, communication, and escalation mechanisms across participating organizations, applying a One Microsoft mindset to align teams around shared operational outcomes.
- Ensure Operations teams have the knowledge, documentation, training, tools, systems access, and resources required to safely and effectively operate new and modified infrastructure.
- Maintain continuity of operational knowledge and lessons learned across projects and sites.
- Align campuses and Capacity Clusters to metro priorities within agreed guardrails; in Tier 4 / X-Large metros, coordinate cross-Metro planning, alignment, and communications with the Metro GM and other Metro Leaders.
- Oversee facilities management across the Chicago Metro, aligning campus facilities plans, maintenance priorities, service standards, and issue resolution with metro-wide safety, reliability, availability, and cost objectives while preserving local and functional leaders’ accountability for execution.
- Provide metro-wide strategy, integration, and governance oversight without assuming local operational execution; Campus Directors retain ownership and accountability for campus execution and initiatives, while OU Portfolio, Capacity Cluster, IT, CE, and other functional Directors retain end-to-end accountability for their respective strategies, delivery, and operational outcomes.
6. Governance, Executive Communication, and Financial Accountability
- Establish consistent governance for infrastructure readiness, with clear decision rights, escalation paths, response expectations, and accountability.
- Ensure appropriate Operations representation in formal design reviews, readiness, Go/No-Go, and infrastructure-governance forums, supported by a centralized intake and issue-management model.
- Provide Metro and regional leadership with concise reporting on portfolio health, readiness, schedule, financial performance, infrastructure risk, reliability, and key decisions.
- Translate complex technical and operational issues into clear, decision-ready information for senior leadership and serve as the senior Operations escalation point for significant infrastructure-delivery and readiness risks.
- Maintain accountability for safety, security, quality, scope, schedule, financial performance, operational readiness, reliability, and risk across the integrated portfolio.
- Provide fiscal oversight for approved budgets and oversee vendor strategy, contracting, performance, and commercial accountability.
- Lead change management across the Chicago Metro, coordinating impact and risk assessments, stakeholder alignment, communications, readiness, and adoption for infrastructure, facilities, and operating-model changes; ensure clear approval, escalation, and implementation governance while maintaining functional ownership of execution.
- Maintain clear metro-wide escalation paths and decision forums, raise issues early, and enable timely, well-informed decisions across CE, IT, and IAM/Logistics leadership.
- Keep the Metro aligned to the standardized organizational model and Organization Design Guardrails, preparing capacity and complexity evidence for leadership-layer changes or exceptions reviewed through the Two-Lens Framework and approved through LT governance.
- Serve as a trusted strategy and integration partner to the Metro Leader while functional Directors retain end-to-end accountability for operational execution and outcomes.
7. Operational Excellence and Continuous Improvement
- Establish and monitor meaningful key performance indicators (KPIs) for infrastructure readiness, delivery quality, reliability, issue resolution, schedule performance, risk reduction, cost efficiency, and organizational effectiveness.
- Use performance insights and lessons learned to establish common standards, share best practices across campuses, identify systemic opportunities, and drive measurable improvements in processes and future datacenter delivery.
- Track indicators such as readiness milestone completion, issue aging, commissioning and turnover defect trends, documentation quality, early-life operational issues, infrastructure availability, capacity acceptance, warranty trends, recurring failures, risk closure, rework and cost avoidance, and lessons-learned implementation.
- Develop a scalable and repeatable infrastructure-integrity and operational-readiness model that strengthens integration between datacenter delivery and Operations across CO+I.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
- High School Qualification or equivalent AND 10+ years' experience of mission-critical service management (e.g., providing IT services, manufacturing, warehouse, retail, military, or managing physical operations in an IT and/or critical environment infrastructure) OR equivalent experience.

- 3+ years' people management experience.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
- Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
Preferred Qualifications:
- Bachelor's or Technical College Degree in Computer Science, Math, Telecommunications, Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, Supply Chain Management or related field AND 15+ years' experience in enterprise-level experience managing large scale and complex projects/programs, or critical environment infrastructures (e.g., UPS, Generator, AHU), or working in physical IT infrastructures (e.g., Servers, SANs, Networking, Capacity, DC Rack/Enclosures, structured cabling) OR High School Qualification or equivalent AND 17+ years' experience in enterprise-level experience managing large scale and complex projects/programs, or critical environment infrastructures (e.g., UPS, Generator, AHU), or working in physical IT infrastructures (e.g., Servers, SANs, Networking, Capacity, DC Rack/Enclosures, structured cabling) OR equivalent experience.

- 5+ years' people management experience.

- Applicable certifications: APICS/Inventory Control, CompTIA, Microsoft, Network Certifications, CCNA Certifications, ITIL v3 Foundation, Microsoft Operations Framework (MOF) Certifications, Leadership Development Certifications, PMP, CDCMP.

- Demonstrated experience across multiple infrastructure lifecycle stages, including design, construction, commissioning, operational readiness, turnover, stabilization, warranty, or live-site operations.
- Demonstrated understanding of mission-critical infrastructure, operational risk, infrastructure delivery, safety, security, quality, cost, schedule, commissioning, and reliability.
- Demonstrated ability to lead through influence and establish accountability across organizations and partners outside direct reporting relationships.
- Strong executive communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical, operational, and business risks into clear recommendations and decisions.
- Proven ability to anticipate, assess, and mitigate infrastructure and operational risk and to build trusted partnerships across engineering, construction, commissioning, Operations, and vendor organizations.
- Demonstrated experience aligning strategy, priorities, and integrated plans across IT Operations, Critical Environments, IAM/Logistics, or comparable cross-functional organizations.
- Experience establishing and operating governance mechanisms, including escalation paths, decision forums, performance reviews, guardrails, and structured decision-making.
- Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence senior leaders and Directors without direct authority while preserving clear functional accountability.
- Demonstrated systems and strategic thinking, governance discipline, cross-functional collaboration, and executive communication skills.
- Extensive experience leading organizations or programs responsible for datacenter infrastructure, operational readiness, critical environments, infrastructure reliability, or large-scale mission-critical operations.
- Experience leading infrastructure programs across multiple sites, campuses, or a regional portfolio.
- Experience delivering retrofit, upgrade, and design-change programs in live mission-critical environments while protecting customer availability and operational continuity.
- Experience across the full infrastructure lifecycle, including design reviews, L1-L5 commissioning, turnover, stabilization, warranty, and operational lifecycle management.
- Working knowledge of Critical Environment infrastructure, including electrical, mechanical, controls, uninterruptible power supply (UPS), generators, switchgear, cooling systems, and battery energy storage systems (BESS), plus familiarity with IT infrastructure, networking, structured cabling, and datacenter logistics.
- Relevant professional certifications or licenses such as PMP, CDCMP, CxA/ACG, LEED AP, OSHA 30, or applicable engineering or construction credentials.
- Experience with organizational design, capacity planning, Capacity Clusters, or multi-site and cross-Metro operating models in hyperscale or mission-critical environments.

raw.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Missiles - Active Clearance
raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Air Dominance and Strike Division is one of Anduril’s fastest growing, most technically complex divisions. We develop and build  collaborative combat aircraft , missiles, and the software that powers these autonomous weapons. We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to lead one of our development programs across various stages of the contract lifecycle from early R&D to contract capture and close. As a Technical Program Manager you will lead the development and integration of Anduril products and technologies alongside the Chief Engineer and will be directly responsible for all elements of cost and schedule to ensure successful delivery of the program.

ABOUT THE JOB

Success in this position hinges on three key facets:

- Systems and engineering mindset - the ability to understand and assess technical concept. Identifying system dependencies, interfaces, technical risks and the impact of key architectural decisions with the engineering team.

- Execution focused - digging into the details, charting the path and owning the outcome. You will be expected to utilize your technical aptitude in conjunction with your program management, and leadership skills to deliver the best outcome for Anduril and the customer.

- Collaborative partnership - managing customer relationships and shaping the future of the program with the government.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- In partnership with the Chief Engineer, own the development and deployment of Anduril’s Air Dominance & Strike technologies to meet the operational needs of the Department of Defense

- Develop strong, trusting relationships with Anduril’s DOD customers, ensuring we have tight feedback loops that enable us shape solutions, rapidly iterate, and ultimately field solutions faster

- Autonomously execute on broad and/or ambiguous requirements from internal engineering, customers, and third party corporate partners to own successful delivery of outcomes on multiple programs simultaneously

- Monitor and manage program progress across cost, schedule, and resource allocation, making tradeoffs that enable us to deliver best-in-class solutions to our customers on-time and on-budget

- Develop and implement lightweight processes, tools, and metrics for program planning, scope management, risk management, and customer communication to enable Anduril to move rapidly

raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril Imaging builds electro-optical and infrared sensor systems that go on Anduril platforms as well as our own stand-alone products. The hardware is precision optics, cooled infrared detectors, custom electronics, and tight-tolerance electromechanical assemblies. Several products are moving from development into rate production at the same time.

ABOUT THE JOB

Senior Commodity Manager owns the supply chain outcomes behind those products. The team is small and growing. You will own supplier relationships end to end, from identifying a source and negotiating the agreement to standing up capacity and holding it through a ramp.

This role requires deep understanding of areas in infrared optics and the materials behind them. Germanium crystal, boules, and blanks. Chalcogenide infrared glass. Lens and window fabrication, grinding, polishing, diamond turning, and centering as well as optical coatings. Lens cell assemblies and related optical assemblies. Detector and dewar assemblies, cold filters, and cryocoolers.

This commodity carries additional exposure. Germanium pricing and availability are driven by export policy and a thin upstream supply base, and the alternative material paths carry their own critical mineral dependencies. The work includes reaching past tier one into the feedstock layer, modeling material price scenarios, and structuring forward positions and consignment arrangements that secure supply rather than just placing orders.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own suppliers end to end. Identify and select sources, run requests for quote, drive input to make-buy decisions, and serve as the commercial and technical owner of the relationship. Supplier signals currently reach Anduril through several uncoordinated paths. You will be the conduit that keeps them consistent across programs.

- Negotiate the commercial structure. Draft and negotiate pricing, capacity commitments, lead times, payment, warranty, and service terms. Build toward long-term agreements where they secure capacity. Sequence leverage deliberately so commitments buy terms rather than just parts.

- Build the cost model, then use it. Develop should-cost and clean-sheet models, run cost-breakdown analysis on quotes, and drive total cost of ownership across the lifecycle. Reconcile bill of material cost against finance so product cost reflects what the parts actually cost.

- Secure capacity ahead of ramp. Map supply network lead time and flexibility, place coverage against demand well before it is needed, and resolve capacity gaps before they become schedule problems. Suppliers in this space book out far in advance. The job is to be early.

- Engage engineering before the design locks. Give design for manufacturability feedback, influence specifications using supply intelligence on availability, lead time, and lifecycle health, so design decisions account for supply reality instead of discovering it.

- De-risk the bill of material. Complete risk assessments, qualify alternates and second sources, drive commonality and supplier rationalization, and manage obsolescence before it gates a build.

- Escalate and clear blockers. Participate in program reviews and operational escalation forums. Triage supply disruptions, resolve shortages, and drive supplier issues to conclusion, including executive escalation when it is warranted.

- Carry compliance into the sourcing decision. Work country of origin, domestic content, defense acquisition regulation, export control, and rated order requirements into supplier selection and purchase order structure. The point is to engineer compliance into the design and supply decision rather than remediate it later.

- Complete supplier qualification. Own the capability and authorization portions of supplier evaluation and coordinate with the Supplier Quality Organization.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering, supply chain, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience

- 8 or more years across sourcing engineering, commodity management, supplier development, supplier quality, manufacturing engineering, or cost engineering

- Experience owning supplier relationships that included both technical assessment and commercial negotiation

- Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and CAD model and assemblies.

- Ability to travel a 10-25% of the time for vendor on-site visits

- Eligible to access export-controlled technical data under United States export control law

- Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. secret clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Advanced technical degree

- Experience in infrared or electro-optical systems, precision optics, photonics, sensors, or other high-precision hardware

- Should-cost or clean-sheet cost modeling, design-to-cost, or value engineering work

- Experience taking a product from development into rate production, particularly in high-mix low-volume environments

- Experience negotiating long-term agreements, supply agreements, or capacity commitments

- Familiarity with defense acquisition regulation flowdowns, export control, rated orders, country of origin, or domestic content requirements

- Experience in a fast-moving company where the process was still being built

- Provide mentorship, coaching, and career development opportunities for team members.

- Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, and results-driven performance.

- Track and report key metrics, including cost savings, supplier quality (PPM), on-time delivery, and supplier capacity.

- Develop and implement scalable processes to improve supplier management and operational efficiency.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, engineering, or related technical field.

- 8+ years of experience in strategic sourcing or supplier development roles, with at least 3+ years of people management experience.

- Experience managing and scaling teams in a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment, leading supplier industrialization efforts for NPI and scaling production.

- Ability to travel up to 50% of the time.

- Ability to relocate, if not already local to be onsite in Costa Mesa, CA.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Master's degree in electrical or electronics engineering.

- Proven ability to lead supplier industrialization efforts for NPI and scaling production.

- Experience with ERP systems and data analysis tools for cost modeling and performance tracking.

- Well-versed in TCO analysis to ensure data-driven analytics tied to component and supplier selection, in a product-based ecosystem.

- Strategic thinker, experienced putting together commodities strategy/roadmap with key engineering stakeholders.

- Proven leadership in driving and influencing other teams to a common goal. You know how to effectively communicate and collaborate cross functionally and with all levels within an organization.

- Can wear different hats and it a strong team player to help your team move forward.

- You are fluent in other cross functional areas to fill gaps and remove roadblocks when needed.

- Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. TS clearance.

US Salary Range
$191,000 — $254,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits .

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

-
No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

- Please always verify communications:

- Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

- Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com .

-
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

-
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ .

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

From detection to tracking, identification, deterrence, and defeat, our family of networked sensors and effectors enables our customers to rapidly close the kill chain against a broad range of uncrewed aerial system (UAS) threats.

The Counter-Intrusion business line works on products that enable operators to protect their people and assets from threats on land and sea. We are deployed in every major global operating theater and support a diversity of mission sets across both U.S. Government and allied partners.

Sentry is the primary product focus of this role and it is fielded across both business lines. The Sentry platform integrates robotics, autonomy, hardware, and software to deliver mission-critical capabilities in defense and security, with a rapidly growing fleet and new variants in development. Product Operations is the team that keeps that fleet healthy once it leaves the factory, working across product, engineering, deployment operations, logistics, and sustainment to turn what happens in the field into actionable improvements.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Product Operations Engineer supporting Air Defense and Counter Intrusion, you will be the architect behind how we observe, maintain, and evolve the deployed Sentry fleet. Where others respond to incidents, you build the systems, queries, and processes that enable prevention. You will develop a deep product understanding, serving as a function SME for all things Sentry. You will work with product engineering partners to design, deploy, and improve a system that supports RCCA cycle execution and delivers actionable product improvement signal, directly impacting the design of next generation hardware and software. You will develop and deploy uptime reporting and observability tooling to measure and facilitate capability availability for customers. You will manage and democratize the Sentry knowledge base for field operations functions and support the proliferation of self service resources.

You should bring strong technical depth in robotics engineering, experience leading iterative design across multiple teams, a systems approach to problem solving, and a familiarity with reliability and quality methodologies such as FRACAS. If you are passionate about ground-breaking technology, contributing to the national security mission, and engineering operational excellence from the ground up, Anduril is interested in speaking with you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Product Subject Matter Expertise: Build and hold deep technical understanding of the Sentry system, hardware and software, and serve as the product operations SME for Sentry across both business lines, helping technical and non-technical stakeholders understand each other.

RCCA Cycle Design and Execution: Partner with product engineering to design, deploy, and continuously improve the system that drives root cause corrective action (RCCA) cycles on fielded Sentry towers, from failure capture through corrective action deployment.

Product Improvement Signal: Turn fleet failure data, field feedback, and reliability trends into actionable product improvement signal for engineering, directly informing the design of next generation Sentry hardware and software.

Reliability and Quality Methodology: Apply and mature failure reporting, analysis, and corrective action (FRACAS) practice for Sentry, establishing how failures are classified, tracked, and closed so reliability improvement is measurable rather than anecdotal.

Uptime Reporting and Capability Availability: Develop and deploy uptime reporting that measures and facilitates capability availability for customers, translating raw telemetry into fleet health metrics that program, product, and leadership stakeholders act on.

Observability Tooling: Proactively build and improve the observability tooling behind that reporting in partnership with hardware and software engineering, so coverage keeps pace with new Sentry variants and new site deployments.

Sentry Knowledge Base: Own, democratize, and continuously improve the Sentry knowledge base for field operations functions, so operational knowledge is codified, accurate, and usable by any level of on call support.

Self Service Enablement: Expand the self service resources, runbooks, SOPs, and troubleshooting guides that field and deployment teams rely on, so more is resolved at the point of need and the escalations that do arrive are better characterized.

Iterative Design Across Teams: Lead iterative design cycles spanning product operations, engineering, and deployment functions, building agreement on what to change next and carrying it through to implementation.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- 5+ years of experience in product operations, technical support, site reliability, or a comparable technical operations role supporting deployed hardware and software systems, with demonstrated progression in scope and ownership

- Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, or another relevant technical field, or equivalent hands-on technical experience (military, industrial, or field support)

- Technical depth in robotics, mechatronics, or complex electromechanical systems, including the ability to reason across hardware, software, and networking boundaries

- Demonstrated experience driving root cause corrective action (RCCA) to closure on complex systems, including how failures are captured, classified, and verified as resolved

- Experience leading iterative design or improvement cycles across multiple engineering and operations teams, carrying a change from problem statement through implementation

- Proficiency developing monitoring queries, dashboards, and alerting configurations using observability platforms such as Datadog, Grafana, or similar tooling

- Experience validating and verifying software changes on distributed or fielded systems, including rollout, verification, and rollback considerations

- Scripting and automation skills (e.g., Python, Bash) with a track record of building tooling that improves operational efficiency, plus fluency with development and issue tracking tooling such as Git and Jira

- Demonstrated ability to author clear, thorough technical documentation including runbooks, SOPs, and troubleshooting guides for both technical and non-technical audiences

- Ability to coordinate technical and non-technical efforts across product, engineering, deployment, and sustainment functions, including across more than one program or customer at a time

- Proven ability to work independently, identify what needs to be built, and deliver it without close direction

- Excellent written, visual, and verbal communication skills

- Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Prior military or government agency exposure or experience

- Familiarity with reliability and quality methodologies such as FRACAS, FMEA, or equivalent structured failure analysis practice

- Experience with Linux system administration and command-line troubleshooting of electromechanical or networked systems

- Experience supporting autonomous sensor systems, counter-UAS systems, and/or complex robotics systems

- Experience building or owning a technical knowledge base, documentation system, or self service support resources

- Exposure to Anduril's Lattice OS or similar command-and-control software platforms

raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

The Supply Chain Sr. Digital Tools Engineer role will act as a Business Systems and Optimization partner for Anduril's Supply Chain team and will own parts of the end-to-end Supply Chain Digital and Process ecosystem. As such, the role will collaborate with internal Supply Chain teams (Procurement, Purchasing, Planning, Program Management) and external teams (IT, Engineering, Business Systems, Strategy, Legal, People, etc.) to develop system implementation plans intended to enhance our digital landscape and increase efficiencies throughout our end-to-end processes, all with a focus on introducing scale and resiliency into our growing people and tools footprint. As a Sr. Digital Tools Engineer, you will have two primary responsibilities:

- Optimizing Supply Chain Systems & Processes: You will work across procurement, purchasing, planning, and program management functions to improve the systems and data infrastructure that power our supply chain operations. You will build out data-capture capabilities, design analytics reporting, and drive system enhancements that enable scalable, sustainable growth.

- Solving Complex Cross-Functional Problems: You will be frequently pulled into high-priority initiatives that span multiple teams and systems—problems that are critical to solve but don't fall neatly into any single team's domain. You bring structure to ambiguity and drive solutions where others see only complexity.

Much of the time, both of these go hand-in-hand. You will be embedded in the business, working cross-functionally with supply chain leaders, IT, engineering, business systems, strategy, legal, people, and other stakeholders to solve our messiest systems and data problems, translate operational needs into technical requirements, and equip teams with the tools and insights they need to perform at their best.

- Support system implementations, upgrades, and migrations by leading user acceptance testing, developing training materials, and championing change management across the organization.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Strong project management capabilities—proven record of getting difficult projects over the finish line while juggling challenging deadlines, an evolving stakeholder base, and moving milestones. Effort and pursuit of progress should be your default mode.

- Ability to fully immerse yourself in a new domain or knowledge area, absorb critical information and the current set of challenges, and proactively progress initiatives toward resolution without needing to be guided through every step.

- Understanding of core supply chain elements—sourcing, procurement, inventory, and payment—and an eagerness to continuously deepen your knowledge base across these areas.

- Strong analytical aptitude with the ability to quickly execute analyses in Excel, SQL, or BI tools (Tableau, Power BI, Looker, etc.). You intuitively think about problems in terms of data models, system logic, and process flows.

- Self-driven and relentlessly proactive. You don't wait on others to solve problems—you step into the gap to offer solutions yourself. We'd rather have to tell you to slow down than to speed up.

- Experience with system integration tools, APIs, or middleware platforms

- Familiarity with data modeling, ETL processes, or data warehousing constructs

- Experience supporting ERP implementations, major system migrations, and/or continuous enhancement projects

- Experience in working on process optimization projects with both internal and external stakeholders under tight deadlines

- Background in hardware manufacturing, aerospace & defense, or other complex supply chain environments

raw.description:
Who We Are

Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.

What We Offer

Salary:
$115,000.00 - $158,500.00
Location:
Santa Clara,CA
You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits .

What You'll Do
This posting is for a Santa Clara, California-based New Product (NPI) instructor. This position is a combination technical instructor and technical expert role on existing and new products. The position is embedded in the business unit (BU) in Gloucester in order to learn the new PLC/NPI products (i.e. the new chambers, new mainframes, and new tools) for the BU, gain experience on the startup and sustaining production tasks on the tool and develop/deliver initial classroom and hands-on training on the tool. Once the tool transitions to volume production, the NPI instructor will train up the volume instructor, who then takes over the product from a training ownership standpoint.
Due to the scheduling of PLC/NPI product development, the NPI instructor will often be researching, gaining knowledge/experience, and developing/delivering for several new tools/chambers at a time, so project management, training/presentation experience, and technical experience (mechanical, electrical, etc.) of semiconductor equipment is required.
Basic breakdown of time is:
~45% learning the new tool and gaining knowledge and experience (mechanical, electrical, software, process, etc.) and developing the course materials, structure and updating of existing courses
~35% delivering training or coordinating structured factory OJT
~20% other activities

Role Responsibilities
- Conducts semiconductor equipment training needs assessment by collecting information pertaining to work procedures, workflow, and functional knowledge from the experts; understanding job-specific functions and tasks; maintains product technical knowledge sufficient to prepare and present defined product courses; disseminates new information to training and business unit staff
- Communicates with product groups to obtain current product information for course updates; manages multiple projects of diverse scope and complexity; directs project team members. Represents AGS TS at divisional meetings, external conferences and industry task force activities
- Determines system utilization requirements by researching and testing systems
- Utilizes Technical Publications and System Product Business Groups to maximize technical documentation efficiencies; occasionally develops customized training materials per customer needs; trains others in standard course development process/Instructional System Design (ISD); ensures the correct revisions of product procedures and schematics; identifies and corrects procedural issues with the business unit
- Lead NPI training development projects with minimal support; develop hardware training student guides by identifying and describing information needs; using basic desktop publishing (PowerPoint and Word); submitting initial versions for review; revising and editing final copy
- Maintains safe and healthy training environment by following organization standards and legal regulations; Provides technical expertise and troubleshooting skills to assist with system repairs; ensures system functionality can support course objectives; ensures all safety retrofits are installed on the training systems
- Presents technical training in house and at customer sites; conducts training classes by presenting job-specific classroom and hands-on learning environments and opportunities; manages classroom/lab activities to ensure fulfillment of course objectives; presents and practices safety per procedure; may train during off shift and/or weekends as assigned; actively certifies others; establishes new certification requirements; Evaluates training by evaluating effectiveness of training to specific job applications
- Provides coaching and leadership to other instructors; serves as mentor to less senior instructors for class delivery, technical development and certification; anticipates, prevents and resolves customer satisfaction issues.
- Ensure operation of equipment by completing preventive maintenance requirements; following manufacturer's instructions; troubleshooting malfunctions; calling for repairs; maintaining equipment inventories; evaluating new equipment and techniques
- Maintains quality service by establishing and enforcing organization standards; demonstrates knowledge and understanding of the AGS Training Services organization and operations and the AGS organization; informs customers of additional AGS TS courses/products available; assists Marketing in building customer relationships and selling AGS TS products; analyzes customer issues/needs to determine future training opportunities; deliver training solutions for customer needs
- Maintains technical and instructional knowledge by attending educational workshops, reviewing publications, etc.
- Contributes to team effort by accomplishing related results as needed
- Will require both domestic and international travel (up to 40%).

- CMP

- If no bachelor’s degree, 6 years of professional semiconductor equipment experience

- Preferred - Nationally recognized certification in “Instructional Design” or 2 years of formal or informal experience in curriculum development and/or instructional design.
- Excellent communication, presentation, problem solving, teamwork and interpersonal communication skills; Resourceful, able to work and learn independently where necessary; Highly self-motivated and dedicated professional
- Presentation skills, written communication, training delivery, project/information management, self-development, presenting technical information, self-confidence, dealing with complexity, Microsoft Office skills
- Equipment: office equipment, power supplies, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, volt meters, soldering irons, hand tools, power tools, and personal computers
- Semiconductor equipment skills: operations, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, alignments, calibrations, and system-level troubleshooting skills on analog/digital electronics
- Knowledge of MS Windows applications and computer networking a plus
- Experience in e-Learning a plus
- Experience in videography and photography a plus

4 - 7 Years

Yes, 25% of the Time

raw.title: Datacenter & Agentic AI Workload Performance Optimization Engineer
raw.location: Santa Clara, California, United States; Toronto, Ontario, Canada
raw.description:
Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.

Tenstorrent is looking for a Workload Performance Optimization Engineer to help optimize the software workloads that run on our next-generation RISC-V platforms. You’ll work across modern datacenter and agentic AI workloads—including Java, Python, PHP, Node.js, Lua, Go, and Rust—to identify performance bottlenecks and develop software, compiler, runtime, and hardware-aware optimizations that improve throughput, latency, and efficiency. This role sits at the intersection of software runtimes, compilers, CPU microarchitecture, and RISC-V silicon. You’ll bring up and tune major runtimes, profile real-world applications, investigate memory and concurrency behavior, and explore optimizations using RISC-V Vector/Matrix capabilities and custom instructions. You’ll also work with AI-assisted development and automated optimization workflows to accelerate the performance engineering process. Your work will directly influence both the RISC-V software ecosystem and the architecture of future Tenstorrent CPUs.

This role is remote, based out of North America.

We welcome candidates at various experience levels for this role. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting.

Who You Are

- You’re a performance engineer who enjoys getting deep into runtimes, compilers, applications, and CPU microarchitecture to understand why software is fast—or slow.

- You have hands-on experience optimizing software on RISC-V or another modern CPU architecture, with a strong understanding of the hardware/software boundary.

- You’re comfortable profiling complex systems, finding bottlenecks, forming hypotheses, and iterating through optimizations using data.

- You’re excited about emerging agentic AI development workflows and using AI tools to automate profiling, coding, benchmarking, and optimization.

- You’re a strong technical collaborator who can work across compiler, runtime, systems software, hardware, and performance modeling teams.

What We Need

- Master’s or PhD in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, with strong experience in performance optimization, computer architecture, compilers, or systems software.

- Hands-on experience with runtime or compiler optimization, such as OpenJDK/JIT, LLVM, GCC, V8, Python, or equivalent systems.

- Strong understanding of CPU performance, memory hierarchies, concurrency, garbage collection, vector/SIMD optimization, and RISC-V architecture.

- Expertise with performance profiling and analysis tools such as Linux perf, runtime profilers, QEMU, tracing tools, and performance modeling environments.

- Strong programming skills in Java, Python, C/C++, and RISC-V assembly, with the ability to work effectively across multiple software layers.

What You Will Learn

- How to optimize modern software stacks from application and runtime all the way down to CPU microarchitecture and silicon.

- How RISC-V Vector, Matrix, and custom ISA capabilities can be used to accelerate real-world datacenter and AI workloads.

- How runtime, compiler, memory, and concurrency decisions impact performance at datacenter scale.

- How to build automated and AI-assisted performance optimization workflows that continuously profile, analyze, modify, and benchmark software.

- How to influence future CPU architecture by connecting real workload behavior and software optimization opportunities to hardware design decisions.

Compensation for all engineers at Tenstorrent ranges from $100k - $500k including base and variable compensation targets. Experience, skills, education, background and location all impact the actual offer made.

Tenstorrent offers a highly competitive compensation package and benefits, and we are an equal opportunity employer.
This offer of employment is contingent upon the applicant being eligible to access U.S. export-controlled technology.  Due to U.S. export laws, including those codified in the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), the Company is required to ensure compliance with these laws when transferring technology to nationals of certain countries (such as EAR Country Groups D:1, E1, and E2).   These requirements apply to persons located in the U.S. and all countries outside the U.S.  As the position offered will have direct and/or indirect access to information, systems, or technologies subject to these laws, the offer may be contingent upon your citizenship/permanent residency status or ability to obtain prior license approval from the U.S. Commerce Department or applicable federal agency.  If employment is not possible due to U.S. export laws, any offer of employment will be rescinded.

raw.title: Senior Technical Program Manager NPI, Anduril Expeditionary Systems
raw.description:

By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril Expeditionary Systems (AES) is the team at Anduril dedicated to the development and fielding of next-generation hardware — from man-portable systems to autonomous launchers — that modernize the command and control capabilities of U.S. and Allied forces. Delivering these systems at speed and scale demands program leaders who can drive complex, cross-functional execution from concept through production, hold accountability across engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing, and engage customers and stakeholders with credibility and clarity. If you thrive at the intersection of technology and operational excellence, join us. Your work will directly shape the balance of defense capabilities on a global scale.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You are the single accountable owner for schedule, cost, and scope across your program, and the primary interface between the program team, senior leadership, and external stakeholders. You will drive decisions, not just surface them.

- Own the full program lifecycle for assigned AES hardware programs — from NPI and prototype builds through low-rate and full-rate production — with accountability for schedule, cost, and scope performance.

- Serve as the primary point of contact for internal stakeholders and external customers — delivering clear, credible program status and representing AES with confidence in program reviews, CDRs, and customer engagements.

- Partner with Supply Chain and Manufacturing to drive production scaling plans, capacity investments, and make/buy decisions that support program commitments.

- Demonstrated track record of delivering complex hardware programs on schedule and within budget, from early development through production

- Strong technical fluency — you can engage substantively with engineering teams on design decisions, system integration challenges, and production readiness criteria

- Deep knowledge of program management disciplines: integrated master scheduling, risk management, earned value or equivalent cost tracking, and requirements management

- Experience supporting NPI programs through DV, PV, or LRIP gates

- Background in financial operations or program controls (budgeting, planning, EVM, cost tracking)

- PMP, CAPM, or equivalent certification

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical Engineering, Operations, or a related technical field

- Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. security clearance

- Familiarity with ITAR-controlled programs and associated documentation and compliance requirements

- Background in manufacturing operations, production engineering, or supply chain management

ABOUT THE JOB

Battlespace Awareness software services comprise advanced algorithms for sense-making and decision-making at tactical timelines.  This role requires an individual with a strong technical background in software development, particularly in the domain of optimization and estimation, and experience managing complex projects with multiple sub-teams and many stakeholders. The Sr Technical Program Manager will be the linchpin in ensuring that the software is developed in line with the objectives defined and is released according to the planned schedule.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
