Overview
Microsoft is committed to ensuring that we develop and deploy our AI technologies in ways that uphold our AI principles and warrant people’s trust. The Office of Responsible AI plays a leading role in this effort as part of Microsoft’s Corporate, External, and Legal Affairs (CELA) division. With a cross-company mandate, we establish internal policy for how our engineering and sales teams implement responsible AI practices, enable our community of Responsible AI Champs to support our responsible AI program, and review engineering and customer projects that require additional input based on potential impact. We also help to shape new laws, norms, and standards to advance responsible AI for the benefit of society at large.

The Sensitive Uses and Emerging Technologies team within the Office of Responsible AI is responsible for providing guidance on Microsoft’s most sensitive and cutting-edge AI products, emerging technologies, and initiatives. Across Microsoft, we work alongside engineering colleagues on AI model and product development and engage with Microsoft researchers and sales teams from around the world. Within the Office of Responsible AI, we partner closely with our Internal Policy & Practice team, whose remit includes developing responsible AI policies and practices that scale across the company and supporting the implementation efforts for our Responsible AI Standard.

As a Principal Technical Program Manager, Responsible AI on the Sensitive Uses and Emerging Technologies team, you will provide internal consulting and assessment of high-impact AI use cases and support all facets of the Sensitive Uses program. You will evaluate AI-driven products to assess risks, define requirements, develop strategic initiatives, manage sensitive use case management programs and processes, support incident response processes, and socialize policies that support Microsoft’s ability to develop and deploy AI systems safely and responsibly. In doing so, you will partner with engineering, policy, research, sales, and marketing, stakeholders to rapidly adjust to the changing AI and policy landscape, drive new requirements across product teams, and cutting-edge AI technology at the forefront of a new computing paradigm.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Responsibilities
- Support the Sensitive Uses and Emerging Technologies team within the Office of Responsible AI to evaluate and develop internal guidance and programs for Microsoft’s highest-impact AI models, products, and use cases from across Microsoft, including model and product releases using generative AI and state-of-the-art frontier models.
- Develop insights, recognize patterns, and assess AI system architectures with an eye toward providing actionable risk mitigation guidance. Use your deep knowledge of use cases and product deployments to develop more generalizable, scalable policies to account for the risks and impacts of AI systems deployed in an increasingly wide range of social contexts.
- Partner with engineering teams to contribute to, prioritize, and deliver on product roadmaps, primarily by evaluating their upcoming product releases for responsible AI risks and evidence of mitigation effectiveness. Develop a deep understanding of AI technology and responsible AI engineering implementations to connect to and develop AI policy.
- Manage, document, and drive progress to uphold responsible AI requirements across a diverse group of Microsoft engineering, sales, and research teams implementing AI systems in products, features, and customer engagements. Think through global challenges and drive accountability and results through others.
- Manage governance programs and processes for AI systems to ensure that specific performance requirements and standards are met throughout the development lifecycle.
- Create relationships to drive orchestration and integration efforts for the development and implementation process of responsible AI for multiple feature areas (e.g., product, services) and large and complex cross-functional projects with internal teams. Collaborates and coordinates across organizations to ensure alignment on product management and release, including tradeoffs, adjustments, and improvements as feasible.
- Embody Microsoft’s  culture and a demonstrated commitment to the company’s core values , including a commitment to high ethical standards, unquestioned integrity, and a commitment to advancing the company’s diversity & inclusion commitments.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's Degree AND 6+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, applied science, technology policy, research, governance, product development; or related area - OR equivalent experience.

- 3+ years experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.

Preferred Qualifications

- 3+ years work experience on issues pertaining to artificial intelligence, machine learning, or responsible AI, such as AI/ML engineering, AI-related technical program management, AI product development, data science with AI/ML components, inclusive design, ethics, safety, fairness, explainability, accessibility, privacy, security, AI governance, and/or AI policy.
- Experience with generative AI a plus but not required.
- Specific technical experience in fields of responsible AI, AI ethics, AI safety, digital safety, or security a plus but not required.
- Experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.
- Ability to navigate ambiguity and adapt to rapidly changing environments and demands. When dealing with emergent and complex topics, you strive to create structure and process that will support progress while remaining flexible as positions evolve.
- Experience working in or with a large, matrixed organization.
- Proven record of being an effective team player dedicated to collective successes. The ability to promote cooperation and solve problems in a timely, creative, and professional manner. Proficiency at working closely and collaboratively with multiple departments and executives, and in cross-functional teams.
- A proven track record of being able to engage and influence a variety of stakeholders, both within and outside Microsoft. Ability to collect and reason through multi-stakeholder perspectives, including those of executives, engineers and developers, sellers, researchers, civil society organizations, and regulators, all of whom grapple with new and complex technologies and their implications for society.
- Highly developed written and verbal communication skills. Ability to proactively advance company positions through high-impact engagement in small and/or large group settings, including communications with business leaders.
- Experience in strategic program management, execution, operations, and evaluation. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, projects, and deadlines simultaneously. You can quickly spot technical and process blockers towards achieving outcomes and work collaboratively to develop strategies to overcome them.
- Proven record of experimentation and openness to feedback, learning from both successes and failures.

raw.title: Senior Technical Program Manager - Lethality Team
raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Lethality Team develops and tests advanced warhead and munitions systems for multiple Anduril platforms. We work across the full hardware lifecycle—from early concepts and rapid prototypes to system testing and production turning evolving mission needs into field-ready capability.

Our programs move quickly, span multiple engineering and operational teams, and rarely follow a perfectly linear path. Success requires clear priorities, disciplined execution, and someone who can keep the larger system moving while technical teams solve hard engineering problems.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to lead cross-functional execution across a portfolio of warhead-development programs. You will connect the Energetics Team with vehicle programs and translate changing requirements, schedules, quantities, and priorities into clear and executable plans.

You will own the program structure that allows engineers to remain focused on technical work: aligning stakeholders, maintaining integrated schedules, tracking requirements and dependencies, surfacing risks early, and driving decisions to closure. Your programs may range from early concepts seeking funding to mature products preparing to deliver thousands of units.

This is a hardware-focused role for someone who understands how design, procurement, fabrication, integration, testing, and production depend on one another. You do not need to be a warhead designer. You do need the technical judgment to ask the right questions, recognize downstream consequences, and keep multiple teams moving toward a shared outcome.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Lead program execution across multiple warhead-development efforts, from early concept and prototype work through testing and production transition.

- Build and maintain integrated plans that connect scope, schedules, requirements, resources, costs, technical dependencies, risks, and decision points.

- Serve as the primary program interface between the Energetics Team and Anduril vehicle teams, aligning what must be delivered, when it is needed, how many units are required, and what changes affect the plan.

- Track requirements across platform and warhead teams, identify gaps or conflicts, and drive the right owners toward timely resolution.

- Translate evolving technical work into clear priorities, milestones, tradeoffs, and commitments for engineering and program stakeholders.

- Anticipate hardware-development constraints—including supplier lead times, fabrication, inspection, integration, test readiness, and production capacity—and incorporate them into realistic schedules.

- Keep rapid prototypes and risk-reduction testing connected to defined program questions, delivery milestones, and broader product outcomes.

- Partner with engineering, Product, Test and Evaluation, Safety, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Production, and program teams to resolve dependencies and maintain alignment.

- Surface schedule, resource, requirements, and execution risks early; frame options and drive decisions before they become delivery failures.

- Create clear program communications, engineering documentation, schedules, cost estimates, risk summaries, and decision records for technical and nontechnical audiences.

- Lead post-test and post-milestone reviews that convert lessons learned into accountable actions and improved execution.

- Help establish practical program-management methods for the growing Energetics portfolio and mentor less-experienced program leaders as the team expands.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- 8+ years experience leading complex hardware-development programs or major workstreams through multiple lifecycle stages, such as concept development, prototyping, procurement, fabrication, integration, testing, or production.

- Experience coordinating several concurrent programs, stakeholder groups, or subsystem teams in a fast-moving R&D or new-product-development environment.

- Working knowledge of hardware-development and manufacturing timelines, with the ability to identify dependencies, build credible schedules, and anticipate downstream risks.

- Experience aligning technical requirements, schedules, resources, risks, and deliverables across teams without relying on direct authority.

- Evidence of bringing structure to ambiguous programs, adapting the level of process to the work, and driving decisions and commitments to closure.

- Ability to communicate technical and program information clearly through written updates, visual plans, reviews, and direct stakeholder conversations.

- Experience preparing engineering or program documentation, project schedules, and cost estimates.

- Ability to travel for program reviews, testing, and customer or partner meetings, including surges up to 25%.

- Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience leading hardware programs in defense, aerospace, space systems, robotics, automotive, advanced manufacturing, consumer hardware, or another high-consequence technical environment.

- Experience supporting munitions, ordnance, energetics, weapons integration, or other complex electromechanical systems.

- Experience managing programs across the full lifecycle, from early R&D through production readiness or scaled delivery.

- Familiarity with requirements tracking, configuration or change management, verification planning, and risk-reduction testing.

- Experience working with suppliers, long-lead hardware, manufacturing constraints, and production ramp decisions.

- Active U.S. security clearance, including DoD Secret or Top Secret, or DOE L or Q.

- Familiarity with Jira, Microsoft Project, Confluence, or similar planning and collaboration tools.

US Salary Range
$167,000 — $222,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits .

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. The department includes procurement, planning and fulfillment, supplier development and quality, logistics, and inventory. Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Maritime Manufacturing Technology Team is responsible for rapidly developing and implementing manufacturing technologies, processes, and materials for cutting-edge defense hardware. The team is developing deployable static and moving surfaces, undersea and sea to air vehicles, and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking our next Technical Program Manager to join our emerging Program Management Office in Santa Ana, CA, working in a cutting-edge start-up environment to advance the state-of-the-possible in subsea robotics. Working across product, engineering, business development, logistics, and operations, you must be a technical leader with the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits.

This role is crucial in ensuring that each initiative aligns with the company's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, balancing innovation with practical execution to drive this novel business line's success. You will be required to learn technical concepts and employ them quickly. You will be expected to use your technical knowledge in conjunction with your program management skills to lead cross-functional efforts and deliver exceptional outcomes.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Technical Ownership : Drive technical outcomes through meticulous understanding of system performance, managing incident response and after-action, using metrics to derive insights into areas for improvement, quantifying the improvements made through investment in those areas, and maintaining a clear understanding of the state of the system that can be communicated to the customer.

- Project Planning : Develop project scope and manage changes through the life of the project. Identify, track, and manage project risks. Generate and maintain project schedules. Ensure successful execution of programs in accordance with desired requirements, on schedule, and on budget.

- New Product Integration : Lead NPI teams to ensure the end-to-end systems integration and manufacturing readiness of new products through to sustained high-rate production ensuring processes, work instructions, test coverage, and tooling are mature enough to rapidly scale complex hardware products. Design, implement, and continuously improve a standardized NPI knowledge transfer framework, including checklists, templates, communication plans, and stage-gate reviews.

- Cross Functional Partnership : Deeply embed with the Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality and Manufacturing teams from early development through the initial production run to gain expert-level product and process knowledge.

- Contract Management : Provide contract management support including statements of work, change orders, financial management, terms and conditions, data rights assertions, etc. Manage deliverables, including routine status updates and final delivery to the customer.

- Autonomous Execution : Autonomously execute on broad and/or ambiguous requirements from internal and external clients. Demonstrate high ownership on all pieces of work. Become a trusted partner to Anduril’s engineers.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- 7+ years of experience specifically in technical project management and/or systems engineering, or related project management and/or systems engineering experience in a relevant industry.

- Demonstrated success leading NPI teams and scaling multiple complex hardware products into high-rate production.

- Hands-on experience with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and Product Data Management (PDM) software.

- Proven track record using first-principles problem-solving to balance aggressive timelines, budgets, and resource allocation in a fast-paced environment.

- Extremely organized and detail oriented with exceptional communication skills.

- Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Direct experience in maritime, naval, or aerospace defense, with knowledge of NAVSEA or MIL-SPEC standards.

- Experience with MES and ERP systems for production and material planning: working with JIRA, Siemens NX, Teamcenter (PLM), or Oracle or equivalents.

- Background in supply chain and/or procurement in a high-rate production environment producing large finished electromechanical goods.

- Hands-on technical credibility having personally built, debugged, or repaired hardware in a production environment, and is comfortable being on the floor with technicians as the default operating mode.

- Technical foundation in mechanical assembly, electrical integration, heavy metal or composite fabrication, or precision machining.

$167,000 — $222,000 USD

raw.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Cross Domain Solutions
raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Connected Warfare Division builds mission-critical systems that enable global command and control for time-sensitive, multi-domain operations. By fusing robotics, sensor networks, and advanced software, we create connected mesh ecosystems that empower our military partners with a comprehensive source of truth for rapid decision-making. Our Mission Command group is at the forefront of delivering software solutions that integrate seamlessly with hundreds of thousands of endpoints worldwide, ensuring operational superiority on a global scale.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Staff Technical Program Manager on the Cross Domain Solutions (CDS) Integration team, you will own the delivery and accreditation of capabilities that allow Lattice to operate securely across classification boundaries. Sitting at the nexus of engineering, vendors, and government authorizing officials, you will navigate complex technical and compliance hurdles to deliver secure, real-time data flows to warfighters in the field.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Drive end-to-end delivery. Own the execution roadmap for integrating Lattice across security domains, ensuring solutions are delivered on time, within scope, and aligned with operational requirements.

- Bridge engineering, compliance, and customers. Act as the technical connective tissue between software engineering, cybersecurity, compliance teams, third-party technology vendors, and customer stakeholders.

- Own assessment and authorization (A&A). Lead the end-to-end security assessment, accreditation, and authorization processes with relevant government Authorizing Officials (AOs) to achieve and maintain Authorizations to Operate (ATOs).

- Lead cross-functional engineering execution. Collaborate closely with internal software, systems, and infrastructure teams to plan, build, integrate, and test functionality.

- Manage strategic technology partnerships. Establish, evaluate, and maintain relationships with third-party hardware and software vendors to meet current demands and scale for future growth.

- Architect for simplicity and scale. Champion engineering decisions that reduce operational complexity and lifecycle costs while building scalable architectures that support future multi-enclave capabilities.

- Ensure rigorous export and security compliance. Partner closely with the Anduril trade compliance and export control teams to ensure all solutions strictly adhere to regulatory and export control requirements.

- Drive disciplined engineering standards. Institute and maintain rigorous engineering, validation, and fielding processes so that deployed solutions are resilient, repeatable, and maintainable in real-world operational environments.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Possess and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility (TS/SCI).

- Demonstrated track record as a Senior or Staff Technical Program Manager, Systems Engineer, or Security Engineer delivering complex IT, networking, or cybersecurity solutions.

- Foundational understanding of computer and network security principles, cybersecurity architectures, threat modeling, and/or defense-in-depth strategies.

- Experience navigating U.S. Government security compliance frameworks (e.g., Risk Management Framework [RMF], NIST SP 800-53, DoDI 8510.01, ICD 503) and driving systems through the ATO process.

- Demonstrated experience managing cross-functional execution across distributed software engineering, infrastructure, and test teams.

- Proven ability to manage technical vendor partnerships, evaluate third-party technologies, and hold external partners accountable to technical milestones.

- Excellent technical communication skills, with the ability to bridge conversations between low-level software engineers, operational military personnel, and senior government authorization authorities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience building, integrating, testing, or authorizing Cross Domain Solutions (CDS) or Multi-Level Security (MLS) architectures within DoD or Intelligence Community (IC) environments.

- Familiarity with National Cross Domain Strategy and Management Office (NCDSMO) requirements and CDS lifecycle processes (Raise-the-Bar standards).

- Experience navigating international export controls, ITAR, and EAR compliance in the context of defense software and security platforms.

- Background in distributed systems, secure cloud environments, and tactical network integration.

US Salary Range
$191,000 — $253,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits .

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

-
No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

- Please always verify communications:

- Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Product Operations Lead to own support delivery for Anduril's Department of Homeland Security accounts, principally U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG). You will manage and mentor a team of Product Operations Technical Specialists while carrying the same technical scope they work daily, setting the standard for how incidents are triaged, root caused, and contained across complex electromechanical systems. You will pair that technical fluency with strong leadership instincts to drive fleet reliability, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence across CBP and USCG deployments, and you should bring an aptitude for debugging and an appetite for real-time response across multiple platforms and organizations. If you are passionate about ground-breaking technology, contributing to the national security mission, and leading a high-performing team at the intersection of technology and sustainment operations, Anduril is interested in speaking with you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Lead the Team: Manage and mentor a team of Product Operations Technical Specialists, owning performance, coaching, and professional development, and set the standard for how the team triages, diagnoses, and resolves incidents.

- Own the Escalation Path: Serve as the escalation point for issues across the DHS accounts, providing expert guidance on the most complex incidents.

- Maintain Operational Readiness: Manage staffing levels and on-call rotations so coverage holds across the DHS accounts.

- Own the Customer Relationship: Act as the point of contact for CBP and USCG product operations, running proactive communications, status briefings, and detail-oriented execution, and coordinating across internal teams to resolve cross-functional issues.

- Sustain the Fleet: Combine an understanding of DHS customers' missions with deep familiarity of our products and system integrations to keep deployed assets healthy, proactively identifying risks to fleet reliability and customer satisfaction.

- Resolve Incidents: Triage, diagnose, and root cause product incidents, managing the ticket queue from intake to closure, and drive postmortem actions including providing status visibility through resolution.

- Improve Observability and Process: Consistently assess and improve the quality of the fleet's observability and telemetry in partnership with product teams, and propose process and product improvements based on customer feedback and available metrics/analytics.

- Maintain Hardware: Perform maintenance on Anduril hardware through the use of Linux command line tools and workflows.

- Build the Playbook: Author and issue product-specific knowledge base articles and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for end-user triaging.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Proven Technical Experience: 4+ years of experience in product operations, technical support, or a similar operational environment, including hands-on support of complex hardware systems, networks, and related technologies.

- Leadership & Mentorship: Demonstrated experience managing, coaching, or mentoring technical team members, with a focus on professional development and operational excellence.

- Problem-Solving Mindset: Strong aptitude for problem solving in unstructured situations at the interface of hardware, software, and networking, and the ability to drive challenging and vague technical problems to clarity and resolution.

- System Ownership: Proven ability to master a technical system and support it in operational environments. Must demonstrate an innate drive to take ownership and be self-sufficient across the depth and breadth of the technical system.

- Communication: Excellent written, visual, and verbal communication skills, comfort briefing senior customer stakeholders, and confidence navigating ambiguity and crafting new ways of doing things.

- Customer Focus: Extremely detail oriented, with a high bar for customer service.

- Clearance: Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

- Travel: Ability to travel as needed to support customer operations and test events.

- Willingness to work non-standard business hours on a rotating shift including weekends and holidays

Join Microsoft Ads as a Principal Technical Program Manager and help shape the systems behind ad delivery at global scale. Ads is a demanding and rewarding engineering domain, with high query volume, tight latency requirements, massive compute and data footprints, and a direct path from engineering improvements to measurable customer and business impact.
A major initial focus for this role will be ads serving runtime and compute-intensive systems, including GPU/CPU inference performance and efficiency. The role also spans the broader Data, Platform and Tools charter across online and offline ads systems, experimentation, metrics, data platforms and pipelines, capacity, developer tooling, and engineering efficiency. We are looking for a versatile technical leader who can quickly develop depth in critical areas, connect work across the end-to-end ads platform.
In this role, you will develop an independent technical point of view grounded in evidence. You will use product requirements, architecture, code paths, production data, logs, experiments, and system behavior to understand complex problems, test hypotheses, identify constraints and trade-offs, and help shape technical direction.
You will turn that understanding into end-to-end execution: framing problems, defining outcomes, aligning engineering and product teams, resolving technical and organizational dependencies, driving implementation and launch, measuring impact, and course-correcting when needed.
You will partner closely with engineering, product, data science, and business leaders across organizations, while identifying systemic opportunities, shaping technical and program direction across teams, and raising the bar for how complex technical initiatives are structured and executed.
Success requires strong technical judgment, curiosity, clear written and verbal communication, ownership, and the ability to earn influence through depth, evidence, and consistent delivery. You are not expected to own every line of production code, but you are expected to understand complex systems end to end, independently find answers, connect decisions across components, challenge assumptions credibly, and drive critical initiatives through to measurable outcomes.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. We build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Responsibilities
* Define and drive the vision, strategy, and measurable outcomes for complex technical programs across the Data, Platform and Tools space.
* Drive improvements in performance, reliability, scalability, capacity, cost efficiency, and operational readiness of high-scale production systems.
* Develop end-to-end understanding across services and online/offline components by reviewing architecture and code paths, analyzing production data and logs, evaluating experiments, and testing hypotheses.
* Form an evidence-based technical point of view, surface trade-offs, and influence engineering and product direction through depth, data, and sound judgment.
* Own complex initiatives end to end — from problem framing and solution definition through alignment, execution, rollout, measurement, and course correction — with accountability for outcomes.
* Define success criteria, metrics, and guardrails; use experimentation, telemetry, and production signals to assess customer, system, and business impact.
* Align engineering, product, data science, and business stakeholders across organizational boundaries, including senior leaders and globally distributed teams.
* Identify and resolve technical, organizational, and execution dependencies and risks; navigate ambiguity and obstacles without losing momentum or lowering the quality bar.
* Communicate program state early and clearly, including progress, risks, misses, trade-offs, and decisions, to both technical and executive audiences.
* Identify systemic opportunities beyond individual initiatives, connect investments across technical areas, and help shape broader technical and program direction.
* Use AI effectively for research, analysis, debugging, system understanding, and program execution while applying appropriate technical judgment and validation.
* Champion a culture of rigor, curiosity, quality, inclusion, and truth-seeking, with decisions grounded in evidence and systems designed for long-term robustness and scale.

Qualifications
Required/minimum Qualifications:
- Bachelor's Degree AND 6+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience building, operating, optimizing, or troubleshooting high-scale ads serving, recommendation, machine learning, data, experimentation, or other distributed systems.
-  Understanding of ads technology and how serving, inference, experimentation, data, identity/privacy, and monetization systems work together.

The Connected Warfare division builds systems to support global command and control missions — joint, time-sensitive, multi-domain, connected mesh ecosystems that bring together hundreds of thousands of endpoints across the globe. raw.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI Factory accelerating energy and compute infrastructure. We are seeking a New Product Introduction (NPI) Engineering Leader in the Spark Business Unit to bridge Spark Hardware Design with enterprise execution.



In this role, “hardware” and “product” refers to the physical infrastructure of the Spark module: structural steel modules, RPPs, DLC cooling loops, CDUs, chillers, piping headers, electrical and mechanical systems, and power distribution gear. Compute hardware (servers, GPUs, storage, networking, and rack specifications) is owned by Cloud Product. Sitting on the Spark Hardware product team, you are the single-threaded owner ensuring the physical module is fully verified for handoff to manufacturing. You gather and lead everything needed to introduce Spark hardware modules into the Crusoe ecosystem, orchestrating the NPI phase-gate process to turn the design team’s output into one complete NPI packet. You don’t run manufacturing. You equip and support Manufacturing and Supply Chain with clean design baselines, complete documentation, and qualified inputs to build at scale.



What You'll Be Working On:
I. Gate Framework & Hardware Release Authority

 - Framework Ownership: Own the Spark hardware NPI framework (Concept to Launch) within the Spark BU to align design engineering progress with enterprise release readiness.

 - Release Authority: Define design release readiness for physical Spark modules. Ensure design freeze and production gates clear only when product specs, subsystem verification tests, and manufacturing handoff criteria are fully met.

 - Design Package Quality: Enforce gate discipline to resolve design, thermal interface, and electrical interference issues in engineering well before drawings and BOMs reach manufacturing, such that manufacturing receives a clean and complete NPI packet.

 - Product Readiness Scorecard: Maintain an objective hardware readiness scorecard (modeled on MRL/PRR standards) providing clear product maturity visibility to leadership and manufacturing.

 - Design Baseline & Change Control: Manage engineering baseline transitions into production. Support ECO/ECN workflows in PLM so Supply Chain and Manufacturing operate against clear, unambiguous release states.

 - Handoff Package Completeness: Deliver complete hardware release packages to downstream teams, including CAD models, structural drawings, electrical single-lines, fluid schematics, multi-level BOMs, and factory acceptance test (FAT) criteria.

II. Enterprise Enablement & Subsystem Integration

 - Cross-Functional Alignment: Translate Spark hardware roadmaps into actionable handoff schedules for Supply Chain, Quality, Manufacturing, and Construction well ahead of production builds.

 - Validation Campaigns: Plan and orchestrate first-of-a-kind (FOAK) prototype builds. Participate on the shop floor during validation runs to feed design-for-manufacturability (DFM) insights back to engineering.

 - Manufacturing Enablement: Partner directly with Manufacturing, ensuring their engineering team has the documentation, assembly instructions, tooling access, and test specs for a smooth line setup.

 - Supply Chain Synchronization: Partner with Supply Chain early to identify long-lead electrical and thermal components, ensuring supplier vetting before design freeze.

 - Subsystem Hardware Integration: Ensure core physical elements (mechanical shells, structural frames, Direct-to-Chip cooling loops, 800V DC distribution, and rack interfaces) are validated as a cohesive package prior to release.

 - Downstream Deployment Handoff: Ensure released packages include clear interface control documents (ICDs) usable by site engineering, civil construction, and commissioning teams.

III. Launch & Continuous Improvement

 - Ramp Support: Partner closely with Manufacturing during initial production ramps to resolve design friction or supply exceptions and protect schedules.

 - Single Source of Truth: Provide executive stakeholders and Spark BU leadership unified visibility into release readiness, subsystem risks, and manufacturing enablement.

 - Closed-Loop Feedback: Lead post-launch reviews following build campaigns to capture field and factory feedback, continually refining release standards for future hardware generations.
   
   

What You'll Bring to the Team:

Education

 - Required: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, or Systems Engineering, or a related physical engineering discipline.

Experience

 - 10 to 15 years in hardware NPI, technical program management, or systems engineering within a physical hardware organization.

 - Direct experience holding release authority and guiding complex hardware programs from concept through transfer-to-manufacturing.

 - Fluent in Level of Development (LOD) frameworks (i.e. LOD 100–400).

 - Proven track record equipping manufacturing, supply chain, and field teams with high-quality release packages.

Technical Depth
NPI & Handoff Methodology: Mastery of phase-gate frameworks, hardware verification, and formal transfer-to-manufacturing processes.

 - PLM & Configuration Management: Expertise in PLM systems, multi-level hardware BOMs, revision control, and structured ECO/ECN workflows.

 - Design for Excellence (DFX): Practical knowledge of DFM, DFA, and DFT principles to optimize design packages for assembly and testing prior to release.

 - Quality & Validation: FMEA, First Article Inspection (FAI), hydrostatic leak testing, and electrical high-pot testing standards.
   
   

Bonus Points

 - Experience with modular, containerized, or prefabricated infrastructure product lines.

 - Familiarity with high-density data center physical requirements (fluid manifolds, heat exchangers, heavy electrical equipment).

 - A collaborative approach combining rigorous design package standards with a commitment to cross-functional empowerment.

raw.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. DATA CENTER ADMIN ISTRATOR

SpaceX is looking for a Sr. Data Center Administrator to help us build and manage our data center infrastructure. As part of our infrastructure team, your responsibility will be the proficient installation and management of server, network, and power systems in our data centers, adhering to best practices to ensure optimal performance. The ideal candidate has experience working with various types of hardware architectures and understands the strengths of each. You will also carry out performance-tuning and quality assurance operations on critical infrastructure components to ensure high level of data quality, availability, and security across the enterprise. In fulfilling this role, you will be expected to collaborate with the team to develop and implement strategies for improved data center operations.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Resolve operational, infrastructure or hardware incidents in multiple data centers.

- Manage complete lifecycle for data center hardware, including deployment, operation, and decommission.

- Physically rack and cable data center equipment.

- Track and logically organize the physical storage of incoming data center equipment.

- Perform quality assurance testing and resolve recurring issues.

- Schedule and track hardware maintenance tasks.

- Update port maps and rack layouts and create operational procedures.

- Monitor the environmental conditions and power/cooling systems of a data center to ensure they are optimum for servers, switches, storage arrays, and other devices.

- Run hardware diagnostics and replace failing parts in a timely manner.

- Upgrade internal system components, including CPUs, memory, and storage.

- Setup and operate common Linux and Windows servers.

- Document processes and keep event logs.

- Work with the purchasing department on the procurement of new data center equipment.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

- Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline and 3+ years of data center experience; OR 5+ years of data center experience in lieu of a degree.

- Professional experience working in a data center or with IT hardware.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

- Certifications related to IT infrastructure such as CompTIA Server+, CompTIA Network+, and CCNP.

- Experience with data center infrastructure management (DCIM), including tools to monitor, measure, manage, and/or control data center utilization.

- In-depth knowledge of data center environments, servers, and network equipment.

- Extensive experience in installing, monitoring, and maintaining data center equipment.

- Linux and Windows OS system administration experience.

- Power and data center cooling capacity planning experience.

- Exceptional analytical and troubleshooting skills.

- Experience working with multiple vendor hardware architectures.

- Experience working with server management tools such as HPE iLO, Cisco CIMC and Dell iDRAC.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

- Willingness to work extended hours and weekends as needed (to respond to network and server errors after hours)

- Ability to pass DOD background check for launch site access.

- Ability to drive (active valid drivers' license).

- To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Air Defense team builds robots that find other robots and knock them out of the sky. At a time when air superiority can no longer be taken for granted, the Air Defense team provides mission critical capabilities to warfighters. From detection to tracking, identification, deterrence, and defeat, our family of networked sensors and effectors enables our customers to rapidly close the kill chain against a broad range of UAS threats. Working across product, engineering, business development, logistics, operations, and mission success, the Air Defense team develops, tests, deploys, and sustains the Anduril Air Defense Family of Systems in challenging operational environments worldwide.

ABOUT THE JOB

As an Air Defense TPM, you must be a technical leader with the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. This role is crucial in ensuring that each initiative aligns with the company's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's success. You will be required to learn technical concepts and employ them quickly. You will be expected to use your technical knowledge in conjunction with your program management skills to lead cross-functional efforts and deliver the best outcome for Anduril and the customer. Deploying our Air Defense capabilities requires thorough understanding of mission requirements, thoughtful orchestration between Anduril teams and external stakeholders, and meticulous planning in the face of ambiguity. You thrive in the unknown and create order out of the chaos.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Stakeholder Engagement: Build and maintain relationships with internal stakeholders, external clients, and industry partners to gather insights, align objectives, and secure buy-in for strategic initiatives. Act as the primary technical liaison for the client, partnering with the account lead to advocate for their needs within the engineering organization and ensuring their feedback directly influences the requirements generation process. Communicate the outputs of these efforts including upcoming software releases, new capabilities, and performance improvement over time.

- Technical Ownership: Drive technical outcomes through meticulous understanding of system performance, managing incident response and after-action, using metrics to derive insights into areas for improvement, quantifying the improvements made through investment in those areas, and maintaining a clear understanding of the state of the system that can be communicated to the customer.

- Strategic Planning and Execution: Translate strategic business goals into actionable project plans, setting clear milestones, and driving initiatives from conception through to successful completion, ensuring they deliver intended outcomes and add value to the business. Oversee the allocation of personnel, budget, and other resources to ensure successful execution of these initiatives.

- Execute Autonomously: Autonomously execute on broad and/or ambiguous requirements from external clients. Demonstrate high ownership on all pieces of work. Become a trusted partner to Anduril’s engineers.

- Enable Cross Team Collaboration: Manage, unblock, and accelerate cross-team projects spanning multiple teams and initiatives. Collaborate closely with other partner teams, such as hardware, product, and test operations as needed.

- Shape Growth Opportunities: Support the drafting of technical proposals, ensuring that potential projects and scaling opportunities with each account are accurately scoped, resourced, and aligned with the organization's capabilities and strategic goals.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Proven customer-facing technical program management and/or systems engineering experience, preferably in the defense, national security, or aerospace domains

- Proven experience leading a technical team of peers to field hardware or software products to real operating environments

- Solid technical aptitude and an ability to understand technical designs, software development lifecycle, challenges and risks; ability to work closely and effectively with engineering teams.

- Ability to work with internal and external stakeholders, across a wide range of technical comfort

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills

- Must be able to obtain a Secret Clearance.

- Experience in rolling out potentially disruptive organizational process changes

- Strong technical, analytical and quantitative skills with the ability to use data and metrics to back up assumptions, recommendations and drive decisions

raw.location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Strategic Defense protects the United States and its allies from ballistic, hypersonic, and air-breathing threats. Those threats now arrive in seconds, maneuver mid-flight, and come in volleys designed to overwhelm the legacy systems meant to stop them — so we're building a software-defined command and control layer that can see, decide, and act faster than any human operator could alone. Our team spans autonomy, tracking, simulation and wargaming, hardware, systems engineering, and test and evaluation to build an accredited fire control system fielded rapidly and at scale.

ABOUT THE JOB

Our team is actively seeking a dynamic and highly motivated Staff Test & Evaluation (T&E) Technical Program Manager (TPM) to quickly integrate into the team. In this role, you will support the Anduril Strategic Defense business line with your technical expertise and foster strategic collaboration across various teams. This includes working closely with program leadership, supporting companies, and government partners. As a valued member of our team, you will play an integral role in testing innovative solutions designed to address real-world challenges. A significant part of your role will involve serving as the government point of contact, coordinating with other capability stakeholders on test objectives, and shaping test scenario requirements to drive Anduril's engineering priorities. This position underscores the importance of an iterative approach to our operations - design, test, field, and refine - thereby driving continuous improvement of our systems and services. As part of a growing T&E team, this role may be asked to support both ground and flight test activities until the full team is in place.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

activities, with a particular emphasis on hardware-in-the-loop lab-based ground tests.

- Coordinate and support execution of testing at private and government owned test ranges to test and evaluate hardware and software systems.

- Deconflict test events internally across Anduril programs and efforts.

- Be responsible for safe operation of all testing efforts, working in accordance with established operating procedures and practices.

- Work closely with Engineering to discuss test results, to include collected data and observations.

- Collect and perform initial test data analysis for the system under test.

- Support the design and implementation of live-virtual-constructive (LVC) test scenarios to stress the system under test without requiring live assets.

- Document test procedures and results, providing detailed reports for engineering teams and stakeholders.

- Conduct testing of classified capabilities in an unclassified setting, working with customer and Anduril security teams to ensure all protocols and security measures are adhered to.

- Integrate T&E processes into the program, ensure adherence throughout the life of the program.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, or a related technical field from an accredited institution.

- Current Top Secret Security Clearance.

- 10+ years of experience in technical program or project management, engineering management, engineering, or comparable skill, preferably supporting testing teams.

- Strong technical background with familiarity in systems engineering and/or software development.

- Must be able to execute the full test engineering process for a System-of-Systems (requirements, test planning, readiness reviews, safety reviews, test execution, test reporting, etc.) with little to no oversight utilizing company test and evaluation policy.

- Experience producing customer facing test deliverables (test plans, test reports, data analysis, etc.) and demonstrated maturity to articulate deliverable to a variety of stakeholders.

- Experience as a test conductor, test director, or similar role while executing testing.

- Experience executing ground test campaigns in hardware and/or software integration lab environments, including stimulus generation and truth system integration.

- Must possess the ability to understand new concepts quickly and solve problems across a variety of engineering areas.

- Must be able to work independently and as part of a multi-disciplinary team to deliver results in a highly ambiguous, fast-paced environment with little to no oversight.

- Experience in C++, Python, or other programming languages for data analysis.

- Familiarity with live-virtual-constructive (LVC) frameworks and simulation environments.

- Experience designing or operating hardware integration lab test benches, including bench fidelity assessment.

raw.title: Senior Global Supply Manager, Sensors and Optics
raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril Imaging builds electro-optical and infrared sensor systems that go on Anduril platforms as well as our own stand-alone products. The hardware is precision optics, cooled infrared detectors, custom electronics, and tight-tolerance electromechanical assemblies. Several products are moving from development into rate production at the same time.

ABOUT THE JOB

Senior Global Supply Manager owns the supply chain outcomes behind those products. The team is small and growing. You will own supplier relationships end to end, from identifying a source and negotiating the agreement to standing up capacity and holding it through a ramp.

This role requires deep understanding of areas in infrared optics and the materials behind them. Germanium crystal, boules, and blanks. Chalcogenide infrared glass. Lens and window fabrication, grinding, polishing, diamond turning, and centering as well as optical coatings. Lens cell assemblies and related optical assemblies. Detector and dewar assemblies, cold filters, and cryocoolers.

This commodity carries additional exposure. Germanium pricing and availability are driven by export policy and a thin upstream supply base, and the alternative material paths carry their own critical mineral dependencies. The work includes reaching past tier one into the feedstock layer, modeling material price scenarios, and structuring forward positions and consignment arrangements that secure supply rather than just placing orders.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own suppliers end to end. Identify and select sources, run requests for quote, drive input to make-buy decisions, and serve as the commercial and technical owner of the relationship. Supplier signals currently reach Anduril through several uncoordinated paths. You will be the conduit that keeps them consistent across programs.

- Negotiate the commercial structure. Draft and negotiate pricing, capacity commitments, lead times, payment, warranty, and service terms. Build toward long-term agreements where they secure capacity. Sequence leverage deliberately so commitments buy terms rather than just parts.

- Build the cost model, then use it. Develop should-cost and clean-sheet models, run cost-breakdown analysis on quotes, and drive total cost of ownership across the lifecycle. Reconcile bill of material cost against finance so product cost reflects what the parts actually cost.

- Secure capacity ahead of ramp. Map supply network lead time and flexibility, place coverage against demand well before it is needed, and resolve capacity gaps before they become schedule problems. Suppliers in this space book out far in advance. The job is to be early.

- Engage engineering before the design locks. Give design for manufacturability feedback, influence specifications using supply intelligence on availability, lead time, and lifecycle health, so design decisions account for supply reality instead of discovering it.

- De-risk the bill of material. Complete risk assessments, qualify alternates and second sources, drive commonality and supplier rationalization, and manage obsolescence before it gates a build.

- Escalate and clear blockers. Participate in program reviews and operational escalation forums. Triage supply disruptions, resolve shortages, and drive supplier issues to conclusion, including executive escalation when it is warranted.

- Carry compliance into the sourcing decision. The Maritime team at Anduril builds world-class autonomous maritime platforms - undersea and surface vehicles and systems and seabed sensors. The team is responsible for taking products like Dive-LD, Dive-XL, Copperhead, and Seabed Sentry from concept to operational systems. As part of this team, your role will involve building the Product Operations function within a larger deployment and sustainment group. We work in close coordination with specialist teams including engineering, program management, and field operations to ensure successful employment of these products and to advance the state-of-the-possible in subsea robotics.

- Experience supporting and/or deploying undersea munitions, vehicles, or unmanned undersea systems (UUVs) as a DoD contractor or military end-user.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We are looking for Global Workplace EMEA Technical Infrastructure Program Manager to join our team!

o   Develop a comprehensive understanding of lab configurations, including slab versus raised floors, cooling methods (air-cooled versus water-cooled), and air and power distribution systems.

o   Partner with global teams to evaluate demand forecasts, utilization trends, and capacity requirements to support strategic decision-making.
o   Provide recommendations based on business priorities, operational requirements, financial analysis, and portfolio objectives.
o   Own regional lab infrastructure coordination, readiness, and operational planning.
o   Coordinate deployments and operational activities involving building technologies and connected systems.
o   Improve consistency, governance, and operational visibility across EMEA labs.
o   Reduce dependency on ad hoc support models and single points of failure.
o   Enable engineering teams to focus on core technical work rather than operational coordination.
o   Develop regional communications, dashboards, and portfolio performance reports.

Industry Trends & Continuous Improvement
Track emerging technologies and best practices in AI-enabled building systems—including energy efficiency, controls, automation, and sustainability—and recommend adoption where it improves reliability or lowers total cost of ownership.
- Benchmark the portfolio’s systems, standards, and practices against industry peers.
- Participate in vendor briefings to stay current on equipment and market trends.
- Help implement new standards, technologies, and approaches across the region and incorporate them into design and specification standards.

- At least 10 years of experience with mechanical or critical building systems (HVAC, chillers, boilers, cooling towers, and BAS/controls) in complex, mission-critical, or multi-site facility environments.
- Experience translating technical business requirements into infrastructure or facility solutions.
- Demonstrated experience managing capital budgets, forecasting, and business case development.
- Direct experience in the design, construction, operation, or maintenance of mechanical and electrical infrastructure, including reading and interpreting construction drawings and specifications and working with AI-enabled building systems.
- Strong troubleshooting and root-cause analysis skills, with the ability to lead responses to critical equipment failures.

The Connected Warfare Division is integrating advanced computing, AI-driven decision-making, and warfighter-centric technology into a single, cohesive ecosystem to revolutionize modern combat. We create joint, time-sensitive, multi-domain, connected mesh systems that serve as the substrate providing the source of truth for critical decisions. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role for someone who wants to be personally in the room for incident calls and switch upgrade planning, not managing from a dashboard

 

What You’ll Be Working On:

 - Maintenance Window Planning & Execution: Own the planning and execution of maintenance windows/production changes for high-availability cloud infrastructure, balancing minimal customer workload disruption against the need for host patching and hardware updates.

 - Incident Management: Coordinate cross-functional response during major incidents or unplanned outages — driving communications, leading post-incident reviews (PIRs), and tracking remediation items through to closure without compromising SLA commitments.

 - Network Switch Upgrades: Support planning for major network switch upgrades and migrations, tracking the hardest dependencies and flagging what's most likely to break before it does.

 - Technical Risk Identification: Catch technical risks in cloud availability programs before the engineering team surfaces them, and know when to solve it directly versus escalate.

 - Vendor & Partner Coordination: Engage directly with hardware/network vendors and Customer Success on high-stakes infrastructure upgrades, keeping customer-facing teams informed through the process.

 - Program Frameworks: Build lightweight, fit-for-purpose execution frameworks for well-scoped availability and reliability programs (e.g., firmware update campaigns) where none exist today.

 - AI-Driven Program Execution: Actively use AI tools to improve risk identification, dependency tracking, and status communication in daily program work.

 - Engineering Credibility: Build trust with an engineering team that hasn't previously worked with a TPM — through technical fluency in maintenance workflows and incident processes, not through imposed process

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

 - Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - 2 to 5+ years of experience as a Technical Program Manager, with direct exposure to cloud infrastructure, availability, or operations environments.

 - Working knowledge of maintenance window planning, host patching, and hardware/firmware update cycles for high-availability systems.

 - Experience with incident management practices: cross-functional incident coordination, post-incident reviews, and remediation tracking against SLA commitments.

 - Familiarity with network switch upgrade or migration planning, including how to identify and track critical dependencies.

 - Demonstrated ability to build basic, lightweight program processes for well-defined initiatives and to know when to escalate versus solve directly.

 - Active use of AI tools in program management work (risk detection, status reporting, dependency mapping), with concrete examples.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills for coordinating incident response and reporting status across technical and customer-facing stakeholders

Bonus Points:

 - Direct experience in GPU or accelerated-computing cloud infrastructure environments.

 - Prior experience partnering with Customer Success or customer-facing teams during infrastructure upgrades.

raw.title: Technical Program Manager, Release & Certification
raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Connected Warfare division builds systems to support global command and control missions — joint, time-sensitive, multi-domain, connected mesh ecosystems that bring together hundreds of thousands of endpoints across the globe. Within Connected Warfare, the Mission Command team builds and operates the software and hardware backbone that other Anduril business lines build on top of: the golden configurations and OS images that ship on every fielded system, and the certification and provisioning pipelines that get hardware out of the factory and into the field. This role owns the mechanics of how a build actually ships and how hardware actually scales.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own the release process for golden configurations and OS images across Menace Management Interface (MMI) and Mission Command's fielded systems — own the calendar, the gates, and the go/no-go call for every release.

- Define and enforce the qualification bar a build has to clear before it ships: test coverage, regression signoff, security/compliance checks, and rollback plan.

- Build and maintain the certification pipeline that qualifies software and hardware builds for factory scaling and provisioning, working with manufacturing, test, and quality to close gaps before they hit the line.

- Partner with engineering to convert one-off releases into a repeatable, auditable process; drive down the manual steps and tribal knowledge required to ship a build.

- Be the point of contact for factory and provisioning teams when a release or certification blocks scaling; triage and drive to resolution.

- Track release health across versions, branches, and fleet, and report status, risk, and blockers to engineering and business-line stakeholders.

- Own the tooling and documentation for the release and certification process, and improve it as the fleet and product surface grow.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. security clearance

- 3+ years as a Technical Program Manager, release manager, or engineer owning software release or hardware qualification processes in an embedded, robotics, or systems environment.

- Direct experience with OS image builds, golden configuration management, or fleet-wide software release processes.

- Comfortable reading test/qualification data and making a go/no-go call under time pressure.

- Experience working across engineering, manufacturing, and quality/test organizations.

- Strong written communication — able to document a release process clearly enough that someone else could run it.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience with hardware certification or provisioning processes in a factory/manufacturing environment.

- Familiarity with embedded Linux, image-based deployment, or configuration management tooling.

- Experience scaling a release process from a small fleet to high-volume production.

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
