raw.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

GLOBAL SUPPLY MANAGER, LOGISTICS

We are a progressive procurement organization pushing the boundaries of traditional procurement reputation and methodologies. We are looking for individuals who can think outside the box to achieve company objectives regarding value and partnerships with our suppliers. Our organization moves quickly, and you must too. SpaceX has the unique ability and desire to influence and shape suppliers to be better with us as we challenge our supply chain on cost, quality and delivery. This individual will support indirect supplier management and SG&A spend reduction initiatives. The purchasing team has aggressive objectives for 2026 that will positively impact our product and bottom line. We are looking for the right person who is equipped and ready for these challenges to join our team.

This role will work closely with SpaceX’s Logistics organization to control costs, mitigate risks, and improve customer experience by maturing cost- and risk-focused strategies with international and domestic parcel couriers, international freight forwarders, domestic freight brokers, warehousing providers, and customs brokers.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Project Management: Responsible for identifying and executing projects to completion including planning, coordinating with stakeholders, and communicating project updates.

- Risk Management: Analyze global supply chain dynamics and market volatility impacting logistics providers; develop procurement strategies like multi-sourcing, diversification, and performance-based clauses to balance cost and risk.

- Contract Management: Responsible for assisting in the authoring of contract documents with the Legal Department. Management of contracts ensuring performance of the supplier to contract obligations. Understand interrelationships between contracts and terms while applying creativity and sound business reasoning to interpret the application of contracts to business needs.

- Negotiations: Negotiate to maximize value and cost savings benefit while lowering risk.

- Supplier Management: Manage preferred supplier relationships for assigned category. Identify areas of need within SpaceX and develop improvement plans with suppliers to meet those needs. Collaborate with Logistics on selection of new suppliers. Create and implement management programs to develop, continuously improve, manage the performance of, and monitor (KPIs) key performance indicators of the supply base that include, but are not limited to on-time delivery, payment terms, cash targets, and cost savings.

- Stakeholder Management: Cultivate partnerships with internal stakeholders (e.g., Logistics, Finance) through clear communication and data-driven insights; advocate for category procurement strategies to ensure alignment and execution on spend initiatives.

- Analysis: Responsible for advanced quantitative analysis to identify financial impacts of decisions and performance for category managed. Perform business process analysis and develop models to improve cost. Collaborate with stakeholders to define SLAs and KPIs for suppliers and measure the appropriate criteria, such as delivery of business results, cost reduction, quality, and timeliness of delivery. Conduct research, perform benchmarking, and gather market analysis for assigned categories.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

- Advanced degree and 4+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; or bachelor’s degree and 6+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; or 10+ years of experience working in one or more of the following:

- Purchasing

- Contract negotiation

- Material or production planning

- Operations or supply chain management

- Material cost control

- Master production scheduling

- 1+ years of experience with SQL and data visualization tools (e.g. Tableau, Power BI, Looker)

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

- Bachelor's degree in supply chain, business, engineering, or a science discipline

- Deep understanding of transportation processes for inbound freight from the port to manufacturing and/or warehouse facilities, air and sea freight

- Experience with carrier cost models, including parcel couriers, freight forwarders, and freight brokers

- Experience with the use/implementation of logistics technology tools including Advance Shipment Notice (ASN) and Transportation Management Systems (TMS)

- Experience with one or more of the following: Python, data mining, data structure, programming

- Exceptional analytical and organizational skills

- Remarkable problem-solving skills

- Ability to prioritize appropriately to meet internal customer and company needs

- Effective written and verbal communication skills, with strong emotional intelligence and the ability to communicate effectively with all levels of internal personnel

- Detail-oriented, self-motivated, and able to respond quickly to a fast-moving and ever-changing environment

- Conducts all activities with the highest integrity

- Ability to prioritize appropriately to meet internal customer and company needs

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

- Willingness to work extended hours and weekends when needed to meet critical deadlines

- This position is based in Bastrop, TX, and requires being onsite full-time – hybrid and remote work will not be considered

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

The Technical Program Manager, Mathematical Software and Algorithms is responsible for overseeing the development, execution, and delivery of the Battlespace Awareness software for critical programs - ensuring it meets all technical, functional, and business requirements. Battlespace Awareness software services comprise advanced algorithms for sense-making and decision-making at tactical timelines.  This role requires an individual with a strong technical background in software development, particularly in the domain of optimization and estimation, and experience managing complex projects with multiple sub-teams and many stakeholders. The Sr Technical Program Manager will be the linchpin in ensuring that the software is developed in line with the objectives defined and is released according to the planned schedule.

- Establish clear objectives and deliverables for the software that align with program needs.

- Documentation and Process Improvement :

- Ensure comprehensive documentation is maintained for the project, including technical specifications, user manuals, and project reports.

- Continuously evaluate and improve project management processes to increase efficiency and effectiveness.

- Ensure that all software releases meet the defined quality standards before deployment.

- Stakeholder Communication :

- Serve as the primary point of contact for all project-related communications, internally across teams and externally with stakeholders.

- Regularly update stakeholders on project status, risks, and milestones through reports and presentations.

- Resource Allocation :

- Assess and allocate necessary resources, including personnel, software, and hardware, to ensure the project is adequately supported.

- Monitor resource utilization and make adjustments as needed to avoid bottlenecks or resource constraints.

- Risk Management :

- Identify potential risks and develop mitigation strategies with the subject matter experts to minimize impact on the project timeline and deliverables.

- Regularly review and update the risk management plan to reflect changes in the project landscape.

- Work with other divisions and departments to ensure software supports the program priorities and meets all integration requirements.

- Facilitate effective communication and collaboration between the Battlespace Awareness business line and other stakeholders to promote a unified approach to program execution.

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.

- Extensive project management experience, preferably in software development.

- Demonstrable understanding of optimization, applied probability, and AI/ML technology.

- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.

- Experience with tools like JIRA, Confluence, and GitHub

- Exceptional verbal and written communication skills.

- Ability to manage high-pressure situations and tight deadlines.

- Must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. security clearance.

- Familiarity and experience working with materiel leadership or mission partners within Army Air & Missile Defense, USMC Ground Based Air Defense, SOCOM, DHS CBP, or allied defense organizations and working knowledge of the counter-UAS and air surveillance competitive landscape.

- Experience working on or alongside a team developing mathematical software, such as optimization solvers, estimation engines, simulation frameworks, or applied probability models.

raw.title: Senior Product Operations Manager
raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Product Operations is the team accountable for the health of the systems and technology that delivers the capabilities our customers depend on. The function identifies, triages, and drives resolution of incidents across the deployed fleet, and converts what is learned in the field into the reliability and sustainment insights that product and engineering teams act upon. We work in close coordination with product engineering, reliability, quality, program management, and field operations teams to maximize capability availability for our end users and inform the next cycle of iterations.

The Maritime and Manuever Dominance (M&MD) teams we support build world-class autonomous robotics platforms, often deployed and operating cooperatively across multiple domains. The team is responsible for taking products like Altius, Ghost, Bolt, Anvil, Omen, Dive-LD, Dive-XL, Copperhead, and Seabed Sentry from concept to operational systems, advancing the state-of-the-possible in multi-asset autonomous robotics.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Senior Manager of Product Operations for Maritime and Maneuver Dominance, you will own product operations across the division's product portfolios and the programs that deliver those products. You will lead multiple Product Operations managers and Product Operations Engineers. Each of whom either leads multiple teams of technical specialists and engineers focused on supporting and improving fielded products, or works closely with product engineers to design in sustainment and customer experience centric feature sets based off of clear VOC Product Operations derived insights. The division's portfolio is scaling, and this role exists to build the support function that scales with it, both for the products it covers first and for the ones that reach the field next.

In this role, you will be building the function as much as operating it, and this work rewards depth. The position requires a strong problem-solving mindset, enough technical depth to follow the work of the engineers and specialists supporting fielded autonomous systems, and the judgment to make decisions with impact that reaches beyond your own organization and the current planning cycle. If you are passionate about cutting-edge technology, advancing national security, and delivering best-in-class operational support services, Anduril invites you to join the team.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Build and Grow the Function: Lead Product Operations across the Maritime and Maneuver Dominance portfolio, managing multiple teams and driving the growth of both sustainment capability and resourcing across the division. Own hiring, performance, development, and organizational design, while also building the function itself: the operating model, the standards, and the capability of the people within it.

Own Service Quality, Internal and External: Hold accountability for the quality of product support delivered to external customers and the quality of VOC signal delivered to internal Anduril product teams. Understand the work at every level of the team, both how it is expected to be done and how it is actually being done, and close the distance between the two.

Scale Support Operations Across the Portfolio: Think strategically about how support scales across the division's full portfolio, current and future. Extend Product Operations coverage to new products and programs as they reach fielded maturity, standing up scope, coverage, escalation paths, and support infrastructure where none exists. All while holding service quality steady as the fielded population grows.

Align Capacity to Demand: Align support headcount demand to measured support volume, fielded asset population, and product delivery schedules. Own annual headcount planning and the function's operating budget for M&MD, and produce defensible demand calculations when planning cycles call for them.

Own the VOC Signal and the fielded product Reliability Loop across the division: Own implementation and measurement of the workflow that converts field failures into structured, high confidence signal for product and reliability engineering teams across the division’s portfolio, spanning failure mode classification, root cause corrective action cycle performance, and recurrence measurement. Ensure adequate partnership and pathways for product aligned teams to abstract individual incidents into systemic improvements, holding engineering partners accountable to the signal provided and your organization accountable to its fidelity.

Set the Support and Sustainment Standard: Establish and enforce the standards by which the organization triages, diagnoses, escalates, and resolves product incidents, including the severity discipline that determines what reaches engineering and when. Build the sustainment approach for complex electromechanical products supporting the evolution of maintenance, spares and hardware action, configuration and calibration management, and the self-service and tooling investments that reduce support burden over time.

Sponsor Function Initiatives: Outline and sponsor the initiatives that mature the function across the business, defining the end state, the measure of success, and the resourcing required. Then hold program management partners accountable for leading and delivering the targeted outcomes.

Be the Interface for Support Requirements: Serve as the point of contact program teams come to when assessing product and customer service support requirements for new and expanding programs. Characterize the cost of the service and define the contract and pricing structures that fund it, in support of proposals and modifications.

Brief Executive Stakeholders: Represent product support to business line and division leadership through recurring reviews of fleet health, reliability trends, sustainment cost, and the maturation of the service. Surface systemic problems with evidence, drive cross-functional prioritization, and help deeply technical teams, program stakeholders, and operators in the field understand each other.

Travel: Ability to travel up to 20% to support customer needs and operations.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Proven Technical Leadership: 8+ years of professional experience managing, mastering, and supporting complex technical systems (maritime, aerospace, robotics, defense, automotive, or other electromechanical domains), including time spent leading the teams that do that work.

- Education: Bachelor's degree in a engineering, business, or other relevant field

- Organizational Leadership: Experience managing managers and leading multi-team organizations, with accountability for outcomes across more than one product line or program, and for the performance and development of the leaders within it.

- Incident Workflow Ownership: Experience owning incident-driven workflows at a standard-setting level, including triage, diagnosis, severity assignment, escalation, and resolution across a fielded fleet.

- Technical Depth: Enough technical depth to follow the work of engineers and specialists supporting fielded robotic and electromechanical systems, including the ability to reason across hardware, software, and networking boundaries.

- Reliability Workflow Familiarity: Demonstrated familiarity with product improvement or reliability lifecycles and processes.

- Sustainment Approach: Experience defining a sustainment model for fielded hardware across its service life, spanning maintenance, spares, and the tooling or self-service investments that reduce support burden.

- Capacity and Cost Modeling: Experience building and defending quantitative models that size support demand, headcount, or cost, including owning annual planning and an operating budget for a function, and stating the assumptions behind the model.

- Program Management: Experience decomposing requirements into deliverables, synthesizing information from several sources into a clear recommendation, and driving that recommendation to a result across multiple functions and teams.

- Executive Influence: Proven ability to align senior cross-functional leadership and influence outcomes without authority over the people who deliver them, including briefing executive stakeholders on operational performance.

- Communication: Excellent written, visual, and verbal communication skills, and confidence navigating ambiguity and establishing new ways of working where none exist.

- Clearance: Active or eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret Security clearance. Holding clearances or background investigations in the past is a plus.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

We recognize that great leaders come from diverse backgrounds. We do not expect you to meet every single one of these criteria:

- Experience establishing a product support or sustainment function from the ground up, including defining the operating model, growing the team, and running remote support operations for complex robotics systems.

- Defense, law enforcement, or other government agency experience leading operational or technical teams.

- Domain knowledge of maritime and/or aviation systems, in a commercial or defense context.

- Consulting or process maturation project experience, and formal training or certification in a continuous improvement or project management discipline (such as Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, Agile, or PMP).

- Fluency with structured root cause methods such as fault tree analysis, fishbone, or 8D problem solving.

- Working knowledge of reliability engineering fundamentals, including failure distributions, mean time between failure and maintenance, and reliability growth.

- Hands-on exposure to the failure behavior of fielded autonomous vehicles, including actuation, power systems, sensing, navigation, and embedded compute, and the ability to diagnose connectivity and networking faults across distributed field systems.

- Enough fluency with fleet data and observability tooling, such as Grafana, Datadog, Jira, SQL, and Palantir Foundry, to interrogate your own organization's analysis.

- Experience translating support scope into contract or pricing structures for operations and sustainment, and familiarity with proposal efforts.

- Fluency with the data layer of sustainment, including incident management systems, asset and configuration data, service bill of materials, and cost association.

- Experience establishing or owning an out-of-hours support capability in a limited risk tolerance environment, including the on-call rotations behind it.

- An active U.S. Secret clearance or higher, prior military service, or a defense and STEM background.

US Salary Range
$147,000 — $196,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits .

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

-
No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

- Please always verify communications:

- Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

- Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com .

-
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

-
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ .

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

Your primary mission is to identify, mitigate, and resolve process bottlenecks and project dependencies, and own knowledge transfers between production sites.

The right person for this role can demonstrate past ownership on solving operational challenges with creative solutions in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. Background in the generation of DFM, DFA, DFX design concepts is an added plus that will increase velocity of knowledge share.

This person will be flexible to provide both solution proposals and support wherever needed to ensure products are built and tested under stringent quality standards. If you are someone who thrives in such an environment, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Own the introduction of configuration management decisions in the production system at Quonset and the follow-on impacts across multiple sites

- Champion the DFM/DFX/DFA of existing production designs into the development pipeline

- Collaborate with leadership on to prevent engineering team scope creep to facilitate the on-schedule release of new and/or improved designs

- Design, implement, and continuously improve a standardized knowledge transfer framework between multiple production sites and multiple new product development site, including checklists, templates, communication plans, and stage-gate reviews.

- Coordinate cross-functional activities, ensuring engineering, supply chain, quality, and production deliverables are completed on time.

- For assigned NPI programs, serve as the primary point of contact of the Quonset site for all knowledge transfer activities.

- Deeply embed with the Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality and Manufacturing teams from early development through the initial production run to gain expert-level product and process knowledge. Lead the effort to capture this knowledge for future transfer.

- Facilitate Cross-Site collaborations by organizing and leading regular communication forums, technical deep dives, and virtual reviews between Engineering and Operations teams at all involved sites, ensuring alignment and de-conflicting issues.

- Mentor and develop key engineers and technicians at receiving sites, empowering them to become self-sufficient subject matter experts for their product lines.

- Proactively break down "not invented here" barriers and foster a company-wide culture of open communication, shared learning, and standardization.

- Manage engineering change workflows (ECR/ECO) affecting manufacturing of transferred technology, including phase-in/out timelines

- Track risks, issues, and actions with mitigation and escalation when needed.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor of Science in Manufacturing Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field.

- 5+ years of progressive experience in a manufacturing or product integration environment, with at least 3 years directly involved in New Product Introduction (NPI).

- Demonstrated experience leading the transfer of a product or process from one manufacturing site to another.

- Deep technical credibility and hands-on experience with modern manufacturing processes and quality systems (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma, AS9100).

- Outstanding communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills; ability to influence and lead teams without direct reporting authority.

- A natural teacher and mentor with a passion for documentation and process improvement.

- Willingness and ability to travel internationally as required.

- Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience in the defense or aerospace industry with a strong understanding of its rigorous quality and documentation requirements.

- Experience administering or architecting knowledge management systems (e.g., Confluence, SharePoint, PLM).

- Experience working with international teams and navigating cultural differences.

raw.title: Quality Inspector, Data Center (Starlink)
raw.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

QUALITY INSPECTOR, DATA CENTER (STARLINK)

SpaceX is on a mission to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. We are building some of the world’s most technically advanced facilities and data centers, which demand rigorous control of nonconforming hardware so vendor defects do not impact installation, operations, or uptime.

As a Quality Inspector supporting the data center Supplier Quality Specialist (SQS) team, you will own day-to-day Material Review Board (MRB) operations at Memphis data centers. You will review hardware flagged by site operations, confirm failures through coordinated or hands-on testing, document nonconformances with complete trace information, submit RMAs, and get parts packaged and shipped back to the vendor so the SQS team can focus on supplier performance, containment strategy, and corrective action.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Own day-to-day MRB operations at Memphis data centers: intake of nonconforming hardware, proper labeling and segregation, designated storage, inventory accuracy, and timely disposition.

- Review hardware flagged by site operations; verify the reported condition, confirm identification (P/N, S/N, location, ticket), and ensure the unit is held, documented, and dispositioned before it re-enters service or inventory.

- Coordinate functional and network testing with network engineers, or perform tests yourself when qualified, to confirm failures prior to RMA.

- Compile supporting documentation (photos, serials, logs, test results, tickets, and packing details) and submit RMA / return-to-vendor requests.

- Package nonconforming parts for return to vendor and coordinate outbound shipment, including paperwork, labeling, and pickup/carrier handoff.

- Verify trace information on nonconforming units and ensure nonconformances are documented completely (part number, serial number, date code/lot, location, failure description, and associated ticket IDs).

- Ensure nonconforming parts remain labeled and stored properly in MRB, that aging holds are actioned in a timely manner, and that stalled items are escalated to the data center SQS.

- Partner with the data center Supplier Quality Specialist on containments, vendor communications, and the data needed for root cause and corrective/preventive action.

- Maintain accurate records in issue-ticket and quality systems; keep MRB status visible to operations, supply chain, and SQS stakeholders.

- Support quality management system policies and procedures for nonconforming material control; identify process gaps and help close them.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

- High school diploma or equivalency certificate.

- 2+ years of experience in quality inspection, receiving inspection, warehouse/MRB, electronics repair/RMA, data center operations, or a related hardware-handling role.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

- Solid computer skills in Microsoft Word, Outlook, and Excel.

- Experience documenting nonconformances and working in ticket, ERP, WMS, or RMA systems.

- Experience packaging, labeling, and shipping returns (RMA / RTV), including ESD and fragile-hardware handling.

- Familiarity with data center hardware (servers, switches, NICs, racks, PDUs, cooling components, or related infrastructure).

- Comfort coordinating or performing basic hardware/network tests (link, ping, POST, visual/LED indicators, or vendor diagnostic utilities) with network or site engineering support.

- Understanding of ISO 9001 / AS9100 quality management systems and nonconforming material control.

- Strong attention to detail on serial-number traceability and documentation completeness.

- Clear written and verbal communication; able to work cross-functionally with site ops, network engineering, supply chain, and SQS.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

- This position is based in Memphis, TN and requires being onsite at data center facilities. Remote work not considered.

- Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted.

- Must be able to stand, walk, bend, and work in a data center environment for extended periods (hot/cold aisles; PPE as required).

- Willingness to work overtime and weekends when needed to meet critical deadlines.

- Travel between Memphis-area data center sites as needed, other SpaceX sites, and potentially suppliers.

Job Details:

Job Description:
The Supply Chain Planning Operations (SCPO) organization is seeking an AI Software Architect to serve as the SCPO AI Lead.
This is a founding technical leadership role embedded within supply planning operations. The role will define and execute the AI strategy for connecting planning and execution data, detecting emerging supply, flagging demand and product risks, and enabling planners and leaders to act on trusted, explainable insights.

The Supply Chain Planning Operations (SCPO) AI Lead will architect and build the intelligent stitching and alerting layer across Plan of Record (POR), Long Range Planning (LRP), Sales and Operations Planning (SnOP), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and other supply chain related data.

The role will convert fragmented data from multiple sources and manual reconciliation into production capabilities that continuously monitor supply execution, identify likely failures, explain the drivers, and guide timely intervention.

The successful candidate will deliver production solutions used in operational decisions, work directly with planners, and establish the technical foundation and engineering practices for SCPO. Please note that this is not a research-only or advisory role.

The SCPO AI Lead is responsible for, but not limited to:

- Define the SCPO AI and data intelligence strategy, architecture, roadmap, and standards in alignment with supply-chain priorities and measurable business outcomes.
- Architect and operationalize a trusted data stitching layer across POR, LRP, SnOP, ERP, and other planning data sources, including lineage, controls, reconciliation, and data-quality monitoring and governance.
- Develop production machine-learning and AI capabilities for time-series analysis, anomaly detection, root-cause identification, supply-risk sensing, and early warning of execution failures.
- Integrate AI outputs with enterprise planning systems and operational workflows using reliable APIs, data pipelines, monitoring, access controls, and override mechanisms.
- Build agentic workflows that automate recurring analyses, evidence gathering, exception triage, and narrative generation while maintaining human-in-the-loop controls, auditability, and appropriate governance.
- Develop scenario and sensitivity capabilities that evaluate supply disruptions, demand changes, yield shifts, capacity reallocations, material constraints, and other operational decisions across planning horizons.
- Create explainable alerts and decision-support experiences that show what changed, why it matters, the level of confidence, and the recommended next action.
- Map the planning-system ecosystem, data flows, manual intervention points, process breakpoints, dependencies, and failure modes; prioritize automation and guardrails based on business risk and value.
- Partner with supply planning, demand planning, manufacturing, foundry, procurement, finance, data engineering, information technology, and business teams to translate operational problems into scalable technical solutions.
- Establish MLOps and software-engineering practices for model versioning, testing, deployment, observability, retraining, documentation, security, and responsible AI governance.
- Communicate technical findings, model limitations, risk signals, architecture decisions, and business recommendations clearly to planners, technical partners, senior managers, and executives.
- Operate with intellectual rigor in ambiguous environments where data, systems, and requirements are incomplete or evolving.
- Commitment to explainability, responsible AI, human oversight, security, and governance for decisions with material financial or operational consequences.

Initial success measures include:

- Within 90 days: define the target stitching architecture, data ownership model, prioritized use-case roadmap, and deploy an initial live reconciliation capability.
- Within 6 months: deploy an explainable alert that detects a material supply-execution risk early enough to support intervention.
- Within 12 months: demonstrate sustained planner adoption, measurable reduction in manual reconciliation, and operational decisions informed by trusted alerts and scenarios.

- Advanced communication skills to tailor complex technical content for engineering, planning, and executive audiences.
- Tolerance for responsible experimentation, including disciplined learning from approaches that do not succeed.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits .

Program Overview

Through the 30-month Supply Chain MBA Development Rotational Program, you will rotate through positions in   Purchasing/Sourcing, Project/Program Management, and Supplier Account Management over the course of 18 months, then apply your learnings to a “Final Placement” role for an additional 12 months.   The Final Placement role may be, but is not limited to, a Materials Project Manager or Supplier Business Manager role. Assignment of Final Placement roles will be based on business need, role availability, and the individual assessments of candidates’ performance and skills displayed during their rotations.   I n the program, participants develop and refine the technical and business skills required to be successful in the Supply Chain organization. You will experience a blended learning environment which includes mentorship, job shadowing, and expanded networking opportunities with leaders and within our Employee Resource Groups such as the Young Professionals Network (YPN).  Participants will have the opportunity to gain high level visibility and create significant impact within a global manufacturing organization.

Position Details

During a series of rotations, participants will take on full-time responsibility of their functional role, which  may  include :

- Issuing RFQs, analyzing proposals, negotiating prices, executing orders, and ensuring delivery in support of New Product Integration/Commercialization manufacturing requirements.

- Developing strategies to  procure  components at the lowest cost consistent with consideration of quality, reliability of source, and urgency of need.

- Previous  experience in Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Manufacturing, Project Management a plus

- Certifications: Six sigma green belt, APICS CPIM, APICS CSCP, PMP a plus

- Flexible and  adaptable  mindset  who thrives in a results-driven culture

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 


Job Description:
The Staff Data & Analytics Engineer, Domain Enablement is a senior, hands-on role responsible for enabling complex business domains on Shield AI’s enterprise data platform. 
This person will lead discovery, scope high-value data and analytics opportunities, and deliver governed data products that make operational data more usable, trustworthy, and scalable for business decision-making. The role works across the data stack—from understanding source systems and defining integration needs through transformation, modeling, semantic design, quality controls, documentation, and business consumption. 
The initial focus for this role is Supply Chain and Manufacturing, including the systems, processes, and data required to support planning, procurement, suppliers, materials, inventory, production, quality, fulfillment, cost, and program operations. Over time, the role may expand to support other complex domains as enterprise priorities evolve. 
This is not a dashboard-development role. The Staff Data & Analytics Engineer will establish the domain data foundations and technical direction needed to deliver durable data products and accelerate future use cases. The ideal candidate combines strong technical depth with the ability to work directly with business partners, clarify ambiguity, and turn complex operational needs into practical, staged solutions. 

What you'll do:
- Lead discovery and end-to-end enablement for complex Supply Chain and Manufacturing domains initially, with flexibility to support other priority enterprise domains as business needs evolve.

- Partner directly with Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Operations leaders to understand business processes, decisions, source systems, reporting needs, metrics, and pain points; collaborate with Finance, Program Finance, Engineering, IT, Security, and other partners where processes, systems, or data intersect.

- Translate ambiguous business needs into clear problem statements, prioritized use cases, phased roadmaps, technical designs, and achievable delivery plans.

- Design and build governed data products across the data stack, including source-system assessment and integration requirements; Bronze, Silver, and Gold data assets; transformation logic; domain marts; curated datasets; semantic models; testing; documentation; and production-readiness controls.

- Define canonical domain concepts, grain, facts, dimensions, conformed entities, historical treatment, business rules, and reconciliation approaches for high-value operational and analytical data.

- Design and deliver governed Supply Chain and Manufacturing data models and analytical assets for concepts such as parts, materials, suppliers, purchase orders, demand, supply, inventory, work orders, production, quality, cost, and fulfillment, aligned to established enterprise patterns and standards.

- Work across ERP, PLM, MES, MRP, procurement, manufacturing, quality, inventory, supplier, finance, and operational systems to create integrated and understandable data products.

- Develop and optimize transformation pipelines using Databricks, SQL, Python, PySpark, Delta Lake, and related technologies as appropriate.

- Apply enterprise ingestion, modeling, naming, semantic, quality, documentation, lineage, and promotion standards across Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers; identify where those standards need to evolve to support complex operational domains.

- Partner with Data Engineering, Platform Engineering, and Data Governance to apply shared standards and establish the ingestion, reliability, security, access, lineage, metadata, stewardship, and quality controls needed for domain data products.
Required qualifications:
- 8+ years of experience in data engineering, analytics engineering, BI engineering, data architecture, or a blended data role.

- Demonstrated experience independently delivering end-to-end data and analytics solutions—from source-system discovery and integration through governed, business-consumable data products.

- Strong experience in at least one complex operational domain, such as Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Procurement, Planning, Logistics, Operations, Industrial, or Program Management.

- Strong dimensional modeling and semantic design skills, including facts, dimensions, grain, conformed dimensions, historical treatment, and auditable business logic.

- Hands-on production experience with Databricks, including Bronze, Silver, and Gold lakehouse patterns, Delta Lake, SQL, and Python and/or PySpark.

- Experience operating in controlled, export-sensitive, government, defense, or security-sensitive environments.

- Experience integrating data from complex enterprise systems, such as ERP, PLM, MES, MRP, procurement, inventory, supplier, quality, production, or financial systems.

- Ability to translate ambiguous business needs into practical delivery scopes, technical designs, and prioritized roadmaps.

- Strong communication skills and comfort partnering directly with business and technical stakeholders.
Preferred qualifications:
- Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, autonomous systems, robotics, advanced manufacturing, industrial operations, or similarly complex and regulated environments.

- Experience supporting Supply Chain or Manufacturing capabilities such as demand planning, supply planning, procurement, supplier performance, inventory and materials management, production, quality, maintenance, repair, or fulfillment.

- Experience with systems such as SAP, Oracle, IFS, Deltek, Costpoint, PLM, MES, MRP, SCM, or comparable enterprise platforms.

- Experience integrating operational measures with Program Finance, cost, inventory valuation, forecasting, planning, or program-performance reporting.

- Experience operating in controlled, export-sensitive, government, defense, or security-sensitive environments.

Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.

What We Offer

Salary:
$84,000.00 - $115,500.00
Location:
Billerica,MA
You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits .

What You'll Do
This posting is for a Billerica, MA-based New Product (NPI) instructor. This position is a combination technical instructor and technical expert role on existing and new products. The position is embedded in the business unit (BU) in Billerica in order to learn the new PLC/NPI products (i.e. the new chambers, new mainframes, and new tools) for the BU, gain experience on the startup and sustaining production tasks on the tool, and develop/deliver initial classroom and hands-on training on the tool. Once the tool transitions to volume production, the NPI instructor will train up the volume instructor, who then takes over the product from a training ownership standpoint.

Due to the scheduling of PLC/NPI product development, the NPI instructor will often be researching, gaining knowledge/experience, and developing/delivering for several new tools/chambers at a time, so project management, training/presentation experience, and technical experience (mechanical, electrical, etc.) of semiconductor equipment is required.

Basic breakdown of time is:
~45% learning the new tool and gaining knowledge and experience (mechanical, electrical, software, process, etc.) and developing the course materials, structure and updating of existing courses
~35% delivering training or coordinating structured factory OJT
~20% other activities

Role Responsibilities
- Conducts semiconductor equipment training needs assessment by collecting information pertaining to work procedures, work flow, and functional knowledge from the experts; understanding job-specific functions and tasks; maintains product technical knowledge sufficient to prepare and present defined product courses; disseminates new information to training and business unit staff

- Communicates with product groups to obtain current product information for course updates; manages multiple projects of diverse scope and complexity; directs project team members. Represents AGS TS at divisional meetings, external conferences and industry task force activities

- Determines system utilization requirements by researching and testing systems

- Utilizes Technical Publications and System Product Business Groups to maximize technical documentation efficiencies; occasionally develops customized training materials per customer needs; trains others in standard course development process/Instructional System Design (ISD); ensures the correct revisions of product  procedures and schematics; identifies and corrects procedural issues with the business unit

- Lead NPI training development projects with minimal support; develops hardware training student guides by identifying and describing information needs; using basic desktop publishing (PowerPoint and Word); submitting initial versions for review; revising and editing final copy

- Maintains safe and healthy training environment by following organization standards and legal regulations; Provides technical expertise and troubleshooting skills to assist with system repairs; ensures system functionality can support course objectives; ensures all safety retrofits are installed on the training systems

- Presents technical training in house and at customer sites; conducts training classes by presenting job-specific classroom and hands-on learning environments and opportunities; manages classroom/lab activities to ensure fulfillment of course objectives; presents and practices safety per procedure; may train during off shift and/or weekends as assigned; actively certifies others; establishes new certification requirements; Evaluates training by evaluating effectiveness of training to specific job applications

- Provides coaching and leadership to other instructors; serves as mentor to less senior instructors for class delivery, technical development and certification; anticipates, prevents and resolves customer satisfaction issues.

- Ensures operation of equipment by completing preventive maintenance requirements; following manufacturer's instructions; troubleshooting malfunctions; calling for repairs; maintaining equipment inventories; evaluating new equipment and techniques

- Maintains quality service by establishing and enforcing organization standards; demonstrates knowledge and understanding of the AGS Training Services organization and operations and the AGS organization; informs customers of additional AGS TS courses/products available; assists Marketing in building customer relationships and selling AGS TS products; analyzes customer issues/needs to determine future training opportunities; deliver training solutions for customer needs

- Maintains technical and instructional knowledge by attending educational workshops, reviewing publications, etc.

- Contributes to team effort by accomplishing related results as needed

- Will require both domestic and international travel (up to 40%).

Tool Specific Required Experience:
- P500, Stratus and Apollo

Qualifications
- Bachelor degree in engineering, education, or training, PLUS 4 years of professional semiconductor equipment experience in installation, programming, safety, maintenance, operation, troubleshooting, and repair of semiconductor machinery equipment (such as robots, programmable controllers, power supplies, pneumatics, vacuum systems, power distributions, facilities, high voltage systems, high current systems, and robot controllers), following manuals, specifications, blueprints, and schematics, and using hand tools, measuring instruments, and testing equipment

- Excellent communication, presentation, problem solving, teamwork and interpersonal communication skills; Resourceful, able to work and learn independently where necessary; Highly self-motivated and dedicated professional

- Presentation skills, written communication, training delivery, project/information management, self-development, presenting technical information, self-confidence, dealing with complexity, Microsoft Office skills

- Equipment use: office equipment, power supplies, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, volt meters, soldering irons, hand tools, power tools, and personal computers

- Semiconductor equipment skills: operations, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, alignments, calibrations, and system-level troubleshooting skills on analog/digital electronics

- Knowledge of MS Windows applications and computer networking a plus

- Experience in e-Learning a plus

- Experience in videography and photography a plus

Yes, 50% of the Time

HPE’s acquisition of Juniper Networks is one of the most significant moves in the company’s history, bringing two networking leaders together to build HPE Networking, with the ambition of creating the best networking business on the planet. This role sits at the center of that effort as part of the Lead-to-Cash (L2C) program, responsible for unifying quoting, ordering, and fulfillment across the combined HPE and Juniper networking portfolios onto a single platform, replacing fragmented legacy systems with one seamless, scalable experience for sellers, partners, and customers worldwide.

As part of a fast-moving, multi-year transformation, the team will stabilize near-term operations, migrate core platforms, onboard   businesses   and suppliers globally, and build new capabilities from the ground up. The choices made here will shape how the combined networking business   operates   for years to come. You will work closely with business leaders, IT architects, suppliers, and partner stakeholders on a program with direct executive visibility, solving integration challenges at a scale few companies ever   attempt .

For the right person, this is a rare opportunity to help build a new business unit from its earliest days, rather than inherit someone else’s systems. You will gain hands-on exposure to enterprise-scale platform integration and cross-functional program leadership, with the kind of complexity and pace that can accelerate your career. If you want your work to have a visible impact on a company making a significant investment in its future, this is where that happens.

Workstream-Specific Details

The Supplier Onboarding Lead   is responsible for   orchestrating the onboarding of manufacturing suppliers and trading partners to HPE’s supply chain network. This role requires deep   expertise   in high-tech manufacturing processes, supply chain management, and SAP S/4HANA integration. The candidate will enable seamless B2B transactions through industry-standard protocols such as EDI, XML, APIs, ensuring partners meet HPE’s operational and compliance standards. Typical transactions may include purchase orders, order acknowledgments, advance ship notices, invoices, inventory updates, and other supply-chain documents. EDI-to-SAP integration commonly supports automated processing of purchase orders, shipping notices, invoices, and acknowledgments while   maintaining   data integrity and business-rule validation. This role is key to HPE's digital transformation initiatives in supplier management and autonomous supply chain operations.

Responsibilities

- Lead the onboarding process for manufacturing partners, ensuring alignment with HPE’s global supply chain strategies and quality standards.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Supply Chain Operations, Manufacturing, IT,   finance   and Business Development to gather requirements and   facilitate   onboarding.

- Manage end-to-end integration setup, focusing on enabling B2B transactions via EDI, XML,   APIs   and other industry standards, leveraging HPE’s integration frameworks.

- Gather and document business requirements for B2B transactions, including purchase orders, order acknowledgments, advance ship notices, invoices, inventory transactions, and master-data exchanges.

- Ensure integrations align with SAP S/4HANA business processes, relevant SAP modules, SAP IDocs, APIs, and approved integration architecture.

- Deploy and oversee agentic AI systems that autonomously manage supplier assessments, intelligent issue resolution, and dynamic workflow adaptation.

- Develop comprehensive onboarding documentation, integration configurations,   playbook   and process workflows aligned with HPE’s standards.

- Ensure compliance with HPE’s security, data privacy, and operational policies throughout the onboarding lifecycle.

- Drive continuous improvement in onboarding processes,   leveraging   industry best   practices   and HPE’s digital transformation initiatives.

- Act as a subject matter expert on supply chain and manufacturing technology, providing guidance and support to partners and internal teams.

- Monitor onboarding progress, resolve issues proactively, and   report on   key metrics to stakeholders. Enable autonomous supplier data validation, compliance verification, and quality standard assessment through agentic AI workflows.

- Identify   opportunities for process improvements using AI-generated insights, process mining analytics, and agentic recommendations.

- Experience with solutions in SAP for order fulfillment/Supply chain function.

- Experience in Logistics execution: Shipping (Delivery processing, Picking, Packing, Goods Issue, Printing and Communication in Shipping), Scheduling, Outbound Delivery, Stock Transport Orders (STO), Shipment Processing and Route Determination.

- Deep understanding of SAP S/4HANA architecture, particularly supply chain and   logistics   modules (MM, SD, LE, GR/IR processes).

- Business

- Manufacturing

- Supply Chain

- Engineering

- 5+ years of experience in global supply chain, ODM/CM management, or electronics manufacturing, with a focus on compute servers and networking hardware

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

raw.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Cross Domain Solutions
raw.location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
raw.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Connected Warfare Division builds mission-critical systems that enable global command and control for time-sensitive, multi-domain operations. By fusing robotics, sensor networks, and advanced software, we create connected mesh ecosystems that empower our military partners with a comprehensive source of truth for rapid decision-making. Our Mission Command group is at the forefront of delivering software solutions that integrate seamlessly with hundreds of thousands of endpoints worldwide, ensuring operational superiority on a global scale.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Staff Technical Program Manager on the Cross Domain Solutions (CDS) Integration team, you will own the delivery and accreditation of capabilities that allow Lattice to operate securely across classification boundaries. Sitting at the nexus of engineering, vendors, and government authorizing officials, you will navigate complex technical and compliance hurdles to deliver secure, real-time data flows to warfighters in the field.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Drive end-to-end delivery. Own the execution roadmap for integrating Lattice across security domains, ensuring solutions are delivered on time, within scope, and aligned with operational requirements.

- Bridge engineering, compliance, and customers. Act as the technical connective tissue between software engineering, cybersecurity, compliance teams, third-party technology vendors, and customer stakeholders.

- Own assessment and authorization (A&A). Lead the end-to-end security assessment, accreditation, and authorization processes with relevant government Authorizing Officials (AOs) to achieve and maintain Authorizations to Operate (ATOs).

- Lead cross-functional engineering execution. Collaborate closely with internal software, systems, and infrastructure teams to plan, build, integrate, and test functionality.

- Manage strategic technology partnerships. Establish, evaluate, and maintain relationships with third-party hardware and software vendors to meet current demands and scale for future growth.

- Architect for simplicity and scale. Champion engineering decisions that reduce operational complexity and lifecycle costs while building scalable architectures that support future multi-enclave capabilities.

- Ensure rigorous export and security compliance. Partner closely with the Anduril trade compliance and export control teams to ensure all solutions strictly adhere to regulatory and export control requirements.

- Drive disciplined engineering standards. Institute and maintain rigorous engineering, validation, and fielding processes so that deployed solutions are resilient, repeatable, and maintainable in real-world operational environments.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Possess and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility (TS/SCI).

- Demonstrated track record as a Senior or Staff Technical Program Manager, Systems Engineer, or Security Engineer delivering complex IT, networking, or cybersecurity solutions.

- Foundational understanding of computer and network security principles, cybersecurity architectures, threat modeling, and/or defense-in-depth strategies.

- Experience navigating U.S. Government security compliance frameworks (e.g., Risk Management Framework [RMF], NIST SP 800-53, DoDI 8510.01, ICD 503) and driving systems through the ATO process.

- Demonstrated experience managing cross-functional execution across distributed software engineering, infrastructure, and test teams.

- Proven ability to manage technical vendor partnerships, evaluate third-party technologies, and hold external partners accountable to technical milestones.

- Excellent technical communication skills, with the ability to bridge conversations between low-level software engineers, operational military personnel, and senior government authorization authorities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience building, integrating, testing, or authorizing Cross Domain Solutions (CDS) or Multi-Level Security (MLS) architectures within DoD or Intelligence Community (IC) environments.

- Familiarity with National Cross Domain Strategy and Management Office (NCDSMO) requirements and CDS lifecycle processes (Raise-the-Bar standards).

- Experience navigating international export controls, ITAR, and EAR compliance in the context of defense software and security platforms.

- Background in distributed systems, secure cloud environments, and tactical network integration.

US Salary Range
$191,000 — $253,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits .

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

-
No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

- Please always verify communications:

- Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

- Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com .

-
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

-
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ .

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

raw.title: Senior Technical Program Manager I, Security and Compliance, Google Cloud
raw.description:
A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Technical Program Manager at Google, you’ll use your technical expertise to lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish. You’ll work with stakeholders to plan requirements, identify risks, manage project schedules, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. You're equally comfortable explaining your team's analyses and recommendations to executives as you are discussing the technical tradeoffs in product development with engineers.

The Google Distributed Cloud (GDC) TPM Team leads cross-functional engineering execution for Google's sovereign, air-gapped (GDCag), and connected (GDCc) edge cloud platforms serving public sector, defense, intelligence, and regulated enterprise customers globally.
As the Security and Compliance Technical Program Manager (TPM) across GDCag and GDCc, you will partner with Security Engineering, Product Management, Operable Component (OC) Tech Leads, and Cloud CISO/Compliance teams to drive GDC's security and accreditation roadmap. You will lead high-priority horizontal security mandates—including Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Migration (CNSA 2.0 / NIST SP 800-208), continuous vulnerability and CVE remediation SLAs, and automated SecAssure compliance controls—while orchestrating US Government (IL5/IL6, FedRAMP High, NIAP) and commercial/sovereign regulatory certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI-DSS) from architectural scoping through audit readiness and release sign-off.
Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $192000 - $278000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google .

- Own and drive cross-functional security and compliance roadmaps across GDC Air-Gapped (GDCag), GDC Connected (GDCc), and Gemini on GDC Connected (GGC) to unlock sovereign, defense, and regulated enterprise accreditations (IL5/IL6, FedRAMP, FIPS).

- Operationalize shift-left security and compliance gates across the software and hardware release lifecycle, delivering master execution plans, dependency maps, risk registers, and executive readiness reviews.

- Partner with engineering and security architects across the full GDC tech stack: bare-metal servers, GPU/AI serving infrastructure, Kubernetes/GKE, Linux OS, networking, storage, KMS/HSMs, IAM, and zero-trust boundary controls.

- Drive cryptographic modernization, continuous vulnerability management (CVE/SBOM), and secure software/firmware supply chain workflows tailored for disconnected and hybrid topologies.

- Align Engineering, Security, Compliance, Product, and Operations (SovOps) stakeholders to resolve complex technical trade-offs and ensure predictable, audit-ready customer releases.

Minimum qualifications:

- Bachelor's degree in a technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

- 8 years of experience in program management.

- Experience with security assessment.

- Experience with security controls.

Preferred qualifications:

- 8 years of experience managing cross-functional or cross-team projects.

- Experience guiding cloud, infrastructure, or enterprise products through regulatory compliance assessments, audit readiness, and continuous compliance monitoring (including DoD IL5/IL6, FedRAMP High, NIST, ISO, or regional data sovereignty frameworks).

- Experience operating within cleared national security environments with active US Government security clearance.

- Experience leading vulnerability assessment and management programs (scan coverage, triage, remediation tracking, and exception governance) across large-scale software or hardware environments.

- Experience embedding shift-left security assessments (such as secure-by-design reviews, pen testing, or cryptographic modernization) into the product lifecycle, and relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCSP).

Technical Program Manager - Software Engineering

This role has been designed as 'Hybrid' with a requirement that you will work on average 2 days per week from an HPE office.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. raw.title: Senior FP&A Analyst - Data Center Finance

raw.description:
Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.



*Note: This position requires presence in our San Francisco, San Jose, or Bellevue office location 4 days per week; Lambda’s designated work from home day is currently Tuesday.


About the Role

As a member of the DC / Infrastructure Finance team, you will report to the Manager of DC / Infrastructure Finance and partner with Data Center Development, Data Center Operations, and Program Operations. You will maintain visibility into site costs, cash requirements, and investment performance from development through deployment and operations, helping leaders manage budgets, evaluate tradeoffs, and deliver capacity efficiently.

 

What You'll Do

Data Center Development Budgets

 - Build and maintain project budgets for data center construction, site improvements, power and cooling infrastructure, and commissioning in partnership with project owners

 - Track actual costs, contractor commitments, change orders, and remaining scope against approved budgets; maintain estimates to complete and forecast total project costs

 - Evaluate contingency usage and changes in scope or schedule, flag potential overruns, and recommend corrective actions

Deployment Timing and Cash Forecasting

 - Translate construction milestones, contractor payment schedules, and commissioning plans into project cash forecasts

 - Model the financial impact of delays, phased deployments, and changes in capacity readiness; coordinate equipment assumptions with Supply Chain Finance

 - Own site and construction payment forecasts as inputs to the consolidated cash forecast for Corporate FP&A and Treasury, clearly separating changes in total cost from changes in payment timing

Data Center Operating Costs

 - Own site operating cost forecasts and budget versus actual analysis across power, colocation, rent, maintenance, and other infrastructure costs

 - Build driver-based models using contracted capacity, energized capacity, deployed GPUs, power consumption, and operating assumptions

 - Explain cost and margin variances caused by deployment ramps, power rates, capacity utilization, and contract terms; identify opportunities to improve efficiency

Investment Economics and Performance

 - Support financial evaluation of new sites, expansions, and infrastructure commitments, including project returns, payback, and sensitivity analysis

 - Analyze capital cost per MW, operating cost per GPU hour, and other site economics using consistent cost definitions and assumptions

 - Own site-level models for investment committee reviews and post-investment assessments, incorporating equipment cost inputs from Supply Chain Finance and comparing project costs, deployment timing, and operating performance with approved investment assumptions

Planning and Accounting Partnership

 - Develop site and project inputs for the annual operating plan, quarterly forecasts, and long-range infrastructure plan

 - Partner with Accounting on accrual inputs, cost coding, and lease accounting (ASC 842) inputs to improve the accuracy of project and operating cost reporting

 - Own facility in-service timing, from construction in progress to placed in service, as an input to the infrastructure depreciation forecast

 - Work with Supply Chain Finance to reconcile site infrastructure and equipment budgets, preventing gaps or double counting in consolidated deployment costs

Reporting and Process Improvement

 - Prepare clear project and site reporting for business reviews, executive discussions, and Board materials, highlighting financial risks and decisions needed

 - Connect project schedules, commitments, and financial actuals using the team’s shared commitments data (purchase orders, invoices, and payments) in repeatable reporting and planning tools

 - Build and maintain repeatable models and workflows in Pigment and AI-assisted tools, reducing manual spreadsheet work

 - Improve the quality and consistency of infrastructure data, forecasts, and reporting as Lambda scales its data center portfolio

You

 - Have a Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field

 - Have 4+ years of experience in FP&A, project finance, infrastructure finance, or a related analytical role

 - Have experience managing project budgets, capital spending forecasts, or operating cost models in data centers, construction, energy, telecom, or another capital-intensive business

 - Understand how project commitments, actual costs, estimates to complete, and payment timing translate into financial forecasts

 - Possess strong financial modeling and Excel skills, including the ability to build driver-based models and evaluate investment returns and scenarios

 - Are comfortable working in enterprise planning systems and building repeatable, automated workflows rather than one-off spreadsheets

 - Can reconcile financial and operational data, identify the causes of variances, and turn findings into practical recommendations

 - Communicate clearly with finance, engineering, construction, and operations stakeholders

 - Are comfortable working independently in an ambiguous, fast-paced environment while managing multiple projects and deadlines

Nice to Have
